<a id="circular-shift"></a>**Circular shift** — Shifting a length-N sequence modulo N, x[((n − m))_N], so samples pushed past the end reappear at the start; the DFT turns it into multiplication by W_N^{km}. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Circular convolution](#circular-convolution).

<a id="clamp-circuit"></a>**Clamp circuit** — A series capacitor and a diode that shift a waveform's DC level so that one of its extremes sits at a fixed voltage; also called a DC restorer. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="class-a-amplifier"></a>**Class-A amplifier** — An amplifier whose output transistor conducts for the whole signal cycle around a fixed bias current; with a resistive load its efficiency is at most 25% (50% with inductor or transformer coupling). *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Conversion efficiency](#conversion-efficiency).

<a id="class-ab-amplifier"></a>**Class-AB amplifier** — A push-pull output stage biased so both transistors conduct a small quiescent current at idle, removing the crossover dead band at the cost of some idle power; the two currents obey i_N·i_P = I_Q² in a bipolar stage. *First defined in* [12-07](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-07-output-stages.md). *See also:* [Class-B amplifier](#class-b-amplifier), [VBE multiplier](#vbe-multiplier).

<a id="class-b-amplifier"></a>**Class-B amplifier** — A push-pull output stage in which each of two complementary transistors conducts for half of each cycle, with no idle current; efficiency (π/4)·V_op/V_CC, at most 78.5%, but with crossover distortion near zero output. *First defined in* [12-07](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-07-output-stages.md). *See also:* [Class-AB amplifier](#class-ab-amplifier), [Crossover distortion](#crossover-distortion), [Class-A amplifier](#class-a-amplifier).

<a id="class-d-amplifier"></a>**Class-D amplifier** — A switching amplifier whose output transistors are driven fully on or off at a frequency well above the signal, with the signal recovered by filtering; practical efficiencies exceed 90% at high output. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Conversion efficiency](#conversion-efficiency).

<a id="clock-skew"></a>**Clock skew** — The difference between the arrival times of a clock edge at two flip-flops; skew that delays the capturing clock helps setup and hurts hold by the same amount. *First defined in* [08-10](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-10-timing-metastability-cdc.md). *See also:* [Jitter](#jitter).

<a id="clock-domain-crossing-cdc"></a>**Clock-domain crossing (CDC)** — Any signal passing between logic clocked by unrelated clocks; it needs a synchronizer for single bits and Gray coding, a handshake or an asynchronous FIFO for multi-bit values. *First defined in* [08-10](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-10-timing-metastability-cdc.md). *See also:* [Synchronizer](#synchronizer), [Asynchronous FIFO](#asynchronous-fifo).

<a id="clock-to-q-delay"></a>**Clock-to-Q delay** — The delay from a flip-flop's active clock edge to its output changing; t_pcq is the longest (used for setup checks) and t_ccq the shortest (used for hold checks). *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md).

<a id="cmos"></a>**CMOS** — Complementary MOS, the logic family that pairs n-channel and p-channel MOSFETs so that in either steady state one device of each pair is off; it draws current mainly while switching. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="cmos-image-sensor"></a>**CMOS image sensor** — An array of pixels, each with a photodiode and transistors, that integrates photocharge and reads it out through a source follower; the dominant camera sensor. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="cmos-inverter"></a>**CMOS inverter** — A PMOS from the supply to the output and an NMOS from the output to ground, with gates tied to the input; the basic CMOS gate, regenerative and drawing only leakage in steady state. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md). *See also:* [CMOS](#cmos), [Voltage transfer characteristic](#voltage-transfer-characteristic).

<a id="co-packaged-optics"></a>**Co-packaged optics** — Optical engines placed in the same package as a switch or processor chip, shortening the electrical path to cut power per bit; announced by NVIDIA and Broadcom for 2025–2026 switches (as of Nov 2026). *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="coaxial-line"></a>**Coaxial line** — An inner conductor inside a coaxial outer conductor carrying equal and opposite charge; the field λ/(2πε₀r) is confined between them, strongest at the inner conductor, and zero outside. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="code-coverage"></a>**Code coverage** — The fraction of code exercised by tests, by statement, branch (decision) or MC/DC criteria; it shows what was not tested, not that what ran was checked. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md). *See also:* [MC/DC](#mc-dc).

<a id="code-density"></a>**Code density** — How few bytes an ISA needs to express a program; denser code fits better in instruction caches and small memories. *First defined in* [14-02](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-02-isa-risc-v-arm-x86.md). *See also:* [Compressed instructions](#compressed-instructions).

<a id="code-review"></a>**Code review** — Examination of every change by another engineer before it is merged, catching defects tests miss, spreading knowledge and enforcing standards; the software counterpart of segregation of duties. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="cofactor"></a>**Cofactor** — C_ij = (−1)^(i+j) times the determinant of the matrix with row i and column j deleted; expanding along a row, det A = Σ a_ij C_ij. Practical only for small matrices. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="coherence-miss"></a>**Coherence miss** — A cache miss on a block the core held earlier but lost to another core's invalidation; the fourth C beside compulsory, capacity and conflict misses. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [False sharing](#false-sharing), [Three Cs (compulsory, capacity, conflict)](#three-cs-compulsory-capacity-conflict).

<a id="coherent-demodulation"></a>**Coherent demodulation** — Recovering a modulated message by multiplying by a local copy of the carrier and low-pass filtering; a phase error φ scales the output by cos φ and a frequency error makes it beat. *First defined in* [11-11](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-11-modulation-and-filtering-applications.md). *See also:* [DSB-SC modulation](#dsb-sc-modulation).

<a id="colpitts-oscillator"></a>**Colpitts oscillator** — An LC oscillator whose tank uses a capacitive divider (C1 and C2 in series with the inductor's resonance) to feed back part of the transistor's output; it oscillates at the resonance of L with C1 and C2 in series and starts if g_m·R exceeds C2/C1. *First defined in* [12-09](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-09-oscillators.md). *See also:* [Negative resistance](#negative-resistance), [Crystal oscillator](#crystal-oscillator).

<a id="column-multiplexer"></a>**Column multiplexer** — The multiplexer that selects one word out of the several held in a memory row, using the low-order address bits, so that the array can be kept roughly square. *First defined in* [08-11](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-11-memories-and-programmable-logic.md). *See also:* [Memory array](#memory-array).

<a id="column-space"></a>**Column space** — C(A), the set of all combinations Ax of the columns of A; Ax = b is solvable exactly when b lies in it. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="commit"></a>**Commit** — In git, a permanent snapshot of the staged project plus its author, date, message and parent commit, named by a hash of its content; commits chain into the project's history. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md).

<a id="common-base-amplifier"></a>**Common-base amplifier** — The bipolar stage with the base at signal ground, the input at the emitter and the output at the collector; a non-inverting current buffer with input resistance about r_e = α/g_m and current gain α. *First defined in* [10-07](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-07-bjt-single-stage-amplifiers.md).

<a id="common-emitter-amplifier"></a>**Common-emitter amplifier** — The bipolar gain stage with the input at the base, the output at the collector and the emitter at signal ground (or through a degeneration resistor); its gain −g_m(R_C ∥ r_o) equals the DC voltage across R_C divided by V_T when r_o is negligible. *First defined in* [10-07](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-07-bjt-single-stage-amplifiers.md).

<a id="common-gate-amplifier"></a>**Common-gate amplifier** — The MOSFET stage with the gate at signal ground, the input at the source and the output at the drain; a non-inverting current buffer with input resistance about 1/(g_m + g_mb) and gain about (g_m + g_mb)R_D. *First defined in* [10-06](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-06-mos-single-stage-amplifiers.md).

<a id="common-impedance-coupling"></a>**Common-impedance coupling** — Interference between two circuits whose currents share a conductor; each circuit's current through the shared impedance produces a voltage in the other, as when a sensor and a motor share a ground return. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Star ground](#star-ground), [IR drop](#ir-drop).

<a id="common-mode-failure"></a>**Common-mode failure** — A failure that takes down several redundant units at once through a shared cause (power feed, design bug, environment), defeating redundancy. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="common-mode-feedback"></a>**Common-mode feedback** — A loop in a fully differential amplifier that senses the average of the two outputs, compares it with a reference and adjusts a bias current, dividing the common-mode error (current mismatch times output resistance) by 1 + g_m,cm·R_out. *First defined in* [12-08](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-08-op-amp-internals.md). *See also:* [Fully differential amplifier](#fully-differential-amplifier).

<a id="common-mode-gain"></a>**Common-mode gain** — The gain from the average of a differential stage's two inputs to its output; for one output of a resistor-loaded pair it is about R_D/(2R_SS), set by the tail's output resistance R_SS. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Differential-mode gain](#differential-mode-gain), [Common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR)](#common-mode-rejection-ratio-cmrr).

<a id="common-mode-rejection-ratio-cmrr"></a>**Common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR)** — The ratio of differential gain to common-mode gain, A_d/A_cm, usually in dB; for a difference amplifier built from resistors of tolerance t it is at worst about (1 + G)/(4t). *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [Instrumentation amplifier](#instrumentation-amplifier).

<a id="common-source-amplifier"></a>**Common-source amplifier** — The MOSFET gain stage with the input at the gate, the output at the drain and the source at signal ground (or through a degeneration resistor); its gain is −g_m(R_D ∥ r_o), and it inverts. *First defined in* [10-06](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-06-mos-single-stage-amplifiers.md).

<a id="companion-model"></a>**Companion model** — The conductance-plus-current-source equivalent that SPICE substitutes for a nonlinear device at each Newton iteration (its tangent line) or for a capacitor or inductor at each time step (its discretized law), so the circuit can be solved by linear MNA. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md). *See also:* [Newton–Raphson method](#newton-raphson-method), [Modified nodal analysis](#modified-nodal-analysis).

<a id="comparator"></a>**Comparator** — An amplifier designed to switch between two output levels according to the sign of its differential input, uncompensated and with fast saturation recovery, often with a push-pull or open-drain logic output. *First defined in* [10-10](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-10-op-amp-application-circuits.md). *See also:* [Schmitt trigger](#schmitt-trigger).

<a id="compensation"></a>**Compensation** — The presence of both donors and acceptors in one region, where the carrier densities depend on the net doping |N_D − N_A| while all the ions still scatter carriers; used to form regions of one type inside another. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md).

<a id="compiler"></a>**Compiler** — A program that translates source code (C, for example) into machine instructions ahead of time, checking types and syntax; its output is assembly or object code for one processor architecture. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Linker](#linker), [Preprocessor](#preprocessor), [Interpreter](#interpreter).

<a id="complementary-fet"></a>**Complementary FET** — A stacked device (CFET) that places the n-channel transistor directly over the p-channel transistor in one footprint, shrinking CMOS cells; projected by the IRDS to follow gate-all-around devices from about 2031. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="complementary-sensitivity"></a>**Complementary sensitivity** — T(s) = L(s)/(1 + L(s)), the closed-loop transfer function from reference to output (and, with a minus sign, from sensor noise to output); S + T = 1 at every frequency, so a loop cannot make both small at once. *First defined in* [15-02](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-02-transfer-functions-and-block-diagrams.md). *See also:* [Sensitivity function](#sensitivity-function).

<a id="completing-the-square"></a>**Completing the square** — Rewriting x² + px + q as (x + p/2)² + (q − p²/4); it turns an irreducible quadratic into an arctangent integral, and in the Laplace domain into a damped sinusoid. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="complex-conjugate"></a>**Complex conjugate** — For z = x + jy, the number z\* = x − jy, its mirror image across the real axis. z z\* = |z|², which is why conjugates are used to divide complex numbers. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="complex-exponential"></a>**Complex exponential** — A signal e^{st} with complex s = σ + jω. It rotates at ω rad/s while its magnitude grows (σ > 0), decays (σ < 0) or stays constant (σ = 0); its real part is a growing, decaying or steady sinusoid. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="complex-number"></a>**Complex number** — A number z = x + jy with real part x and imaginary part y (both real numbers), drawn as a point or arrow in the complex plane. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Imaginary unit](#imaginary-unit), [Complex plane](#complex-plane).

<a id="complex-permittivity"></a>**Complex permittivity** — ε_c = ε′ − jε″, which folds a material's loss (conduction or polarization lag) into its permittivity for time-harmonic fields; ε″ = σ/ω for pure conduction, and ε″/ε′ is the loss tangent. *First defined in* [13-04](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-04-maxwells-equations.md). *See also:* [Loss tangent](#loss-tangent).

<a id="complex-plane"></a>**Complex plane** — The plane in which a complex number x + jy is plotted at horizontal coordinate x (real axis) and vertical coordinate y (imaginary axis). *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="complex-power"></a>**Complex power** — S = V_rms I_rms\* = ½ V I\* = P + jQ (VA), whose real part is average power, imaginary part reactive power and magnitude apparent power; complex powers of all elements of a circuit sum to zero. *First defined in* [07-06](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-06-ac-power-and-power-factor.md). *See also:* [Reactive power](#reactive-power), [Apparent power](#apparent-power).

<a id="complex-replacement"></a>**Complex replacement** — Solving an ODE with input cos ωt by solving it with input e^{jωt} and taking the real part; valid because the equation has real coefficients. It is the proof behind phasor analysis. *First defined in* [02-04](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-04-forced-response-and-resonance.md). *See also:* [Phasor](#phasor).

<a id="compliance-voltage"></a>**Compliance voltage** — The lowest output voltage at which a current source still delivers its intended current with its intended output resistance; V_ov for a basic MOS mirror, V_TN + 2V_ov for a simple cascode mirror. *First defined in* [10-08](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-08-current-sources-and-mirrors.md). *See also:* [Current mirror](#current-mirror).

<a id="compound-semiconductor"></a>**Compound semiconductor** — A semiconductor made of two or more elements, such as GaAs, InP, GaN or SiC; III–V compounds offer light electrons and direct gaps, while SiC and GaN offer wide gaps and high critical fields. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="compressed-instructions"></a>**Compressed instructions** — Shorter encodings of common instructions (RISC-V's 16-bit C extension, Arm's Thumb) that restrict operands to save code size; RISC-V reports typical whole-program savings of 25–30%. *First defined in* [14-02](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-02-isa-risc-v-arm-x86.md). *See also:* [Code density](#code-density).

<a id="compute-express-link-cxl"></a>**Compute Express Link (CXL)** — An interconnect standard that runs on the PCIe physical layer and adds cache-coherent protocols for accelerators and attached memory, enabling memory expansion and pooling; CXL 4.0 (Nov 2025) runs at 128 GT/s. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [PCI Express (PCIe)](#pci-express-pcie).

<a id="condition-codes"></a>**Condition codes** — Status flags (zero, negative, carry, overflow) set as a side effect of arithmetic or compare instructions and tested by later branches, as in x86 and Arm; RISC-V has none and branches compare registers directly. *First defined in* [14-02](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-02-isa-risc-v-arm-x86.md).

<a id="condition-number"></a>**Condition number** — κ = σ_max/σ_min for a square invertible matrix, the worst-case amplification of relative error when solving Ax = b; a large κ, not a small determinant, means nearly singular. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="conditional-distribution"></a>**Conditional distribution** — The distribution of Y given X = x, the joint distribution divided by the marginal of X along that slice. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="conditional-expectation"></a>**Conditional expectation** — E[Y | X = x], the mean of the conditional distribution of Y given X = x; evaluated at the random X, E[Y | X] is itself a random variable, the minimum mean-square-error predictor of Y, and E[E[Y | X]] = E[Y] (law of iterated expectations). *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="conditional-independence"></a>**Conditional independence** — Events that are independent once a third event (such as a die's true state) is known, even though they may be dependent unconditionally. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="conditional-probability"></a>**Conditional probability** — P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B), the probability of A among the outcomes where B occurred. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md). *See also:* [Bayes' rule](#bayes-rule).

<a id="conductance"></a>**Conductance** — The reciprocal of resistance, G = 1/R = i/v, in siemens (A/V); convenient for parallel elements and nodal analysis. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md). *See also:* [Resistance](#resistance).

<a id="conductance-matrix"></a>**Conductance matrix** — The matrix G of nodal analysis, G v = i. Diagonal entries are the total conductance at each node; off-diagonal entries are minus the conductance between two nodes. It is symmetric, sparse and, once a node is grounded, nonsingular. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md). *See also:* [Stamp](#stamp), [Modified nodal analysis](#modified-nodal-analysis).

<a id="conduction-angle"></a>**Conduction angle** — The fraction of each cycle, expressed as an angle, during which a rectifier diode conducts; about the square root of 2V_r/V_p radians in a peak rectifier. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="conductivity-effective-mass"></a>**Conductivity effective mass** — The effective mass that sets a carrier's acceleration, and hence mobility, averaged over equivalent valleys as a harmonic mean; for silicon electrons 1/m_c = (1/3)(1/m_l + 2/m_t), giving about 0.26 m0. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Effective mass](#effective-mass), [Density-of-states effective mass](#density-of-states-effective-mass).

<a id="confidence-interval"></a>**Confidence interval** — An interval computed from data by a procedure that covers the true parameter in a stated fraction (for example 95%) of repeated experiments; any single interval either contains the truth or not. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="conjugate-match"></a>**Conjugate match** — The AC form of maximum power transfer, Z_L = Z_th\*, in which the load's resistance equals the source's and its reactance cancels the source's. *First defined in* [06-09](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-09-maximum-power-transfer.md). *See also:* [Matched load](#matched-load), [Maximum power transfer](#maximum-power-transfer).

<a id="conjugate-matching"></a>**Conjugate matching** — Choosing a load impedance equal to the complex conjugate of the source's Thévenin impedance, which maximizes average power to the load (P_max = V_Th,rms²/(4R_Th)) at 50% efficiency. *First defined in* [07-06](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-06-ac-power-and-power-factor.md).

<a id="consensus-theorem"></a>**Consensus theorem** — AB + A'C + BC = AB + A'C; the term BC is redundant because one of the other two is 1 whenever it is. Removing consensus terms simplifies logic; adding them back removes glitches (hazards). *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="conservative-field"></a>**Conservative field** — A vector field whose line integrals depend only on the endpoints, equivalently the gradient of a potential, equivalently curl-free on a region without holes; electrostatic fields are conservative, which is what makes voltage well defined. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Line integral](#line-integral), [Curl](#curl).

<a id="constant-drop-diode-model"></a>**Constant-drop diode model** — A diode model that is an open circuit when off and a fixed voltage source (typically 0.7 V for silicon) when on; adequate when the circuit's voltages are several times the drop. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="constant-field-scaling"></a>**Constant-field scaling** — Dennard's scaling rules (1974) in which dimensions and voltages shrink by 1/κ and doping rises by κ, so fields stay constant, delay falls by 1/κ and power density stays constant. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="constant-gm-input-stage"></a>**Constant-gm input stage** — A complementary rail-to-rail input stage whose bias control keeps the total transconductance constant across the common-mode range, for square-law devices by giving each pair a quarter of its current where both conduct. *First defined in* [12-08](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-08-op-amp-internals.md). *See also:* [Rail-to-rail input](#rail-to-rail-input).

<a id="contacted-poly-pitch"></a>**Contacted poly pitch** — The center-to-center spacing of transistor gates including room for the contacts between them (CPP); with cell height, the main physical measure of logic density. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="contamination-delay"></a>**Contamination delay** — The shortest time from an input change until an output starts to change (t_cd); it bounds how soon a new input can disturb a downstream register and sets hold-time constraints. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="continuity"></a>**Continuity** — f is continuous at a if f(a) is defined, the limit at a exists, and the two are equal; informally, the graph can be drawn without lifting the pen. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="continuity-equation"></a>**Continuity equation** — Charge conservation in local form, ∇ · J = −∂ρ/∂t; integrated over a node that stores no charge it becomes Kirchhoff's current law. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="continuity-of-capacitor-voltage-and-inductor-current"></a>**Continuity of capacitor voltage and inductor current** — The rule that v_C and i_L cannot change instantaneously (it would take infinite current or voltage, and infinite power). Other circuit variables can jump at switching instants. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="continuous-assignment"></a>**Continuous assignment** — A Verilog assign statement, which drives a net with an expression that is re-evaluated whenever any operand changes; it describes combinational logic. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="continuous-integration"></a>**Continuous integration** — CI; automatically building and testing a project on a clean machine every time a change is pushed, so problems that depend on one person's setup are caught within minutes. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md).

<a id="continuous-time-linear-equalizer-ctle"></a>**Continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE)** — An analog filter in a high-speed receiver that boosts high frequencies relative to low ones with a zero placed below its poles, to undo the channel's frequency-dependent loss; its boost comes mostly from lowering the low-frequency gain. *First defined in* [11-08](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-08-laplace-transform-and-system-functions.md). *See also:* [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros).

<a id="continuous-time-signal"></a>**Continuous-time signal** — A signal x(t) defined at every real instant t, such as the voltage on a wire; the domain of analog front ends and of the Laplace and continuous-time Fourier transforms. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Discrete-time signal](#discrete-time-signal).

<a id="control-hazard"></a>**Control hazard** — A pipeline hazard caused by a branch or jump whose outcome or target is not known when the next instructions must be fetched. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Flush](#flush), [Branch penalty](#branch-penalty).

<a id="control-unit"></a>**Control unit** — The combinational (or sequential) logic that decodes each instruction and sets the datapath's multiplexer selects and write enables; in RISC-V, a main decoder on the opcode plus an ALU decoder. *First defined in* [14-05](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-05-single-cycle-datapath.md). *See also:* [Main decoder](#main-decoder), [Datapath](#datapath).

<a id="controllability"></a>**Controllability** — The property that some input can drive a system's state from any value to any other in finite time; tested by rank[B AB … A^(n−1)B] = n. An uncontrollable mode cannot be moved by any feedback through that input. *First defined in* [15-10](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-10-state-space-introduction.md). *See also:* [Observability](#observability), [Pole placement](#pole-placement).

<a id="conversion-efficiency"></a>**Conversion efficiency** — The fraction η = P_L/P_DC of the supply power that an amplifier delivers to its load as signal power. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md).

<a id="conversion-gain"></a>**Conversion gain** — The voltage change per collected electron at a pixel's sense node, q/C_FD, typically tens to hundreds of microvolts per electron. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="convolution"></a>**Convolution** — The operation y(t) = ∫ h(t−λ) u(λ) dλ that gives a linear time-invariant system's output from its input and impulse response; for a first-order low-pass, an exponentially weighted average of past inputs. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="convolution-integral"></a>**Convolution integral** — y(t) = ∫ x(τ) h(t − τ) dτ, the output of a continuous-time LTI system with impulse response h; the limit of a staircase of narrow pulses, each launching a scaled, shifted copy of h. *First defined in* [11-03](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-03-convolution.md). *See also:* [Convolution](#convolution), [Graphical convolution](#graphical-convolution).

<a id="convolution-sum"></a>**Convolution sum** — y[n] = Σₖ x[k] h[n − k], the output of a discrete-time LTI system with impulse response h; derived from x[n] = Σₖ x[k] δ[n − k], time invariance and linearity. Its length is the sum of the input and response lengths minus one. *First defined in* [11-03](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-03-convolution.md). *See also:* [Convolution](#convolution), [Impulse response](#impulse-response).

<a id="convolution-theorem"></a>**Convolution theorem** — Convolution in time is multiplication in frequency, x \* h ↔ X(jω)H(jω), and multiplication in time is convolution in frequency (divided by 2π); the frequency response of an LTI system is the transform of its impulse response. *First defined in* [11-06](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-06-continuous-time-fourier-transform.md).

<a id="core-license"></a>**Core license** — A licence to build a licensor's ready-made processor design into one's chips, for a licence fee plus a per-chip royalty (Arm calls it a technology licence agreement). *First defined in* [14-02](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-02-isa-risc-v-arm-x86.md). *See also:* [Architecture license](#architecture-license).

<a id="core-loss"></a>**Core loss** — Power lost in a magnetic core to hysteresis and eddy currents, roughly constant at fixed voltage and frequency; it is the no-load loss of a transformer, measured by the open-circuit test, and rises with frequency. *First defined in* [07-09](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-09-mutual-inductance-and-transformers.md).

<a id="corner-frequency"></a>**Corner frequency** — For a single-pole response H = 1/(1 + jωτ), the frequency ω = 1/τ where |H| = 1/√2 (−3 dB) and the phase is −45°; commonly used to define bandwidth. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="correlation-coefficient"></a>**Correlation coefficient** — ρ = Cov(X, Y)/(σ_X σ_Y), between −1 and 1; it measures only linear association, so uncorrelated variables can still be dependent. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="correlation-time"></a>**Correlation time** — The time scale τ_c over which a process's autocorrelation decays (RC for RC-filtered noise); a record of length T holds about T/(2τ_c) independent samples. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="coulomb-counting"></a>**Coulomb counting** — Estimating a battery's state of charge by integrating measured current over time; offsets accumulate, so gauges recalibrate at known states. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="coulombs-law"></a>**Coulomb's law** — The force between point charges, F = q₁q₂/(4πε₀r²) along the line joining them; repulsive for like signs, attractive for unlike, falling as the inverse square of distance. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="coupling-and-cohesion"></a>**Coupling and cohesion** — Coupling is how much modules depend on each other; cohesion is how focused a module is on one purpose. Good designs have low coupling (narrow, stable interfaces) and high cohesion. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="coupling-coefficient"></a>**Coupling coefficient** — k = M/√(L₁L₂), from 0 (no shared flux) to 1 (all flux shared); near 1 for windings on a common core, much lower for separated coils such as a wireless charger's. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="covariance"></a>**Covariance** — Cov(X, Y) = E[(X − μ_X)(Y − μ_Y)] = E[XY] − μ_Xμ_Y; zero for independent variables, and the cross term in the variance of a sum. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="cpi"></a>**CPI** — (Cycles per instruction.) The average number of clock cycles per executed instruction, the frequency-weighted average of each instruction class's cycles; its reciprocal is IPC. *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md). *See also:* [IPC](#ipc).

<a id="cramers-rule"></a>**Cramer's rule** — For a nonsingular system, xᵢ = det(Bᵢ)/det(A), where Bᵢ is A with column i replaced by b. Useful for small symbolic results, never for large numerical systems. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="crest-factor"></a>**Crest factor** — Peak value divided by RMS value; √2 for a sine, 1 for a square wave, √3 for a triangle. Instruments and amplifiers specify the crest factor they can handle. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="critical-angle"></a>**Critical angle** — The angle of incidence, θc = arcsin(n₂/n₁), above which a wave going from a denser to a less dense medium is totally reflected; 41.8° from glass (n = 1.5) into air. *First defined in* [13-06](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-06-reflection-and-transmission.md). *See also:* [Total internal reflection](#total-internal-reflection), [Snell's law](#snells-law).

<a id="critical-field"></a>**Critical field** — The peak electric field at which a junction breaks down by avalanche, about 3×10⁵ V/cm in silicon (rising slowly with doping); with it, breakdown voltage scales as εE_c²/(2qN) and drift-region resistance as V²/E_c³. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="critical-length"></a>**Critical length** — The interconnect length beyond which reflections matter and a net must be treated as a transmission line; a common guideline sets it where the one-way delay reaches about one sixth of the signal's rise time (about 2.5 mm on FR-4-like board at 100 ps). *First defined in* [13-07](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-07-transmission-lines-time-domain.md). *See also:* [Rise time](#rise-time).

<a id="critical-path"></a>**Critical path** — The slowest input-to-output path through a block of logic; its propagation delay limits the clock frequency of the design. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="critical-point"></a>**Critical point** — A point where f'(x) = 0 or f' does not exist; interior maxima and minima occur only at critical points (Fermat's theorem). *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="critically-damped"></a>**Critically damped** — A second-order system with ζ = 1, whose repeated root gives the response (c₁ + c₂t)e^{−αt}; the boundary between ringing and creeping, though not the fastest to settle within a tolerance band. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="cross-product"></a>**Cross product** — a × b, a vector perpendicular to both a and b, of length |a||b|sin θ (the area of their parallelogram), directed by the right-hand rule. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="cross-correlation"></a>**Cross-correlation** — r_xy[n] = Σₖ x[k] y[k + n], a measure of how well y matches shifted copies of x; it equals convolution with x reversed in time. Deep-learning "convolution" layers compute cross-correlations. *First defined in* [11-03](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-03-convolution.md). *See also:* [Matched filter](#matched-filter).

<a id="crossover-distortion"></a>**Crossover distortion** — Distortion of a class B stage near zero output, where neither transistor conducts until its base–emitter voltage reaches about 0.6 V; it is worst for small signals and is removed by class AB bias. *First defined in* [12-07](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-07-output-stages.md). *See also:* [Class-B amplifier](#class-b-amplifier), [Class-AB amplifier](#class-ab-amplifier).

<a id="crossover-frequency"></a>**Crossover frequency** — The frequency at which a loop gain's magnitude falls to one; the phase margin is read there, and for a well-compensated loop it is close to the closed-loop bandwidth. *First defined in* [12-06](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-06-stability-and-compensation.md). *See also:* [Phase margin](#phase-margin), [Loop gain](#loop-gain).

<a id="cryptographic-hash"></a>**Cryptographic hash** — A function (SHA-1, SHA-256) mapping any data to a fixed-length fingerprint such that any change to the input changes about half the output bits and collisions are infeasible to find; git names files and commits by such hashes. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md).

<a id="crystal-lattice"></a>**Crystal lattice** — A periodic array of points in space at each of which an identical group of atoms (the basis) sits; silicon is a diamond lattice, two interpenetrating face-centered cubic lattices, with 8 atoms per cubic cell of side 0.5431 nm. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="crystal-oscillator"></a>**Crystal oscillator** — An oscillator whose frequency is set by a quartz crystal, modelled as a motional L_m, C_m, R_m branch in parallel with C_0; its quality factor of 10⁴ to 10⁶ makes the frequency nearly independent of the amplifier, and the load capacitance pulls it by parts per million. *First defined in* [12-09](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-09-oscillators.md). *See also:* [Colpitts oscillator](#colpitts-oscillator).

<a id="cumulative-distribution-function-cdf"></a>**Cumulative distribution function (CDF)** — F_X(x) = P(X ≤ x), which rises from 0 to 1; any interval probability is a difference of CDF values, and the density is its derivative. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="curl"></a>**Curl** — ∇ × F, the circulation of a vector field per unit area at a point, as a vector along the axis of rotation; magnetic fields have curl where current flows. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="current-amplifier"></a>**Current amplifier** — An amplifier that senses an input current and delivers an output current, modeled by its short-circuit current gain A_is with R_i and R_o; ideally R_i → 0 and R_o → ∞. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md).

<a id="current-density"></a>**Current density** — Current per unit area as a vector field, J = nqv_d (A/m²); the current through a surface is the flux of J, and J = σE in an ohmic material. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="current-divider"></a>**Current divider** — Parallel resistors sharing a current in proportion to their conductances; for two, i1 = i R2/(R1 + R2), so the smaller resistor takes the larger current. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="current-gain"></a>**Current gain** — The common-emitter ratio β_F = I_C/I_B of a bipolar transistor, about 100 in typical devices; the common-base gain α_F = I_C/I_E = β_F/(1 + β_F) is just below 1. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="current-mirror"></a>**Current mirror** — Two or more transistors sharing a gate (base) voltage with one diode-connected, so that the others copy its current in the ratio of their sizes, independent of the threshold to first order. *First defined in* [10-02](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-02-mosfet-dc-operation-and-biasing.md). *See also:* [Diode-connected transistor](#diode-connected-transistor).

<a id="current-mirror-load"></a>**Current-mirror load** — A current mirror used as the load of a differential pair, which copies one side's signal current to the other so that both halves' currents reach a single-ended output, doubling its transconductance to g_m. *First defined in* [12-02](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-02-active-loads-cascodes-multistage.md). *See also:* [Active load](#active-load), [Five-transistor OTA](#five-transistor-ota), [Differential pair](#differential-pair).

<a id="current-mode-logic-cml"></a>**Current-mode logic (CML)** — Logic or buffering built from differential pairs that steer a constant tail current fully to one side, giving small differential swings across resistor loads, high speed and nearly constant supply current; standard in high-speed serial links. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Differential pair](#differential-pair), [Differential signaling](#differential-signaling).

<a id="current-sense-shunt"></a>**Current-sense shunt** — A low-value resistor (milliohms) whose voltage, i R_sh, measures current; its value trades signal against I²R loss, and four-terminal parts with Kelvin layout keep copper's 0.39%/°C out of the measurement. *First defined in* [06-11](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-11-practical-dc-circuits-and-measurement.md). *See also:* [Four-terminal (Kelvin) measurement](#four-terminal-kelvin-measurement), [Burden voltage](#burden-voltage).

<a id="cutoff-frequency"></a>**Cutoff frequency** — The frequency f_T at which a transistor's short-circuit current gain falls to 1; for a bipolar transistor 1/(2π[τ_F + (C_jE + C_jC)V_T/I_C]), rising with current until the Kirk effect sets in. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="cyclic-prefix"></a>**Cyclic prefix** — A copy of the last G samples of each OFDM symbol placed in front of it, so that a channel with up to G + 1 taps convolves the symbol circularly; it removes inter-symbol and inter-carrier interference at an overhead of G/(N + G). *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [OFDM](#ofdm), [Circular convolution](#circular-convolution).

<a id="cyclic-redundancy-check-crc"></a>**Cyclic redundancy check (CRC)** — An error-detecting check formed as the remainder of the message polynomial divided by a generator polynomial over GF(2); a degree-r CRC catches every burst of length r or less, and Ethernet frames end in a 32-bit one. *First defined in* [08-01](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-01-number-systems-and-codes.md). *See also:* [Hamming distance](#hamming-distance).

<a id="cyclomatic-complexity"></a>**Cyclomatic complexity** — McCabe's count of linearly independent paths through a function, M = E − N + 2 for its control-flow graph, equal to the number of decision points plus one; also the number of basis-path tests. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="cyclotron-frequency"></a>**Cyclotron frequency** — The orbital frequency of a charge in a uniform magnetic field, f_c = |q|B/(2πm), independent of speed; 28.0 GHz per tesla for an electron. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="c-v-characteristics"></a>**C–V characteristics** — The small-signal capacitance of a MOS structure against gate voltage, C_ox in accumulation, falling through depletion, and either returning to C_ox (quasi-static, or in a transistor) or staying at C_min (high frequency) in inversion; used to extract oxide thickness, doping and oxide charge. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md). *See also:* [C–V profiling](#c-v-profiling).

<a id="c-v-profiling"></a>**C–V profiling** — Extracting doping from capacitance–voltage data, using the slope of 1/C² against voltage (which gives the doping of the lightly doped side) and its intercept (which gives the built-in potential). *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="letter-d"></a>

## D

<a id="d-flip-flop"></a>**D flip-flop** — An edge-triggered storage element whose output takes the value D had at the active clock edge and holds it until the next edge; the basic register cell of synchronous design. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md). *See also:* [Master–slave flip-flop](#master-slave-flip-flop), [Setup time](#setup-time), [Hold time](#hold-time).

<a id="d-latch"></a>**D latch** — A level-sensitive storage element that is transparent (Q follows D) while its clock or enable is active and holds its value while it is inactive. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md). *See also:* [D flip-flop](#d-flip-flop).

<a id="dadda-tree"></a>**Dadda tree** — A multiplier reduction tree that brings the partial-product columns down to target heights 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 13, ... using as few adders as possible, needing n^2 - 4n + 3 full adders for an n by n multiplier. *First defined in* [08-09](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-09-arithmetic-circuits.md). *See also:* [Carry-save adder](#carry-save-adder), [Partial product](#partial-product).

<a id="damped-natural-frequency"></a>**Damped natural frequency** — ω_d = ω₀√(1 − ζ²), the frequency at which an underdamped system actually rings. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Natural frequency](#natural-frequency).

<a id="damping-ratio"></a>**Damping ratio** — ζ = α/ω₀, the single number that classifies a second-order system: underdamped (ζ < 1, rings), critically damped (ζ = 1) or overdamped (ζ > 1); overshoot depends only on ζ. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="dark-current"></a>**Dark current** — The current an image-sensor pixel or photodiode collects with no light, mainly thermal generation through traps in depleted regions and at interfaces; it scales roughly with n_i and so grows rapidly with temperature. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="dark-silicon"></a>**Dark silicon** — The part of a power-limited chip that cannot switch at full speed at the same time as the rest, because running all of it would exceed the power or thermal budget. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="darlington-pair"></a>**Darlington pair** — Two bipolar transistors with the first one's emitter driving the second one's base, giving a current gain of about the product of the two betas at the cost of two base-emitter drops and slower turn-off; the Sziklai pair uses a complementary driver to keep a single drop. *First defined in* [12-07](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-07-output-stages.md). *See also:* [Class-AB amplifier](#class-ab-amplifier).

<a id="data-hazard"></a>**Data hazard** — A pipeline hazard in which an instruction needs a result that an earlier instruction has not yet written back (a read-after-write dependence). *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Forwarding (bypassing)](#forwarding-bypassing), [Load-use hazard](#load-use-hazard).

<a id="dataflow-accelerator"></a>**Dataflow (accelerator)** — The choice of which operand an accelerator array keeps in place while the others move (weights, outputs or inputs), which determines the data reuse the hardware exploits. *First defined in* [14-14](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-14-ai-accelerators.md). *See also:* [Weight-stationary](#weight-stationary), [Output-stationary](#output-stationary).

<a id="dataflow-limit"></a>**Dataflow limit** — The execution time with unlimited resources and perfect prediction, set by the longest latency-weighted chain of true dependences (the critical path); no machine can be faster. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [Instruction-level parallelism (ILP)](#instruction-level-parallelism-ilp), [True dependence](#true-dependence).

<a id="datapath"></a>**Datapath** — The part of a processor that holds and transforms data — program counter, memories, register file, ALU, adders and multiplexers — steered by the control unit. *First defined in* [14-05](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-05-single-cycle-datapath.md). *See also:* [Control unit](#control-unit).

<a id="datapath-and-controller-fsmd"></a>**Datapath and controller (FSMD)** — The split of a design into a small FSM that sequences operations and a datapath of registers, counters and arithmetic that performs them, linked by control and status signals. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [Finite state machine (FSM)](#finite-state-machine-fsm).

<a id="dbm"></a>**dBm** — Power expressed in decibels relative to 1 mW, 10·log10(P / 1 mW); 0 dBm = 1 mW and 30 dBm = 1 W. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md). *See also:* [Decibel](#decibel).

<a id="dc-blocker"></a>**DC blocker** — The filter (1 − z^−1)/(1 − a z^−1) with a just below 1, a zero at z = 1 and a pole just inside it, which removes DC and passes frequencies above about (1 − a) rad/sample; used to strip converter offsets. *First defined in* [16-02](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-02-dtft-and-z-transform-for-dsp.md).

<a id="dc-gain"></a>**DC gain** — H(0), the steady-state output per unit of constant input for a stable system; it is also the final value of the unit-step response. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Transfer function](#transfer-function), [Final-value theorem](#final-value-theorem).

<a id="dc-level-shifting"></a>**DC level shifting** — Moving a signal's DC level between directly coupled stages, by alternating NMOS and PMOS stages, by a source or emitter follower (a shift of V_GS or V_BE), or by a fixed drop across diodes or resistors carrying a set current. *First defined in* [12-02](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-02-active-loads-cascodes-multistage.md). *See also:* [Multistage amplifier](#multistage-amplifier), [Level shifter](#level-shifter).

<a id="dc-bias-derating"></a>**DC-bias derating** — The loss of capacitance of class II ceramic capacitors (X5R, X7R) under applied DC voltage, because their ferroelectric dielectric's permittivity falls with field; a part can deliver a fraction of its marked value at its working voltage. *First defined in* [07-01](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-01-capacitors-and-inductors.md). *See also:* [Multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC)](#multilayer-ceramic-capacitor-mlcc).

<a id="de-broglie-wavelength"></a>**De Broglie wavelength** — The wavelength λ = h/p associated with a particle of momentum p; about 0.12 nm for a 100 eV electron, comparable to atomic spacings, which is why electrons diffract from crystals. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="de-moivres-theorem"></a>**De Moivre's theorem** — (r∠θ)ⁿ = rⁿ∠nθ. Raising a complex number to a power raises its magnitude to that power and multiplies its angle. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="de-morgans-theorem"></a>**De Morgan's theorem** — The complement of an OR is the AND of the complements, and the complement of an AND is the OR of the complements; to complement an expression, swap AND and OR and complement every literal. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md). *See also:* [Bubble pushing](#bubble-pushing).

<a id="debye-length"></a>**Debye length** — The screening length L_D = √(εkT/(q²N)) over which mobile carriers smooth out a charge disturbance; 41 nm at 10¹⁶ cm⁻³ in silicon, and the scale of the soft edges of a depletion region. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="decibel"></a>**Decibel** — A logarithmic ratio, 10·log10 of a power ratio (or 20·log10 of an amplitude ratio for equal impedances); 3 dB ≈ 2× power, 10 dB = 10× power. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="decimation"></a>**Decimation** — Keeping every M-th sample of a sequence, y[n] = x[Mn]; it discards samples, so unlike continuous-time compression it can lose information, and its effect on energy depends on which samples are kept. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Zero-insertion interpolation](#zero-insertion-interpolation).

<a id="decimation-in-frequency"></a>**Decimation in frequency** — The FFT split into even- and odd-indexed output bins (input split into halves), giving natural input order, bit-reversed output order, and butterflies that multiply the difference by the twiddle. *First defined in* [16-04](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-04-the-fft.md). *See also:* [Decimation in time](#decimation-in-time).

<a id="decimation-in-time"></a>**Decimation in time** — The FFT split into even- and odd-indexed input samples, giving bit-reversed input order, natural output order, and butterflies that multiply by the twiddle before the add and subtract. *First defined in* [16-04](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-04-the-fft.md). *See also:* [Decimation in frequency](#decimation-in-frequency), [Bit-reversed order](#bit-reversed-order).

<a id="decision-feedback-equalizer-dfe"></a>**Decision-feedback equalizer (DFE)** — A receiver equalizer that subtracts the interference of earlier symbols computed from its own past decisions; one wrong decision can then cause a burst of errors, which transmitter precoding limits to about two bit errors. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="decoder"></a>**Decoder** — A block with n inputs and 2^n outputs, exactly one of which is 1 (the minterm of the inputs); with an enable input it is also a demultiplexer, and it selects rows in memories and decodes instructions. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="decoupling-capacitor"></a>**Decoupling capacitor** — A capacitor placed close to a load to supply its fast current changes until the regulator responds, limiting the droop to ΔI·Δt/C and the spike to L·di/dt; its effectiveness at high frequency is limited by inductance more than by capacitance. *First defined in* [07-01](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-01-capacitors-and-inductors.md). *See also:* [Equivalent series inductance (ESL)](#equivalent-series-inductance-esl).

<a id="deep-depletion"></a>**Deep depletion** — The non-equilibrium state of a MOS capacitor swept into inversion faster than thermal generation can supply minority carriers, so the depletion region grows beyond its equilibrium maximum; CCD pixels collect photo-electrons in this state. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="defect-level-dppm"></a>**Defect level (DPPM)** — The fraction of shipped (test-passing) parts that are defective, usually in defective parts per million; the Williams–Brown model gives DL = 1 − Y^(1−T). *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="defective-matrix"></a>**Defective matrix** — A square matrix with fewer independent eigenvectors than its size (a repeated eigenvalue short of eigenvectors); it cannot be diagonalized, and its powers and exponentials contain extra factors k or t. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="definite-integral"></a>**Definite integral** — The limit of Riemann sums ∫_a^b f(x) dx, equal to the signed area under f; its units are those of f times those of x. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="degenerate-semiconductor"></a>**Degenerate semiconductor** — A semiconductor so heavily doped that its Fermi level lies within a few kT of a band edge or inside a band, so that Boltzmann statistics fail and the Fermi–Dirac integral is needed; silicon becomes degenerate above roughly 10¹⁸–10¹⁹ cm⁻³. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md). *See also:* [Fermi–Dirac integral](#fermi-dirac-integral), [Band-gap narrowing](#band-gap-narrowing).

<a id="delay-margin"></a>**Delay margin** — The largest extra time delay a stable loop tolerates before it oscillates, PM (in radians) divided by the gain crossover frequency; a delay adds phase lag ωT without changing the magnitude. *First defined in* [15-07](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-07-frequency-domain-design.md). *See also:* [Phase margin](#phase-margin).

<a id="delta-connection"></a>**Delta connection** — Three-phase sources or loads connected end to end in a loop, each element between two lines; no neutral. A balanced Δ of Z_Δ is equivalent to a Y of Z_Δ/3. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="delta-wye-transformation"></a>**Delta–wye transformation** — Replacing three resistors in a triangle (delta) by three meeting at a node (wye), or the reverse, with equal behaviour at the three terminals; R_a = R_ab R_ca/(R_ab + R_bc + R_ca). *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="demand-paging"></a>**Demand paging** — Mapping a page only when it is first accessed, by servicing the resulting page fault, so that memory is allocated or loaded lazily. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Page fault](#page-fault), [Thrashing](#thrashing).

<a id="density-of-states"></a>**Density of states** — The number of electron states per unit energy (and per unit volume), g(E) ∝ √E for free electrons; multiplied by the occupation f(E) it gives how many electrons sit at each energy. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="density-of-states-effective-mass"></a>**Density-of-states effective mass** — The mass of a single spherical band that would hold as many states as the real, possibly anisotropic and multi-valley, band; for silicon electrons m_dn = 6^(2/3)(m_l m_t²)^(1/3), about 1.08 m0 at the band edge. It sets N_C and N_V. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Conductivity effective mass](#conductivity-effective-mass).

<a id="departure-angle"></a>**Departure angle** — The angle at which a root-locus branch leaves a complex open-loop pole, 180° minus the angles from the other poles plus the angles from the zeros; the analogous arrival angle applies at a complex zero. *First defined in* [15-06](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-06-root-locus.md). *See also:* [Root locus](#root-locus).

<a id="dependent-source"></a>**Dependent source** — An ideal voltage or current source whose value is a fixed multiple of a voltage or current elsewhere in the circuit (VCVS, VCCS, CCVS, CCCS); it models gain in transistors and amplifiers and stays in place when independent sources are turned off. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [VCVS](#vcvs), [VCCS](#vccs), [CCVS](#ccvs), [CCCS](#cccs), [Small-signal model](#small-signal-model).

<a id="depletion-approximation"></a>**Depletion approximation** — The model of a junction's space-charge region as completely empty of carriers between sharp edges and exactly neutral outside, which turns Poisson's equation into simple integrals; accurate to a few percent except near flat band. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="depletion-region"></a>**Depletion region** — The layer around a pn junction stripped of mobile carriers, leaving fixed ionized dopants (−qN_A on the p side, +qN_D on the n side); Gauss's law gives its triangular field, peaking at the junction. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="dereference"></a>**Dereference** — To access the object a pointer points to (\*p in C, or p->field for a struct); dereferencing an invalid or null pointer is undefined behavior. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="derivative"></a>**Derivative** — The instantaneous rate of change f'(a) = lim_{h→0} (f(a + h) − f(a))/h, the slope of the tangent line; its units are the output's units per input unit. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md). *See also:* [Difference quotient](#difference-quotient), [Differentiable](#differentiable).

<a id="derivative-kick"></a>**Derivative kick** — The large, brief controller output produced when the derivative term acts on the error and the setpoint steps; it is avoided by taking the derivative of the measurement only and is bounded by the derivative filter at K_p(1 + N). *First defined in* [15-08](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-08-pid-control.md). *See also:* [Setpoint weighting](#setpoint-weighting).

<a id="describing-function"></a>**Describing function** — The effective gain of a memoryless nonlinearity for a sinusoidal input, the fundamental of its output divided by the input amplitude; an oscillator's amplitude settles where the describing-function loop gain equals one. *First defined in* [12-09](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-09-oscillators.md). *See also:* [Barkhausen criterion](#barkhausen-criterion).

<a id="desensitivity-factor"></a>**Desensitivity factor** — The factor 1 + T by which negative feedback divides the fractional sensitivity of the closed-loop gain to the forward gain, dA_f/A_f = (dA/A)/(1 + T); the feedback network's own errors are not divided. *First defined in* [12-05](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-05-feedback-topologies.md). *See also:* [Loop gain](#loop-gain), [Negative feedback](#negative-feedback).

<a id="design-for-test-dft"></a>**Design for test (DFT)** — Design features (scan chains, built-in self-test, test access) that make manufactured chips testable for defects at low cost. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="design-under-test-dut"></a>**Design under test (DUT)** — The design instantiated inside a testbench, whose outputs are driven, observed and checked against a reference model. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md). *See also:* [Testbench](#testbench).

<a id="design-verification"></a>**Design verification** — The engineering function (and activity) of demonstrating, before tapeout, that a design's RTL implements its specification, using simulation, coverage, formal methods and emulation. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="determinant"></a>**Determinant** — The number det A attached to a square matrix, fixed by three rules (det I = 1, a row exchange flips the sign, linearity in each row); it equals ± the product of the pivots, is zero exactly when A is singular, and |det A| is the volume scale factor of the map x → Ax. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md). *See also:* [Cofactor](#cofactor), [Inverse matrix](#inverse-matrix).

<a id="dft-bin"></a>**DFT bin** — One of the N frequencies 2πk/N (k f_s/N in hertz) at which the DFT samples the DTFT; bins above N/2 are negative frequencies, and the bin spacing f_s/N is the reciprocal of the record length. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Discrete Fourier transform (DFT)](#discrete-fourier-transform-dft).

<a id="diagonalization"></a>**Diagonalization** — Writing A = XΛX⁻¹ with eigenvectors in X and eigenvalues in Λ, possible when A has n independent eigenvectors; it gives powers as Aᵏ = XΛᵏX⁻¹. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="diagonally-dominant-matrix"></a>**Diagonally dominant matrix** — A matrix in which each diagonal entry is at least the sum of the magnitudes of the other entries in its row; a nodal conductance matrix is, with strict inequality at nodes that have conductance to ground. *First defined in* [06-04](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-04-nodal-analysis.md). *See also:* [Conductance matrix](#conductance-matrix), [Positive definite matrix](#positive-definite-matrix).

<a id="diamond-structure"></a>**Diamond structure** — The crystal structure of Si, Ge and diamond, a face-centered cubic lattice with a two-atom basis offset by (a/4)(1,1,1), giving 8 atoms per cubic cell and four tetrahedral bonds per atom. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Crystal lattice](#crystal-lattice), [Zinc blende](#zinc-blende).

<a id="dielectric"></a>**Dielectric** — An insulator that polarizes in an electric field, reducing the field of a given free charge by its relative permittivity ε_r and raising a capacitor's capacitance by the same factor. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md). *See also:* [Relative permittivity](#relative-permittivity).

<a id="dielectric-breakdown"></a>**Dielectric breakdown** — The sudden failure of an insulator when the field is strong enough to tear electrons loose and start an avalanche; about 3 MV/m in air and above 10 MV/cm in thermal SiO₂. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="dies-per-wafer"></a>**Dies per wafer** — The number of whole dies that fit on a round wafer, approximated by πd²/(4A) − πd/√(2A); the subtracted edge-loss term grows in relative size as dies get larger. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="difference-equation"></a>**Difference equation** — A recursion relating a sequence's present and past values, y[n] + a₁y[n − 1] + … + a_N y[n − N] = b₀x[n] + … + b_M x[n − M]; with constant coefficients and initial rest it defines a causal LTI system, the discrete-time counterpart of a linear ODE. *First defined in* [11-04](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-04-lti-systems-and-differential-equations.md). *See also:* [IIR filter](#iir-filter), [Characteristic equation](#characteristic-equation).

<a id="difference-quotient"></a>**Difference quotient** — The slope (f(a + h) − f(a))/h of the secant line through two nearby points; its limit as h → 0 is the derivative. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="differentiable"></a>**Differentiable** — Having a derivative at a point; differentiability implies continuity, but not conversely (|x| is continuous with a corner at 0). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="differential-nonlinearity-dnl"></a>**Differential nonlinearity (DNL)** — For a data converter, the deviation of each code step from the ideal 1 LSB, in LSBs; it is largest where many bits switch at once, such as the major carry. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Superposition](#superposition).

<a id="differential-pair"></a>**Differential pair** — Two matched transistors whose emitters or sources share a tail current source, so that the tail fixes their total current and the input difference decides how it splits; the input stage of op-amps, comparators and CML buffers. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Tail current source](#tail-current-source), [Half-circuit](#half-circuit), [Common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR)](#common-mode-rejection-ratio-cmrr).

<a id="differential-signaling"></a>**Differential signaling** — Sending a signal as equal and opposite voltages on two wires and receiving their difference, which doubles the signal and cancels interference common to both wires. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="differential-mode-gain"></a>**Differential-mode gain** — The gain from the difference of a differential stage's two inputs to its output, g_mR_D for a resistor-loaded pair with a differential output and half that for one output. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Common-mode gain](#common-mode-gain), [Differential pair](#differential-pair).

<a id="differentiator-op-amp"></a>**Differentiator (op-amp)** — An op-amp circuit with a capacitor at the input and a resistor in the feedback path, giving v_out = −RC dv_in/dt; a resistor in series with the capacitor caps its gain for fast changes, turning a step's impulse into a finite exponential spike. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="diffraction"></a>**Diffraction** — The spreading of a wave through an aperture or around an edge by about λ/aperture radians; a slit's first zero is at sin θ = λ/a, a circular aperture's at 1.22λ/D. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="diffusion"></a>**Diffusion** — The net flow of carriers from regions of high to low concentration caused by random thermal motion alone, with flux −D dn/dx (Fick's law); the carrier spread grows as √(Dt). *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md). *See also:* [Diffusion coefficient](#diffusion-coefficient), [Fick's law](#ficks-law).

<a id="diffusion-capacitance"></a>**Diffusion capacitance** — The small-signal capacitance from minority charge stored in a forward-biased diode, proportional to bias current; τ_p g_d/2 for a long diode and W²g_d/(3D) for a short one, usually far larger than the junction capacitance in forward bias. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md). *See also:* [Junction capacitance](#junction-capacitance).

<a id="diffusion-coefficient"></a>**Diffusion coefficient** — The constant D linking diffusion flux to concentration gradient (cm²/s); for silicon at 300 K about 35 cm²/s for electrons and 12 cm²/s for holes in lightly doped material, related to mobility by D = (kT/q)μ. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md). *See also:* [Einstein relation](#einstein-relation).

<a id="diffusion-length"></a>**Diffusion length** — The average distance a minority carrier diffuses before recombining, L = √(Dτ); regions much shorter than L transport carriers with little recombination, those much longer absorb them. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="digital-resonator"></a>**Digital resonator** — A second-order recursive filter with poles at r e^{±jω0} near the unit circle (often with zeros at z = ±1), whose response peaks at ω0 with gain about 1/(1 − r), −3 dB width about 2(1 − r) rad/sample and Q about ω0/[2(1 − r)]; it rings for about 1/(1 − r) samples. *First defined in* [16-02](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-02-dtft-and-z-transform-for-dsp.md). *See also:* [Notch filter](#notch-filter), [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros).

<a id="digital-signal"></a>**Digital signal** — A signal that is discrete in time and takes values from a finite set, such as ADC output codes; quantization makes it digital, sampling only makes it discrete-time, and it need not be binary. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Quantization noise](#quantization-noise), [PAM4](#pam4).

<a id="dimension"></a>**Dimension** — The number of vectors in any basis of a subspace (all bases have the same number). *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="dimensional-analysis"></a>**Dimensional analysis** — Checking that every term of an equation has the same physical units (and that arguments of exp, log and trig functions are dimensionless) to catch errors and derive relationships. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md).

<a id="diode-connected-transistor"></a>**Diode-connected transistor** — A transistor with its gate tied to its drain (or base to collector), which is always saturated (active) and behaves as a two-terminal device whose voltage sets itself to carry the current fed to it; the input half of a current mirror. *First defined in* [10-02](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-02-mosfet-dc-operation-and-biasing.md).
