<a id="kronig-penney-model"></a>**Kronig–Penney model** — An exactly solvable model of an electron in a one-dimensional periodic array of square barriers whose dispersion relation, cos kd = F(E), shows how allowed bands and forbidden gaps arise; energies with |F(E)| ≤ 1 are allowed. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Bloch's theorem](#blochs-theorem), [Energy band](#energy-band).

<a id="ktc-noise"></a>**kT/C noise** — The thermal noise sampled onto a capacitor through any resistance, with RMS value √(kT/C), about 64 µV for 1 pF at 300 K; independent of the resistance. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="letter-l"></a>

## L

<a id="lhopitals-rule"></a>**L'Hopital's rule** — For 0/0 or ∞/∞ forms, lim f/g = lim f'/g' when the latter exists (named for L'Hôpital); other indeterminate forms are first rewritten as quotients. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="l-network"></a>**L-network** — A two-element matching network with one series and one shunt reactance; matching R_high to R_low needs Q = √(R_high/R_low − 1), X = Q·R_low and B = Q/R_high, with low-pass and high-pass forms. *First defined in* [13-09](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-09-smith-chart-and-matching.md). *See also:* [Impedance matching](#impedance-matching), [Quality factor](#quality-factor).

<a id="l-section-match"></a>**L-section match** — A lossless two-element network (a series reactance next to the lower resistance and a shunt reactance across the higher) that transforms one resistance into another at one frequency; its Q is √(R_high/R_low − 1). *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md). *See also:* [Mismatch loss](#mismatch-loss).

<a id="lag-compensator"></a>**Lag compensator** — C(s) = (1 + s/z)/(1 + s/p) with z > p, a pole followed by a zero; placed about a decade below crossover, it raises the low-frequency loop gain (and the error constants) by z/p at a cost of a few degrees of phase and a slow settling tail. *First defined in* [15-09](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-09-lead-lag-compensation.md). *See also:* [Lead compensator](#lead-compensator), [Pole–zero doublet](#pole-zero-doublet).

<a id="lagrange-multiplier"></a>**Lagrange multiplier** — The factor λ in ∇f = λ∇g at a constrained optimum; it equals the rate of change of the optimal value with the constraint level, a shadow price. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="lagrange-remainder"></a>**Lagrange remainder** — The error of a degree-n Taylor polynomial, f^(n+1)(ξ)(x − a)^(n+1)/(n + 1)! for some ξ between a and x; bounding f^(n+1) bounds the error. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="landauer-limit"></a>**Landauer limit** — The minimum energy to erase one bit of information, kT ln 2 (about 2.9×10^−21 J at 300 K); practical logic uses orders of magnitude more. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="lane-serial-link"></a>**Lane (serial link)** — One pair of differential signal pairs (transmit and receive) of a serial link such as PCIe; links bundle 1 to 16 lanes, and bandwidth scales with the lane count. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [PCI Express (PCIe)](#pci-express-pcie).

<a id="laplace-transform"></a>**Laplace transform** — F(s) = ∫ f(t) e^(−st) dt from 0⁻ to ∞, with s = σ + jω complex; it turns differentiation into multiplication by s (minus initial conditions), so linear constant-coefficient ODEs become algebra. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Transfer function](#transfer-function), [Partial fractions](#partial-fractions).

<a id="laplaces-equation"></a>**Laplace's equation** — The equation del-squared V = 0 obeyed by the electrostatic potential in a charge-free uniform region; its solutions have no interior maxima or minima, each point being the average of its surroundings. *First defined in* [13-02](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-02-electrostatics-boundary-value-problems.md). *See also:* [Poisson's equation](#poissons-equation), [Uniqueness theorem](#uniqueness-theorem).

<a id="laplacian"></a>**Laplacian** — The divergence of the gradient, ∇²V; in Cartesian coordinates the sum of second partial derivatives. Laplace's equation ∇²V = 0 governs potential in charge-free regions; the vector Laplacian is ∇(∇·A) − ∇×∇×A. *First defined in* [13-01](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-01-vector-calculus-refresher.md). *See also:* [Gradient](#gradient), [Divergence](#divergence).

<a id="latch-inference"></a>**Latch inference** — Synthesis creating a latch because a combinational block leaves an output unassigned on some path, so the output must hold its previous value; prevented by default assignments, complete case/if statements or always_comb. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="latency"></a>**Latency** — The delay between an input event and the corresponding output; a filter that needs M future samples can only run in real time delayed by M samples, so a symmetric N-tap FIR filter has a latency of (N − 1)/2 samples. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md).

<a id="lattice-mismatch"></a>**Lattice mismatch** — The fractional difference f = (a_layer − a_substrate)/a_substrate between the lattice constants of an epitaxial layer and its substrate; 4.2% for Ge on Si, 0.14% for AlAs on GaAs. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Epitaxy](#epitaxy).

<a id="law-of-large-numbers"></a>**Law of large numbers** — The sample mean of independent, identically distributed variables converges to their expectation as the sample grows; its standard error falls like σ/√n. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="law-of-mass-action"></a>**Law of mass action** — In equilibrium, np = n_i², independent of doping, because thermal generation of electron–hole pairs balances their recombination, which is proportional to np; it fails under illumination or current. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md).

<a id="law-of-the-junction"></a>**Law of the junction** — The boundary condition that the minority-carrier density at each depletion edge equals its equilibrium value times e^(qV_A/kT), because the quasi-Fermi levels stay flat across the depletion region; the starting point of the diode equation. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md). *See also:* [Quasi-Fermi level](#quasi-fermi-level), [Ideal diode equation](#ideal-diode-equation).

<a id="law-of-total-variance"></a>**Law of total variance** — Var(Y) = E[Var(Y | X)] + Var(E[Y | X]): the average spread within groups plus the spread of the group means. Explains why mixed wafers, lots or tools vary far more than any one group. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="lcr-meter"></a>**LCR meter** — An instrument that measures a component's complex impedance at a chosen test frequency and level and reports it through a two-element series or parallel model (Cs–Rs, Cp–Rp, Ls–Rs, Lp–Rp, D, Q). *First defined in* [07-05](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-05-sinusoidal-steady-state-and-impedance.md).

<a id="lead-compensator"></a>**Lead compensator** — C(s) = (1 + αTs)/(1 + Ts) with α > 1, a zero followed by a pole; it adds up to arcsin((α − 1)/(α + 1)) of phase at ω_m = 1/(T√α), used to raise phase margin and crossover. It is a PD controller with a filtering pole. *First defined in* [15-09](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-09-lead-lag-compensation.md). *See also:* [Lag compensator](#lag-compensator), [Phase margin](#phase-margin).

<a id="leakage-inductance"></a>**Leakage inductance** — The part of a winding's inductance whose flux does not link the other winding (k < 1); it appears in series in a transformer's equivalent circuit and causes load-dependent voltage drop. *First defined in* [07-09](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-09-mutual-inductance-and-transformers.md). *See also:* [Coupling coefficient](#coupling-coefficient).

<a id="least-recently-used-lru"></a>**Least recently used (LRU)** — A replacement policy that evicts the block in the set that has gone longest without being accessed; real caches often approximate it (pseudo-LRU). *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Set-associative cache](#set-associative-cache).

<a id="least-significant-bit-lsb"></a>**Least significant bit (LSB)** — The smallest step an N-bit converter resolves, full scale / 2^N; errors and noise are often expressed in LSBs. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="least-squares"></a>**Least squares** — Choosing x̂ to minimize ‖b − Ax‖² when Ax = b has no exact solution; geometrically, Ax̂ is the projection of b onto the column space, so the residual is orthogonal to every column. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md). *See also:* [Normal equations](#normal-equations), [Projection](#projection).

<a id="lenzs-law"></a>**Lenz's law** — The induced current flows so as to oppose the change in flux that produced it (the minus sign in Faraday's law), a consequence of energy conservation. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="level-curve"></a>**Level curve** — The set of points where a function of two variables takes a constant value; a contour line. The gradient is perpendicular to it. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="level-shifter"></a>**Level shifter** — A circuit that translates logic levels between two voltage domains so that families with incompatible thresholds can communicate. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="lifetime-killing"></a>**Lifetime killing** — The deliberate shortening of minority-carrier lifetime, by deep-level impurities such as gold or platinum or by irradiation, to speed the turn-off of power diodes and IGBTs at the cost of higher leakage. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="limit"></a>**Limit** — The value L that f(x) approaches as x approaches a (without equaling a), written lim_{x→a} f(x) = L; the value f(a) itself plays no role. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md). *See also:* [One-sided limit](#one-sided-limit), [Continuity](#continuity).

<a id="limit-comparison-test"></a>**Limit comparison test** — If a_k, b_k > 0 and a_k/b_k tends to a finite positive limit, the series Σ a_k and Σ b_k converge or diverge together. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="limit-cycle"></a>**Limit cycle** — A small sustained oscillation in a fixed-point recursive filter with zero or constant input, caused by rounding inside the feedback loop; it cannot occur in the exact linear system. *First defined in* [11-04](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-04-lti-systems-and-differential-equations.md). *See also:* [IIR filter](#iir-filter).

<a id="limiter"></a>**Limiter** — A circuit, also called a clipper, that holds its output below (or above) a set level, typically with diodes from the signal to a reference; the limiting is soft because the diode is exponential. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="line-and-phase-quantities"></a>**Line and phase quantities** — Line voltages are between lines and line currents flow in them; phase quantities belong to each source or load element. In Y, V_L = √3 V_p (leading by 30°) and I_L = I_p; in Δ, V_L = V_p and I_L = √3 I_p. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="line-integral"></a>**Line integral** — The integral of a vector field's component along a path, ∫ F · dr; for a force it is work, for an electric field it is (minus) the voltage difference. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Vector field](#vector-field).

<a id="line-regulation"></a>**Line regulation** — The change in a regulator's output per unit change in its input voltage; r_z/(R + r_z) for a Zener shunt regulator. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="line-spectrum"></a>**Line spectrum** — The plot of a periodic signal's Fourier coefficients (magnitude and phase) against frequency; it consists of lines at the harmonic frequencies only. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md).

<a id="linear-combination"></a>**Linear combination** — A sum c₁v₁ + … + c_kv_k of vectors times scalars. Every matrix–vector product Ax is the linear combination of A's columns with weights x. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="linear-element"></a>**Linear element** — An element whose i–v characteristic is a straight line through the origin (v = Ri); sources, whose lines miss the origin, and diodes are not linear in this sense. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="linear-independence"></a>**Linear independence** — Vectors are independent if the only combination of them equal to 0 has all weights zero; otherwise one of them is a combination of the others. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="linear-phase"></a>**Linear phase** — A frequency response whose phase is −ωτ (plus a constant or sign flips at zeros), so every frequency is delayed by the same τ; a real FIR filter with symmetric or antisymmetric taps has it exactly, with τ = (N − 1)/2 samples. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Group delay](#group-delay), [Distortionless transmission](#distortionless-transmission).

<a id="linear-region"></a>**Linear region** — The MOSFET operating region with V_DS below V_Dsat, where I_D = (W/L)μC_ox(V_GS − V_TH − mV_DS/2)V_DS and the device acts as a voltage-controlled resistor for small V_DS (also called the triode region). *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="linear-feedback-shift-register-lfsr"></a>**Linear-feedback shift register (LFSR)** — A shift register whose input is the XOR of selected stages (the taps); with taps from a primitive polynomial it steps through all 2^n - 1 nonzero states before repeating. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Primitive polynomial](#primitive-polynomial), [Pseudo-random bit sequence (PRBS)](#pseudo-random-bit-sequence-prbs).

<a id="linearity"></a>**Linearity** — The property of a system whose response obeys homogeneity and additivity; circuits of resistors, dependent sources, capacitors and inductors are linear, diodes and transistors (beyond small signals) are not. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Homogeneity](#homogeneity), [Superposition](#superposition).

<a id="linearity-of-expectation"></a>**Linearity of expectation** — E[aX + bY + c] = aE[X] + bE[Y] + c for any random variables, independent or not; it gives expected counts as sums of probabilities. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md). *See also:* [Indicator variable](#indicator-variable).

<a id="linearization"></a>**Linearization** — Replacing a function near a point by its tangent line, L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a); the error grows as the square of the distance from a. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md). *See also:* [Small-signal model](#small-signal-model).

<a id="linearly-graded-junction"></a>**Linearly graded junction** — A junction whose net doping varies linearly through it, N_D − N_A = ax; its depletion width grows as the cube root of the voltage, W = (12ε(V_bi − V_A)/(qa))^(1/3). *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="link-margin"></a>**Link margin** — Received power minus receiver sensitivity, in dB; the extra loss a radio link can tolerate before it fails. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="linked-list"></a>**Linked list** — A sequence of separately allocated nodes, each pointing to the next; O(1) insertion and removal next to a known node, O(n) search, and poor cache behavior compared with arrays. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="linker"></a>**Linker** — The build stage that combines object files and libraries into one executable, connecting each use of a function or variable to its single definition; a missing definition gives an "undefined reference" error. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="linker-relaxation"></a>**Linker relaxation** — A RISC-V linker optimization that shrinks long instruction sequences once final addresses are known, such as replacing an AUIPC + JALR call with a single JAL when the target is within ±1 MiB. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="linting"></a>**Linting** — Static checking of source code for suspicious constructs (width mismatches, inferred latches, unused signals, incomplete sensitivity lists) without simulating it; Verilator's --lint-only mode is a widely used HDL linter. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="list-comprehension"></a>**List comprehension** — A one-expression loop that builds a list, such as [r \* 1000 for r in values if r > 0]; dict and set comprehensions work the same way. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="litmus-test"></a>**Litmus test** — A tiny multithreaded program, such as store buffering or message passing, whose allowed final outcomes characterize a memory consistency model. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Memory consistency model](#memory-consistency-model).

<a id="littles-law"></a>**Little's law** — For any stable queueing system, average occupancy = throughput × average time in the system; it sizes a processor's window (about width × latency to hide) and the outstanding requests a memory system needs. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md).

<a id="load-factor"></a>**Load factor** — For a hash table, entries divided by slots (α = n/m); linear probing needs about ½(1 + 1/(1 − α)) probes per successful search and ½(1 + 1/(1 − α)²) per miss, so tables resize before α reaches about 0.75. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="load-line"></a>**Load line** — The straight line i = (V_Th − v)/R_Th that a linear network imposes on the device it drives; the operating point is where it crosses the device's characteristic. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="load-line-voltage-regulator"></a>**Load line (voltage regulator)** — A deliberately finite DC loop gain in a processor voltage regulator (adaptive voltage positioning), so the output behaves as a small resistance R_LL = ΔV/ΔI; it removes overshoot on load release and lets each transient use the whole tolerance band. *First defined in* [15-12](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-12-control-applications-pll-regulators-thermal.md). *See also:* [Target impedance](#target-impedance).

<a id="load-regulation"></a>**Load regulation** — The change in a regulator's output per unit change in load current, equal to minus its output resistance; −(R ∥ r_z) for a Zener shunt regulator. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="load-switch"></a>**Load switch** — An integrated MOSFET switch with its gate driver and controlled turn-on, used to connect or disconnect a power rail from a load while limiting inrush current. *First defined in* [10-02](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-02-mosfet-dc-operation-and-biasing.md).

<a id="load-reserved-store-conditional-lr-sc"></a>**Load-reserved/store-conditional (LR/SC)** — A pair of atomic instructions: LR loads a word and registers a reservation, and SC stores only if the reservation is still valid, reporting success or failure, so that a short retry loop implements any atomic update. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Spin lock](#spin-lock).

<a id="load-use-hazard"></a>**Load-use hazard** — A data hazard in which an instruction uses the result of the load just before it; the data arrives too late even for forwarding, so the pipeline stalls one cycle unless the compiler schedules an independent instruction in between. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md).

<a id="loaded-q"></a>**Loaded Q** — The quality factor of a resonator as used, including the source and load resistances in parallel (or series) with its own losses; always below the unloaded Q, so the bandwidth f0/Q_L is wider than the resonator alone gives. *First defined in* [07-08](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-08-filters-and-resonance.md). *See also:* [Quality factor](#quality-factor), [Insertion loss](#insertion-loss).

<a id="loader"></a>**Loader** — The part of the operating system that maps an executable's code and data into a process's memory, sets up its stack and jumps to its entry point; on a bare microcontroller, start-up code plays this role. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="loading-effect"></a>**Loading effect** — The drop in a source's or divider's output when a load draws current from it; the relative error is about R_source/R_load when the load is much larger. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="loading-factor"></a>**Loading factor** — An ADC's full-scale amplitude divided by the RMS of a noise-like input, k = V_FS/σ; it trades clipping noise (small k) against granular quantization noise (large k). *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="load-store-architecture"></a>**Load–store architecture** — An ISA in which arithmetic operates only on registers and memory is accessed only by explicit load and store instructions (RISC-V, Arm), in contrast to ISAs such as x86 whose arithmetic can read or write memory directly. *First defined in* [14-02](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-02-isa-risc-v-arm-x86.md).

<a id="locality"></a>**Locality** — The tendency of programs to reuse data and instructions they accessed recently (temporal locality) and to access addresses near recent ones (spatial locality); the property every cache relies on. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Cache block](#cache-block).

<a id="log-log-plot"></a>**Log-log plot** — A graph with both axes logarithmic; a power law y = kxⁿ plots as a straight line of slope n. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="log-normal-distribution"></a>**Log-normal distribution** — The distribution of e^X for Gaussian X; skewed right, with median e^μ and mean e^(μ + σ_ℓ²/2), where σ_ℓ is the standard deviation of X. Subthreshold leakage across devices is approximately log-normal. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="logarithmic-differentiation"></a>**Logarithmic differentiation** — Differentiating ln y instead of y, which turns products, quotients and variable exponents into sums; for example (x^x)' = x^x(1 + ln x). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="logic-synthesis"></a>**Logic synthesis** — Automatic translation of a register-transfer-level description into an optimized netlist of library cells, by elaboration, technology-independent optimization, technology mapping and timing-driven refinement. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md). *See also:* [Technology mapping](#technology-mapping), [And-inverter graph (AIG)](#and-inverter-graph-aig).

<a id="logistic-equation"></a>**Logistic equation** — N' = rN(1 − N/K), growth proportional to the current base and to the remaining room; its S-shaped solution models adoption, epidemics and populations, rising fastest at N = K/2. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="lookup-table-lut"></a>**Lookup table (LUT)** — A small memory of 2^k configuration bits selected by k inputs, able to implement any k-input function; the basic logic element of FPGAs (usually k = 4 or 6). *First defined in* [08-11](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-11-memories-and-programmable-logic.md). *See also:* [Field-programmable gate array (FPGA)](#field-programmable-gate-array-fpga), [Shannon expansion](#shannon-expansion).

<a id="loop"></a>**Loop** — Any closed path through the branches of a circuit that visits no node more than once. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md).

<a id="loop-analysis"></a>**Loop analysis** — The generalization of mesh analysis to any circuit; one loop current per link of a spanning tree (b − n + 1 fundamental loops), with KVL written around each loop. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Spanning tree](#spanning-tree), [Mesh analysis](#mesh-analysis).

<a id="loop-gain"></a>**Loop gain** — The product Aβ of forward gain and feedback fraction around a feedback loop; the closed-loop gain error is about 1/(Aβ). *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="loop-tiling"></a>**Loop tiling** — Restructuring loops to work on blocks (tiles) of data small enough to stay in a cache while they are reused, also called blocking; the key optimization of dense linear algebra. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Locality](#locality).

<a id="lorentz-force"></a>**Lorentz force** — The total electromagnetic force on a charge, F = q(E + v × B); the magnetic part is perpendicular to the velocity and does no work. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="loss-tangent"></a>**Loss tangent** — tan δ, the ratio of a dielectric's lossy to stored response; it makes waves decay at about πf√ε_r tan δ / c nepers per meter, about 0.025 for FR-4-class laminates and 0.004 for low-loss ones at 10 GHz. *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="lot-tolerance-percent-defective-ltpd"></a>**Lot tolerance percent defective (LTPD)** — The defective percentage that a sampling plan rejects with high confidence (usually 90%); zero failures in 230 samples demonstrates LTPD 1. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="low-k-dielectric"></a>**Low-k dielectric** — An interconnect insulator with permittivity below SiO₂'s 3.9 (SiOF, carbon-doped SiOCH at 2.7–3.0, porous films below 2.5, air gaps at 1), used to cut wire capacitance, delay and power. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="low-level-injection"></a>**Low-level injection** — The condition that excess carrier densities are much smaller than the majority density, so the majority density is essentially unchanged and recombination is linear in the excess, U = Δp/τ. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="low-rank-approximation"></a>**Low-rank approximation** — Keeping the first k terms of the SVD, A_k = Σ_{i≤k} σᵢuᵢvᵢᵀ, the closest rank-k matrix to A (Eckart–Young), with 2-norm error σ_{k+1}. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="lti-system"></a>**LTI system** — A system that is both linear and time-invariant; it is completely described by its impulse response (convolution) and passes complex exponentials unchanged in shape, only scaled. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md).

<a id="lu-factorization"></a>**LU factorization** — A = LU, with L lower triangular holding the elimination multipliers and U upper triangular holding the pivots (PA = LU with row exchanges). Factor once in O(n³), then solve each right-hand side in O(n²). *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="luminous-efficacy"></a>**Luminous efficacy** — Light output in lumens (power weighted by the eye's sensitivity) per watt; 683 lm/W at 555 nm, and about 414 lm/W at most for white light with good color rendering. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="lumped-matter-discipline"></a>**Lumped-matter discipline** — The conditions under which fields can be replaced by voltages and currents in lumped elements obeying KVL and KCL, chiefly that the circuit is small compared with the signal wavelength (or line delay is short compared with edge time). *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Transmission line](#transmission-line), [Wavelength](#wavelength).

<a id="letter-m"></a>

## M

<a id="machine-epsilon"></a>**Machine epsilon** — The gap between 1 and the next representable floating-point number, 2^−52 ≈ 2.22×10^−16 for IEEE 754 double precision; the relative precision of a computation. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="magnetic-circuit"></a>**Magnetic circuit** — A path of high-permeability material that guides magnetic flux, analysed like a resistive circuit with magnetomotive force as the source, flux as the current and reluctance as the resistance; an air gap usually dominates its reluctance. *First defined in* [13-03](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-03-magnetostatics-and-inductance.md). *See also:* [Reluctance](#reluctance), [Magnetomotive force](#magnetomotive-force).

<a id="magnetic-dipole-moment"></a>**Magnetic dipole moment** — m = NIA for a current loop (A·m²), pointing along the loop's normal; in a field it feels torque m × B and has energy −m · B, and far away it makes a 1/r³ dipole field. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="magnetic-energy-density"></a>**Magnetic energy density** — The energy per unit volume in a magnetic field, u = B²/(2µ) (about 0.4 MJ/m³ at 1 T in air); in a gapped core most of the energy sits in the gap. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="magnetic-field"></a>**Magnetic field** — The field B (tesla; 1 T = 10⁴ gauss) that exerts force qv × B on moving charges; produced by currents and magnetic moments, with field lines that always close on themselves. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="magnetic-flux"></a>**Magnetic flux** — The surface integral of B, Φ = ∬ B · dA, in webers (1 Wb = 1 T·m² = 1 V·s); its rate of change induces EMF. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="magnetic-tunnel-junction"></a>**Magnetic tunnel junction** — Two ferromagnetic layers separated by a nanometer-thin oxide whose tunneling resistance depends on whether their magnetizations are parallel; the storage element of MRAM. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="magnetic-vector-potential"></a>**Magnetic vector potential** — The field A whose curl is the magnetic flux density, B = ∇ × A; it points along the currents that produce it, obeys ∇²A = −µJ in the Coulomb gauge, and its circulation around a loop is the flux through the loop. *First defined in* [13-03](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-03-magnetostatics-and-inductance.md). *See also:* [Biot–Savart law](#biot-savart-law), [Magnetic flux](#magnetic-flux).

<a id="magnetization"></a>**Magnetization** — The magnetic dipole moment per unit volume of a material, M (A/m), produced by electron spins and orbits; H = B/µ₀ − M, and in a linear material M = χ_m H, so that B = µ_r µ₀ H. *First defined in* [13-03](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-03-magnetostatics-and-inductance.md). *See also:* [Relative permeability](#relative-permeability), [Ferromagnetism](#ferromagnetism).

<a id="magnetizing-inductance"></a>**Magnetizing inductance** — The finite inductance of a transformer's core, appearing as a shunt branch in its equivalent circuit; it draws the magnetizing current needed to set up the flux even with no load. *First defined in* [07-09](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-09-mutual-inductance-and-transformers.md).

<a id="magnetomotive-force"></a>**Magnetomotive force** — The ampere-turns NI that drive flux around a magnetic circuit, the analogue of voltage; equal to the line integral of H around the circuit, and to flux times total reluctance. *First defined in* [13-03](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-03-magnetostatics-and-inductance.md). *See also:* [Magnetic circuit](#magnetic-circuit), [Reluctance](#reluctance).

<a id="magnitude"></a>**Magnitude** — The length |z| = √(x² + y²) of a complex number's arrow (also called modulus or absolute value). *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="magnitude-condition"></a>**Magnitude condition** — K = 1/|G(s)| at a point on the root locus, the product of the distances from the open-loop poles divided by the product of the distances from the zeros; it gives the gain that puts a closed-loop pole there. *First defined in* [15-06](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-06-root-locus.md). *See also:* [Root locus](#root-locus).

<a id="main-decoder"></a>**Main decoder** — The part of the control unit that maps the 7-bit opcode to the datapath's control signals (register write, multiplexer selects, memory write, branch, jump). *First defined in* [14-05](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-05-single-cycle-datapath.md). *See also:* [Control unit](#control-unit).

<a id="majority-carrier"></a>**Majority carrier** — The more numerous carrier type in a doped region, electrons in n-type and holes in p-type material; its density is approximately the net doping. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md). *See also:* [Minority carrier](#minority-carrier).

<a id="marginal-distribution"></a>**Marginal distribution** — The distribution of one variable obtained from a joint distribution by summing or integrating out the others. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="marginal-stability"></a>**Marginal stability** — The case of simple poles on the imaginary axis and none in the right half-plane; the free response neither grows nor decays, but the system is not BIBO stable, because a bounded input at the pole frequency produces a growing output. *First defined in* [15-05](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-05-stability-routh-hurwitz.md). *See also:* [BIBO stability](#bibo-stability).

<a id="markov-chain"></a>**Markov chain** — A random process that moves between states with fixed transition probabilities; its distribution evolves as u_{k+1} = Pu_k, its steady state is the eigenvector for λ = 1, and its convergence rate is set by the second-largest |λ|. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="markovs-inequality"></a>**Markov's inequality** — For a nonnegative random variable, P(X ≥ a) ≤ E[X]/a. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="masons-gain-formula"></a>**Mason's gain formula** — T = Σ PₖΔₖ / Δ, the transfer function of a signal-flow graph, where Pₖ are the forward-path gains, Δ = 1 − Σ loops + Σ products of non-touching pairs − Σ non-touching triples + …, and Δₖ is Δ computed from the loops that do not touch path k. *First defined in* [15-02](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-02-transfer-functions-and-block-diagrams.md). *See also:* [Signal-flow graph](#signal-flow-graph).

<a id="master-slave-flip-flop"></a>**Master–slave flip-flop** — An edge-triggered flip-flop made of two latches on opposite clock phases; the master follows D while the clock is low and closes at the rising edge, as the slave opens and passes the captured value to Q. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md).

<a id="matched-filter"></a>**Matched filter** — A filter whose impulse response is a known pattern reversed in time; its output is the correlation of the input with the pattern and peaks where the pattern occurs, adding the pattern's samples coherently against noise. *First defined in* [11-03](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-03-convolution.md). *See also:* [Cross-correlation](#cross-correlation).

<a id="matched-load"></a>**Matched load** — A load equal to the source's Thévenin resistance (for AC, its complex conjugate), which draws the maximum power, at half the open-circuit voltage (and at 50% efficiency when the source resistance is physical); on a transmission line, a load equal to Z0, which reflects nothing. *First defined in* [06-09](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-09-maximum-power-transfer.md). *See also:* [Maximum power transfer](#maximum-power-transfer), [Conjugate match](#conjugate-match).

<a id="matching-coefficient"></a>**Matching coefficient** — The constant A_Vt = σ(V_TH)√(WL) (mV·µm) that describes how random threshold mismatch shrinks with device area; for random dopant fluctuation it follows from Poisson statistics of the depletion charge. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="matrix"></a>**Matrix** — A rectangular m×n array of numbers; multiplying it by a vector is a linear map from n-component to m-component vectors. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md). *See also:* [Matrix multiplication](#matrix-multiplication).

<a id="matrix-exponential"></a>**Matrix exponential** — e^{At} = I + At + (At)²/2! + …, the matrix that maps an initial state to the state at time t for x' = Ax; computed by diagonalization, by (sI − A)⁻¹, or numerically by scaling and squaring. *First defined in* [02-09](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-09-systems-of-odes-and-matrix-exponential.md).

<a id="matrix-multiplication"></a>**Matrix multiplication** — The product AB defined so that (AB)x = A(Bx); entry (i, j) is row i of A dotted with column j of B. It is associative but not commutative, and an n×n product costs n³ multiply–adds. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="matthiessens-rule"></a>**Matthiessen's rule** — Independent scattering mechanisms add their rates, so 1/μ = 1/μ_lattice + 1/μ_impurity + …; the lowest mobility dominates, like resistors in series. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md). *See also:* [Mobility](#mobility).

<a id="maximum-a-posteriori-map-detection"></a>**Maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection** — Choosing the hypothesis with the largest posterior probability given the observation, which minimizes the probability of error; with equal priors it reduces to maximum-likelihood detection. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="maximum-oscillation-frequency"></a>**Maximum oscillation frequency** — The frequency f_max at which a transistor's power gain falls to 1, about √(f_T/(8π r_b C_jC)) for a bipolar transistor, so base resistance and base–collector capacitance matter as much as transit time. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="maximum-power-point-tracking-mppt"></a>**Maximum power point tracking (MPPT)** — A converter control method that continually adjusts its input operating point (for example by perturb and observe) to extract the most power from a varying source such as a solar cell or thermoelectric generator. *First defined in* [06-09](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-09-maximum-power-transfer.md). *See also:* [Maximum power transfer](#maximum-power-transfer).

<a id="maximum-power-transfer"></a>**Maximum power transfer** — A source of resistance R_s delivers the most power to a load R_L = R_s, namely V_s²/(4R_s); when R_s is a physical series resistance the efficiency is then only 50 %. Used for weak signals (RF, sensors), never for power delivery. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="maxterm"></a>**Maxterm** — A sum containing every input variable exactly once, so that it is 0 in exactly one row of the truth table; the complement of the minterm of the same row. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md). *See also:* [Product of sums (POS)](#product-of-sums-pos), [Minterm](#minterm).

<a id="maxwells-equations"></a>**Maxwell's equations** — Gauss's law, Gauss's law for magnetism, Faraday's law and the Ampère–Maxwell law; with the Lorentz force they are all of classical electromagnetism and predict waves travelling at 1/√(µ₀ε₀) = c. *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="mc-dc"></a>**MC/DC** — Modified condition/decision coverage; each condition in a decision is shown to independently change the outcome by a pair of tests differing only in that condition; needs at least N + 1 tests for N conditions; required for DO-178C Level A. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="mealy-machine"></a>**Mealy machine** — An FSM whose outputs depend on the present state and the present inputs, so they respond within the same cycle but carry a combinational path from input to output. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [Moore machine](#moore-machine).

<a id="mean-free-path"></a>**Mean free path** — The average distance a carrier travels between scattering events, λ = v_F τ; about 39–40 nm for electrons in copper at room temperature, which is why narrower copper wires lose conductivity. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="mean-time-between-failures-mtbf"></a>**Mean time between failures (MTBF)** — The reciprocal of a constant failure rate, 1/λ; a fleet statistic (failures per unit-hour), not an expected lifetime of an individual unit. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="mean-time-to-failure-mttf"></a>**Mean time to failure (MTTF)** — The expected lifetime of a non-repairable component, 1/λ for a constant failure rate λ; MTBF is the analogous figure for repairable systems, and the two are often used loosely as synonyms. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md). *See also:* [Mean time between failures (MTBF)](#mean-time-between-failures-mtbf).

<a id="mean-value-theorem"></a>**Mean value theorem** — For f continuous on [a, b] and differentiable inside, f'(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) for some c in (a, b); hence a bound on |f'| bounds the change of f. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="mechanical-time-constant"></a>**Mechanical time constant** — The time constant RJ/(RB + K²) of a DC motor's speed response when its inductance is neglected; the back-EMF term K²/R usually dominates the damping. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md).

<a id="memory-array"></a>**Memory array** — A grid of bit cells organized in rows and columns, with a row decoder that selects one wordline and column multiplexers that select the addressed word from the selected row. *First defined in* [08-11](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-11-memories-and-programmable-logic.md). *See also:* [Wordline and bitline](#wordline-and-bitline), [Column multiplexer](#column-multiplexer).

<a id="memory-coalescing"></a>**Memory coalescing** — The combining of a warp's memory accesses into as few sectors or cache lines as possible, achieved when consecutive threads access consecutive addresses. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [Warp](#warp).

<a id="memory-consistency-model"></a>**Memory consistency model** — The part of an ISA's contract that specifies the order in which a core's loads and stores to different addresses may appear to other cores, such as sequential consistency, TSO or RISC-V's RVWMO. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Sequential consistency](#sequential-consistency), [Total store ordering (TSO)](#total-store-ordering-tso), [Fence](#fence).

<a id="memory-leak"></a>**Memory leak** — Heap memory that is never freed after its last pointer is lost; harmless in a short program, fatal in a long-running device that slowly exhausts its RAM. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="memory-safety"></a>**Memory safety** — The guarantee that a program cannot access memory outside the objects it is entitled to (no overflows, use after free or invalid pointers); C and C++ lack it, Rust, Python and Java provide it, and hardware such as Arm MTE and CHERI can enforce parts of it. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="memory-level-parallelism-mlp"></a>**Memory-level parallelism (MLP)** — The number of cache misses outstanding at once; by Little's law, delivered bandwidth equals outstanding misses times block size divided by latency. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Little's law](#littles-law), [Prefetching](#prefetching).

<a id="memory-mapped-i-o"></a>**Memory-mapped I/O** — Accessing hardware peripheral registers at fixed memory addresses with ordinary loads and stores; in C, through volatile pointers to those addresses. *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="memoryless-property"></a>**Memoryless property** — P(T > s + t | T > s) = P(T > t), so a surviving item is as good as new; only the exponential (continuous) and geometric (discrete) distributions have it. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="memoryless-system"></a>**Memoryless system** — A system whose output at each time depends only on the input at that same time, such as a resistor divider or a squarer; capacitors, inductors, delays and sums over past samples give memory. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md).

<a id="mems"></a>**MEMS** — Micro-electro-mechanical systems, mechanical structures (springs, masses, membranes, resonators) a few micrometers in size made with semiconductor processes and read out electrically; accelerometers, gyroscopes, microphones and timing resonators are MEMS. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="merge-sort"></a>**Merge sort** — Sorting by recursively sorting two halves and merging them in linear time; n log2 n comparisons in every case, stable, needs O(n) extra memory, and within lower-order terms of the comparison-sort lower bound log2(n!). *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="mesh"></a>**Mesh** — In a planar circuit, a loop that encloses no other branch (a window pane of the drawing); the meshes form a set of b − n + 1 independent loops. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="mesh-analysis"></a>**Mesh analysis** — Solving a planar circuit with circulating mesh currents as unknowns, writing KVL around each mesh so that KCL holds automatically; for resistors and voltage sources the result is R·i = v. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Mesh current](#mesh-current), [Nodal analysis](#nodal-analysis), [Supermesh](#supermesh).

<a id="mesh-current"></a>**Mesh current** — A current assigned to circulate around one mesh of a planar circuit; an outer branch carries its mesh current and a shared branch the difference of two. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Mesh](#mesh), [Mesh analysis](#mesh-analysis).

<a id="mesi-protocol"></a>**MESI protocol** — A write-invalidate cache-coherence protocol whose block states are Modified, Exclusive, Shared and Invalid; the Exclusive state lets a core write data no other core holds without a bus transaction. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Cache coherence](#cache-coherence), [Snooping](#snooping).

<a id="metal-gate"></a>**Metal gate** — A metallic gate electrode, replacing doped polysilicon in advanced CMOS since about 2007, which removes poly depletion and works with high-k dielectrics; NFETs and PFETs need different work-function metals. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="metastability"></a>**Metastability** — The state of a bistable element left near its balance point by an input that changed within its setup-hold window; it resolves to 0 or 1 after a random time whose tail falls exponentially with time constant tau. *First defined in* [08-10](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-10-timing-metastability-cdc.md). *See also:* [Synchronizer](#synchronizer).

<a id="meter-accuracy-specification"></a>**Meter accuracy specification** — A bound on a reading's error, stated as ±(% of reading + counts) or ±(% of reading + % of range) for given conditions (temperature band, time since calibration); the fixed term dominates low on a range. *First defined in* [06-11](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-11-practical-dc-circuits-and-measurement.md). *See also:* [Resolution (measurement)](#resolution-measurement), [Worst-case analysis](#worst-case-analysis).

<a id="method-of-images"></a>**Method of images** — Replacing a grounded conductor by fictitious charges outside the region of interest that make the conductor's surface an equipotential; by uniqueness, the real charges plus the images give the true field in the region. *First defined in* [13-02](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-02-electrostatics-boundary-value-problems.md). *See also:* [Uniqueness theorem](#uniqueness-theorem).

<a id="method-of-undetermined-coefficients"></a>**Method of undetermined coefficients** — Finding a particular solution of a linear ODE by guessing the input's form (constant, polynomial, exponential, sinusoid) with unknown coefficients and matching; multiply the guess by t when it already solves the homogeneous equation. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="microarchitecture"></a>**Microarchitecture** — One implementation of an ISA — its pipeline, caches, branch predictors and execution units — which determines speed and power but not what a program computes. *First defined in* [14-02](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-02-isa-risc-v-arm-x86.md). *See also:* [Instruction-set architecture (ISA)](#instruction-set-architecture-isa).

<a id="midband-gain"></a>**Midband gain** — An amplifier's gain in the frequency range where coupling and bypass capacitors act as short circuits and device capacitances as open circuits, between the low and high corner frequencies. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md).

<a id="miller-compensation"></a>**Miller compensation** — Compensation of a two-stage amplifier by a capacitor C_c across the inverting second stage, which splits the two poles; the gain-bandwidth product becomes g_m1/C_c, the second pole is about g_m2/C_L, and a right-half-plane zero appears at g_m2/C_c. *First defined in* [12-06](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-06-stability-and-compensation.md). *See also:* [Pole splitting](#pole-splitting), [Nulling resistor](#nulling-resistor), [Right-half-plane zero](#right-half-plane-zero).

<a id="miller-effect"></a>**Miller effect** — An impedance connected between the input and output of an inverting amplifier of gain −A looks (1 + A) times smaller (for a capacitance, larger) from the input, because the amplifier multiplies the voltage across it. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Test source](#test-source).

<a id="miller-indices"></a>**Miller indices** — Three integers (hkl) naming a crystal plane, found by taking the reciprocals of its axis intercepts in units of the lattice constant and clearing fractions; [hkl] names a direction, which in cubic crystals is normal to (hkl). *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md).

<a id="miller-theorem"></a>**Miller theorem** — An impedance Z bridging two nodes whose voltages satisfy V_2 = AV_1 can be replaced by Z/(1 − A) from node 1 to ground and Z/(1 − 1/A) from node 2 to ground; for a capacitor across an inverting gain −A_v it gives the input capacitance C(1 + A_v). *First defined in* [12-03](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-03-frequency-response-miller-poles-zeros.md). *See also:* [Miller effect](#miller-effect).

<a id="millmans-theorem"></a>**Millman's theorem** — Practical voltage sources V_k with series resistances R_k in parallel are equivalent to one source of voltage Σ(V_k/R_k)/Σ(1/R_k) with resistance (Σ 1/R_k)^−1. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Source transformation](#source-transformation).

<a id="minimum-energy-point"></a>**Minimum-energy point** — The supply voltage at which a digital circuit's energy per operation is smallest, where falling switching energy balances rising leakage energy; typically a few hundred millivolts in subthreshold CMOS. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="minimum-phase-system"></a>**Minimum-phase system** — A stable system with no zeros in the right half-plane and no pure delay; its phase is fixed by its magnitude curve (Bode's gain–phase relation), so a steady slope of n × 20 dB/decade implies a phase near n × 90°. *First defined in* [07-07](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-07-frequency-response-and-bode-plots.md). *See also:* [Right-half-plane zero](#right-half-plane-zero), [Bode plot](#bode-plot).

<a id="minority-carrier"></a>**Minority carrier** — The less numerous carrier type in a doped region, with density n_i² divided by the majority density in equilibrium; minority carriers govern junction leakage, diffusion currents and bipolar transistor action. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md). *See also:* [Majority carrier](#majority-carrier), [Law of mass action](#law-of-mass-action).

<a id="minority-carrier-diffusion-equation"></a>**Minority-carrier diffusion equation** — The continuity equation for minority carriers in a quasi-neutral region under low-level injection, ∂Δp/∂t = D_p ∂²Δp/∂x² − Δp/τ_p + G_L; it yields the currents of diodes, bipolar transistors and photodiodes. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md). *See also:* [Continuity equation](#continuity-equation), [Diffusion length](#diffusion-length).

<a id="minority-carrier-lifetime"></a>**Minority-carrier lifetime** — The average time an excess minority carrier survives before recombining; under low-level injection the net recombination rate is Δp/τ. In silicon it ranges from milliseconds in pure, lightly doped material to nanoseconds in heavily doped or contaminated regions. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="minterm"></a>**Minterm** — A product containing every input variable exactly once, true or complemented, so that it is 1 in exactly one row of the truth table; m5 = AB'C for three inputs. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md). *See also:* [Sum of products (SOP)](#sum-of-products-sop), [Maxterm](#maxterm).

<a id="mismatch-loss"></a>**Mismatch loss** — −10 lg(1 − |Γ|²), the dB shortfall between the power a mismatched load receives and the source's available power. *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md). *See also:* [Return loss](#return-loss), [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="misra-c"></a>**MISRA C** — A widely used set of C coding guidelines for safety-critical embedded software, originating in the automotive industry; the current edition is MISRA C 2025, which targets C11/C18. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="miss-rate"></a>**Miss rate** — The fraction of accesses to a cache that miss. The local miss rate counts only the accesses that reach a level; the global miss rate counts all accesses issued by the core. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Average memory access time (AMAT)](#average-memory-access-time-amat).

<a id="mixer"></a>**Mixer** — A circuit that multiplies two signals, producing their sum and difference frequencies; it shifts a band from one frequency to another in every radio transmitter and receiver. *First defined in* [11-11](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-11-modulation-and-filtering-applications.md). *See also:* [Superheterodyne receiver](#superheterodyne-receiver), [Image frequency](#image-frequency).

<a id="mlperf"></a>**MLPerf** — MLCommons' machine-learning training and inference benchmarks, with a Closed division (reference models, comparable systems) and an Open division, and inference scenarios from single-stream latency to offline throughput. *First defined in* [14-15](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-15-roofline-and-benchmarks.md). *See also:* [Benchmark](#benchmark).

<a id="mobility"></a>**Mobility** — Drift speed per unit field, µ = eτ/m (cm²/V·s); copper about 44, lightly doped silicon about 1400 for electrons and 470 for holes. Conductivity is neµ. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="mode-field-diameter"></a>**Mode field diameter** — The diameter of the (approximately Gaussian) light spot of a single-mode fibre's guided mode, larger than the core; about 9 µm at 1310 nm for standard single-mode fibre, and it sets splice and connector losses. *First defined in* [13-10](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-10-waveguides-and-resonators.md). *See also:* [V-number](#v-number).

<a id="model-reduction"></a>**Model reduction** — Simplifying a model by dropping states whose dynamics are much faster (or much less important) than those of interest, such as a motor's electrical time constant beside its mechanical one. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md).

<a id="modified-nodal-analysis"></a>**Modified nodal analysis** — The formulation SPICE uses, namely KCL at every node plus extra equations for voltage sources, giving a linear system G·v = i (re-linearized each iteration for nonlinear devices). *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="modulation-doping"></a>**Modulation doping** — Placing donors in a wide-gap barrier so their electrons fall into an undoped narrow-gap channel next to it, separating the electrons from the ionized donors and keeping their mobility high. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="modulation-index"></a>**Modulation index** — In conventional AM, the depth m of the envelope variation A[1 + m x(t)] with |x| ≤ 1; m ≤ 1 keeps the envelope equal to the message, and the sideband share of power is m²P_x/(1 + m²P_x). *First defined in* [11-11](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-11-modulation-and-filtering-applications.md). *See also:* [Amplitude modulation (AM)](#amplitude-modulation-am).

<a id="module-python"></a>**Module (Python)** — A .py file whose functions and names are loaded with import; a package is a folder of modules, and the standard library and pip-installed packages are both used this way. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="modulo-n-counter"></a>**Modulo-N counter** — A counter that cycles through N states and then returns to 0, such as a decade (modulo-10) counter; it needs the smallest number of flip-flops n with 2^n at least N. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Synchronous counter](#synchronous-counter).

<a id="moment"></a>**Moment** — E[Xⁿ], the nth moment of a random variable; the first is the mean, and central moments E[(X − μ)ⁿ] give variance (n = 2), skewness (3) and kurtosis (4) after standardizing. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="moment-of-inertia"></a>**Moment of inertia** — Rotational inertia, I = Σ m r² (kg·m²); ½MR² for a uniform disk. It plays the role of mass in rotation. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="moment-generating-function"></a>**Moment-generating function** — M(s) = E[e^{sX}]; for independent variables the MGF of a sum is the product of their MGFs, which turns convolution into multiplication. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="momentum"></a>**Momentum** — The product p = mv (kg·m/s); conserved in an isolated system, and changed only by impulse. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="moore-machine"></a>**Moore machine** — An FSM whose outputs depend only on the present state, so they change only after a clock edge and respond to an input one cycle later. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [Mealy machine](#mealy-machine).

<a id="moores-law"></a>**Moore's law** — Gordon Moore's observation that the number of components on the most cost-effective chip grows exponentially, doubling every year (1965) and, from his 1975 revision, about every two years. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="mos-capacitor"></a>**MOS capacitor** — A metal (or polysilicon) gate on a thin insulator on a semiconductor, whose surface can be driven into accumulation, depletion or inversion by the gate voltage; the control structure of every MOSFET. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="mosfet"></a>**MOSFET** — The metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistor, a MOS capacitor with source and drain junctions, in which the gate voltage sets the inversion charge of a channel and the drain voltage drives it; the most widely used semiconductor device. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="motional-emf"></a>**Motional EMF** — The EMF Bℓv across a conductor of length ℓ moving at speed v through a field B, the Lorentz force on its charges; the basis of generators. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="moving-average-filter"></a>**Moving-average filter** — The FIR filter y[n] = (1/N)(x[n] + ... + x[n − N + 1]); linear phase with delay (N − 1)/2 samples, white-noise variance gain 1/N, and nulls at multiples of f_s/N, which makes it a cheap filter for a tone and all its harmonics. *First defined in* [16-01](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-01-discrete-time-systems-review.md). *See also:* [FIR filter](#fir-filter), [Recursive moving sum](#recursive-moving-sum).

<a id="multi-cycle-processor"></a>**Multi-cycle processor** — A processor that breaks each instruction into short steps of one clock cycle each, letting instructions take different numbers of cycles and reusing one ALU and memory across steps. *First defined in* [14-05](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-05-single-cycle-datapath.md). *See also:* [Single-cycle processor](#single-cycle-processor).

<a id="multi-threshold-cmos"></a>**Multi-threshold CMOS** — The practice of offering several threshold-voltage flavors on one chip, using high-V_TH devices everywhere and low-V_TH devices only on speed-critical paths, to trade leakage against speed. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="multigate-transistor"></a>**Multigate transistor** — A MOSFET whose thin body is gated from two or more sides (double-gate, FinFET, gate-all-around), so no leakage path is far from a gate and the subthreshold swing approaches its ideal value. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="multilayer-ceramic-capacitor-mlcc"></a>**Multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC)** — A capacitor of many thin ceramic layers interleaved with electrodes; class 1 (C0G) is stable, while class 2 (X5R, X7R) uses BaTiO₃ with ε_r in the thousands and loses capacitance with DC bias and temperature. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="multiple-feedback-mfb-filter"></a>**Multiple-feedback (MFB) filter** — An active filter section built around an op-amp as an inverting integrator, with feedback through both a resistor and a capacitor into a virtual ground; it inverts, has low sensitivity and avoids the Sallen–Key's high-frequency leakage. *First defined in* [07-08](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-08-filters-and-resonance.md). *See also:* [Sallen–Key filter](#sallen-key-filter).

<a id="multiplexer"></a>**Multiplexer** — A block that connects one of 2^k data inputs to its output, chosen by k select lines; a 2^(n-1)-input multiplexer with an inverter can implement any n-input function, which is how FPGA lookup tables work. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md). *See also:* [Shannon expansion](#shannon-expansion), [Decoder](#decoder).

<a id="multiply-accumulate-mac"></a>**Multiply-accumulate (MAC)** — The operation acc = acc + a·b, the inner loop of filters, matrix products and neural networks; its multiplier and accumulator widths set much of a DSP or AI chip's area and energy. *First defined in* [08-09](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-09-arithmetic-circuits.md). *See also:* [Q format](#q-format).

<a id="multiply-high"></a>**Multiply-high** — An instruction that returns the upper half of a double-width product (RISC-V MULH, MULHU, MULHSU); used for full-width products and for dividing by constants. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md).

<a id="multistage-amplifier"></a>**Multistage amplifier** — A cascade of gain stages whose gains multiply, reduced by loading where one stage's output resistance meets the next stage's input resistance; offsets of later stages refer to the input divided by the gain before them. *First defined in* [12-02](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-02-active-loads-cascodes-multistage.md). *See also:* [Telescopic cascode amplifier](#telescopic-cascode-amplifier), [Systematic offset](#systematic-offset).

<a id="mutable-object"></a>**Mutable object** — An object whose contents can change after creation (Python lists, dicts, sets); immutable objects (numbers, strings, tuples) cannot, which makes sharing them safe. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="mutual-inductance"></a>**Mutual inductance** — The flux linked in one coil per ampere in another, M (henries), so that v₂ = M di₁/dt; M = k√(L₁L₂). *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="letter-n"></a>

## N

<a id="nagaoka-coefficient"></a>**Nagaoka coefficient** — The factor K ≤ 1 by which a finite solenoid's inductance falls below the long-solenoid formula µ₀N²A/ℓ, because the field spreads out near the ends; about 0.92 for a coil five diameters long and 0.82 for one two diameters long. *First defined in* [13-03](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-03-magnetostatics-and-inductance.md). *See also:* [Solenoid](#solenoid), [Inductance](#inductance).

<a id="name-dependence"></a>**Name dependence** — A write-after-read (WAR, anti-) or write-after-write (WAW, output) dependence, which exists only because two values share a register name and is removed by register renaming. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [True dependence](#true-dependence), [Register renaming](#register-renaming).

<a id="nan"></a>**NaN** — Not a Number, the IEEE 754 value produced by undefined operations such as 0/0; it propagates through arithmetic and compares unequal to everything, including itself. *First defined in* [05-02](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-02-numpy-and-vectorization.md).

<a id="nand-gate"></a>**NAND gate** — A gate whose output is 0 only when all inputs are 1, the complement of AND; functionally complete on its own, and in static CMOS the cheapest multi-input gate (pMOS in parallel, nMOS in series). *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md). *See also:* [Functional completeness](#functional-completeness), [Static CMOS](#static-cmos).

<a id="nanosheet"></a>**Nanosheet** — A thin, wide silicon channel layer, several of which are stacked and each wrapped by the gate in a gate-all-around transistor; its drawn width sets the device width continuously. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="natural-frequency"></a>**Natural frequency** — ω₀ = 1/√(LC) (rad/s), the frequency at which a second-order system would oscillate with no damping; for a mass on a spring, √(k/m). *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="natural-logarithm"></a>**Natural logarithm** — ln y, the inverse of eˣ, defined for y > 0; it turns products into sums, ln(ab) = ln a + ln b. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="natural-response"></a>**Natural response** — The response of a circuit with no sources acting, driven only by the energy initially stored in its capacitors and inductors; for a first-order circuit, an exponential decay. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="negative-feedback"></a>**Negative feedback** — Returning a fraction of a system's output to subtract from its input, which trades excess gain for gains set by passive components, lower sensitivity to the amplifier's parameters and corrected errors. *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [Loop gain](#loop-gain), [Virtual short](#virtual-short).

<a id="negative-resistance"></a>**Negative resistance** — A port whose current flows out when a positive voltage is applied (v/i < 0), so it delivers power; it requires an active element such as a dependent source with positive feedback, and is the basis of oscillators. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Dependent source](#dependent-source).

<a id="neper"></a>**Neper** — The natural-logarithm unit of a logarithmic ratio, ln(F2/F1) Np for amplitudes and ½ ln(P2/P1) Np for powers; 1 Np = 20/ln 10 = 8.686 dB. Bode wrote his gain–phase relations in nepers and radians. *First defined in* [07-07](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-07-frequency-response-and-bode-plots.md). *See also:* [Decibel](#decibel).

<a id="neper-frequency"></a>**Neper frequency** — α (1/s), the decay rate of a second-order system's envelope e^{−αt}; R/(2L) for a series RLC and 1/(2RC) for a parallel RLC. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="netlist"></a>**Netlist** — A text description of a circuit listing each element, its value and the nodes it connects; the input to a circuit simulator (node 0 is ground). *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="network-on-chip-noc"></a>**Network-on-chip (NoC)** — An on-chip interconnect of routers and point-to-point links, often a 2D mesh, that carries packets between cores, caches, memory controllers and accelerators, scaling better than a shared bus or a crossbar. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [Bisection bandwidth](#bisection-bandwidth).

<a id="neutral-current"></a>**Neutral current** — The phasor sum of the three line currents in a four-wire system; zero for balanced loads without triplen harmonics, nonzero for unbalanced loads. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).
