<a id="newtons-laws-of-motion"></a>**Newton's laws of motion** — (1) A body with no net force keeps a constant velocity; (2) the net force equals the rate of change of momentum, F = dp/dt = ma for constant mass; (3) forces come in equal and opposite pairs. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="newtons-method"></a>**Newton's method** — Root finding by repeatedly solving the tangent-line approximation, x_{k+1} = x_k − f(x_k)/f'(x_k); converges quadratically near a simple root but can diverge from a poor start. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md). *See also:* [Newton–Raphson method](#newton-raphson-method), [Quadratic convergence](#quadratic-convergence).

<a id="newton-raphson-method"></a>**Newton–Raphson method** — An iterative root-finding method, x_{k+1} = x_k − g(x_k)/g′(x_k), that circuit simulators use to solve nonlinear equations; it converges quadratically near a solution but can overshoot far from it. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="nodal-analysis"></a>**Nodal analysis** — Solving a circuit with the voltages of its non-reference nodes as unknowns, writing KCL at each node so that KVL holds automatically; for resistors and current sources the result is G·v = i. *First defined in* [06-04](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-04-nodal-analysis.md). *See also:* [Conductance matrix](#conductance-matrix), [Modified nodal analysis](#modified-nodal-analysis), [Supernode](#supernode).

<a id="node"></a>**Node** — A point where two or more circuit elements connect, together with the ideal wire joining them; in the lumped model it stores no charge. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md). *See also:* [Branch](#branch), [Loop](#loop).

<a id="node-voltage"></a>**Node voltage** — The voltage of a node relative to the reference node; every branch voltage is the difference of its two node voltages, so node voltages satisfy KVL by construction. *First defined in* [06-04](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-04-nodal-analysis.md). *See also:* [Reference node (ground)](#reference-node-ground), [Nodal analysis](#nodal-analysis).

<a id="noise-enhancement"></a>**Noise enhancement** — The rise in output noise when an equalizer inverts a channel: the equalizer's gain is high wherever the channel's response is low, so noise there is amplified; it grows without bound near a channel null and limits how much loss linear equalization can recover. *First defined in* [16-02](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-02-dtft-and-z-transform-for-dsp.md). *See also:* [Feed-forward equalizer (FFE)](#feed-forward-equalizer-ffe), [Decision-feedback equalizer (DFE)](#decision-feedback-equalizer-dfe).

<a id="noise-figure"></a>**Noise figure** — 10 log₁₀ of the noise factor F, the ratio of a system's total output noise to the part due to a source at 290 K; a receiver's noise floor is −174 dBm/Hz + 10 log₁₀B + NF. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="noise-gain"></a>**Noise gain** — The gain 1 + R2/R1 from a signal at the op-amp's + input (offset voltage, input noise) to its output; it is the same for inverting and non-inverting stages and sets the finite-gain error, about (noise gain)/A. *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [Input offset voltage](#input-offset-voltage), [Loop gain](#loop-gain).

<a id="noise-margin"></a>**Noise margin** — The amount of noise a digital connection can tolerate, NM_L = V_IL − V_OL and NM_H = V_OH − V_IH. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="non-blocking-assignment"></a>**Non-blocking assignment** — The Verilog assignment a <= b, whose right-hand side is evaluated immediately but whose update is deferred to the end of the time step, so all registers in a clocked block sample their inputs simultaneously like real flip-flops. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md). *See also:* [Blocking assignment](#blocking-assignment).

<a id="non-minimum-phase-system"></a>**Non-minimum-phase system** — A system with a zero (or delay) in the right half-plane; its step response starts in the wrong direction (undershoot), and the zero limits how fast any feedback controller can make the loop, as in a boost converter. *First defined in* [15-03](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-03-time-response.md). *See also:* [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros).

<a id="non-recurring-engineering-nre"></a>**Non-recurring engineering (NRE)** — One-time costs of developing a product (design labor, EDA tools, IP licenses, masks, prototypes), as opposed to per-unit manufacturing cost. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="nonlinear-least-squares"></a>**Nonlinear least squares** — Fitting a model whose parameters enter nonlinearly (such as a time constant in an exponential) by iteratively minimizing the sum of squared residuals from a starting guess, as SciPy's curve_fit does; it also estimates the parameters' standard errors. *First defined in* [05-03](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-03-scipy-sympy-matplotlib.md). *See also:* [Least squares](#least-squares), [Residual](#residual).

<a id="norm"></a>**Norm** — The length of a vector, ‖v‖ = √(v·v); for a sampled signal, ‖v‖/√N is its RMS value. For complex vectors, ‖v‖² = Σ|vᵢ|². *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md). *See also:* [Dot product](#dot-product).

<a id="normal-equations"></a>**Normal equations** — AᵀA x̂ = Aᵀb, the square system whose solution is the least-squares fit; uniquely solvable when A has independent columns. Software prefers QR or SVD, which avoid squaring the condition number. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="normal-mode"></a>**Normal mode** — A pattern of motion in which every part of a coupled linear system oscillates at the same frequency; mathematically an eigenvector of the system, such as the in-phase and out-of-phase modes of two coupled resonators. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="normalized-impedance"></a>**Normalized impedance** — z = Z/Z₀, an impedance divided by the reference (characteristic) impedance; Γ = (z − 1)/(z + 1), and admittance is normalized as y = Y·Z₀. *First defined in* [13-09](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-09-smith-chart-and-matching.md). *See also:* [Smith chart](#smith-chart).

<a id="norton-equivalent"></a>**Norton equivalent** — A current source I_N (the short-circuit current) in parallel with R_th, equivalent at two terminals to any linear network; V_th = R_th I_N. *First defined in* [06-08](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-08-thevenin-and-norton.md). *See also:* [Thevenin equivalent](#thevenin-equivalent), [Short-circuit current](#short-circuit-current).

<a id="notch-filter"></a>**Notch filter** — A band-stop filter whose response falls to zero at one frequency, from numerator zeros on the imaginary axis (s² + ω0²); used to remove a single interfering tone such as mains hum. *First defined in* [07-08](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-08-filters-and-resonance.md).

<a id="null-pointer"></a>**Null pointer** — A pointer value (NULL) that points to no object, used to signal "none" or failure (malloc returns NULL when out of memory); must be checked before dereferencing. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="null-space"></a>**Null space** — N(A), the set of all solutions of Ax = 0; every solution of Ax = b is one particular solution plus a vector in N(A). *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="nulling-resistor"></a>**Nulling resistor** — A resistor R_z in series with a Miller compensation capacitor; R_z = 1/g_m2 moves the right-half-plane zero to infinity, and a larger value turns it into a left-half-plane zero that can cancel the second pole, at the cost of a new pole near 1/(R_zC_1). *First defined in* [12-06](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-06-stability-and-compensation.md). *See also:* [Miller compensation](#miller-compensation), [Right-half-plane zero](#right-half-plane-zero).

<a id="numerical-aperture"></a>**Numerical aperture** — NA = n sin θ_max, the half-angle of the cone of light a lens or fiber accepts; it sets lithography resolution (∝ 1/NA) and fiber acceptance (√(n₁² − n₂²)). *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="nyquist-criterion"></a>**Nyquist criterion** — Z = N + P, the number of unstable closed-loop poles equals the clockwise encirclements of −1 by the Nyquist plot of L(s) plus the number of open-loop right-half-plane poles; stability requires N = −P. It follows from the argument principle and handles time delay exactly. *First defined in* [15-07](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-07-frequency-domain-design.md). *See also:* [Phase margin](#phase-margin), [Gain margin](#gain-margin).

<a id="nyquist-frequency"></a>**Nyquist frequency** — Half the symbol (or sample) rate: the highest frequency in a symbol pattern alternating every symbol, the reference frequency at which link channels are specified, and the limit of unambiguous frequency for sampled signals. *First defined in* [11-06](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-06-continuous-time-fourier-transform.md).

<a id="nyquist-rate"></a>**Nyquist rate** — Twice the highest frequency in a band-limited signal: the sample rate the sampling theorem requires to be exceeded (compare the Nyquist frequency, half the sample rate actually used). *First defined in* [11-10](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-10-sampling-aliasing-reconstruction.md). *See also:* [Nyquist frequency](#nyquist-frequency), [Sampling theorem](#sampling-theorem).

<a id="nyquist-zone"></a>**Nyquist zone** — One of the frequency intervals [(n − 1)f_s/2, nf_s/2] into which sampling at f_s divides the axis; every zone folds onto the first, with even zones spectrally inverted. *First defined in* [11-10](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-10-sampling-aliasing-reconstruction.md). *See also:* [Band-pass sampling](#band-pass-sampling).

<a id="letter-o"></a>

## O

<a id="object-file"></a>**Object file** — The output of an assembler or compiler for one source file — machine code and data in sections (.text, .data, .rodata, .bss), a symbol table, and relocations — in a format such as ELF. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md). *See also:* [Relocation](#relocation).

<a id="observability"></a>**Observability** — The property that a system's initial state can be determined from its outputs over a finite time; tested by the rank of the matrix of stacked C, CA, …, CA^(n−1). It is the dual of controllability. *First defined in* [15-10](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-10-state-space-introduction.md). *See also:* [Controllability](#controllability), [State observer](#state-observer).

<a id="occupancy"></a>**Occupancy** — The number of warps resident on an SM as a fraction of the maximum, limited by registers, shared memory and block slots; it determines how much memory latency the SM can hide. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [Streaming multiprocessor (SM)](#streaming-multiprocessor-sm).

<a id="ofdm"></a>**OFDM** — Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing: data symbols are placed on DFT bins (subcarriers), converted to a time signal by an inverse DFT, and recovered by a DFT; with a cyclic prefix, each subcarrier sees the channel as one complex gain. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Cyclic prefix](#cyclic-prefix), [Discrete Fourier transform (DFT)](#discrete-fourier-transform-dft).

<a id="off-state-current"></a>**Off-state current** — The drain current I_off at V_GS = 0 and V_DS = V_DD, mainly subthreshold leakage, equal to the threshold-defining current times 10^(−V_TH/S); it sets standby power. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="offset-drift"></a>**Offset drift** — The change of an amplifier's input offset voltage with temperature, specified in µV/°C; unlike the room-temperature offset, it cannot be removed by a single calibration. *First defined in* [10-09](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-09-real-op-amps-nonidealities.md). *See also:* [Input offset voltage](#input-offset-voltage).

<a id="ohms-law"></a>**Ohm's law** — Current proportional to voltage, V = IR, or locally J = σE; it holds for metals and doped semiconductors at moderate fields and fails at high fields, high frequencies, very short lengths and in junctions. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="ohmic-contact"></a>**Ohmic contact** — A metal–semiconductor contact with low resistance in both directions, made by doping the semiconductor so heavily that the barrier is only nanometers thick and carriers tunnel through it. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="on-resistance"></a>**On-resistance** — The drain-to-source resistance of a MOSFET switched fully on, about 1/[μC_ox(W/L)(V_GS − V_TH)] in deep triode; data sheets quote R_DS(on) at stated gate voltages and temperatures. *First defined in* [10-02](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-02-mosfet-dc-operation-and-biasing.md).

<a id="one-hot-encoding"></a>**One-hot encoding** — A state assignment with one flip-flop per state, exactly one of which is 1; it gives shallow next-state logic and detects any single bit flip, at the cost of N flip-flops and many illegal codes. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [State assignment](#state-assignment), [Illegal state](#illegal-state).

<a id="one-sided-junction"></a>**One-sided junction** — A strongly asymmetric junction (P⁺N or N⁺P) whose depletion region, capacitance and breakdown voltage are set by the lightly doped side, W ≈ √(2ε(V_bi − V_A)/(qN)). *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="one-sided-limit"></a>**One-sided limit** — A limit taken from one side only, x → a⁻ (from below) or x → a⁺ (from above). Circuit analysis writes v(0⁻) and v(0⁺) for the values just before and just after a switching instant. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="open-circuit"></a>**Open circuit** — A break with zero current whatever the voltage across it (R = ∞); an unconnected terminal or an open ideal switch. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md). *See also:* [Short circuit](#short-circuit).

<a id="open-circuit-time-constants"></a>**Open-circuit time constants** — The products R_i0C_i of each capacitor and the resistance it sees with every other capacitor open; their sum is exactly the coefficient b_1 of the circuit's denominator, and 1/Σ R_i0C_i is a conservative estimate of the upper −3 dB frequency. *First defined in* [12-04](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-04-high-frequency-analysis-methods.md). *See also:* [Zero-value time constants](#zero-value-time-constants), [Dominant-pole approximation](#dominant-pole-approximation).

<a id="open-circuit-voltage"></a>**Open-circuit voltage** — The terminal voltage of a source or network with no load connected (zero current), V_oc. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="open-drain-output"></a>**Open-drain output** — An output stage that can only pull its pin low; a pull-up resistor supplies the high level, which allows wired-OR connections and level shifting at the cost of a resistor-capacitor rise time and static current when low. *First defined in* [10-10](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-10-op-amp-application-circuits.md).

<a id="operating-point"></a>**Operating point** — The DC voltages and currents of a circuit with its sources at their DC values (capacitors open, inductors shorted); also called the bias point. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="operational-amplifier"></a>**Operational amplifier** — A high-gain differential amplifier, v_out = A(v+ − v−), with very high input resistance and low output resistance, used almost always with negative feedback so that the external components, not A, set the circuit's behavior. *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [VCVS](#vcvs), [Virtual short](#virtual-short), [Negative feedback](#negative-feedback).

<a id="optical-fiber"></a>**Optical fiber** — A glass core of slightly higher index than its cladding that guides light by total internal reflection; single-mode fiber (≈ 9 µm core) for long reach, multimode for short links at 850 nm. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="optical-phonon"></a>**Optical phonon** — A high-energy lattice vibration (63 meV in silicon) in which neighboring atoms move against each other; emission of optical phonons by hot carriers is the main cause of velocity saturation. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md).

<a id="order-of-accuracy"></a>**Order of accuracy** — The exponent p in a numerical method's global error ∝ hᵖ; halving the step divides the error by 2ᵖ (Euler 1, Heun 2, RK4 4). *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md).

<a id="ordinary-differential-equation"></a>**Ordinary differential equation** — An equation relating an unknown function of one variable to its derivatives; its order is that of the highest derivative. A first-order ODE y' = f(t, y) describes any system with a single store of charge, flux, heat or money. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="orthogonal-matrix"></a>**Orthogonal matrix** — A square matrix Q with orthonormal columns, so QᵀQ = I and Q⁻¹ = Qᵀ; it is a rotation or reflection, preserves lengths and angles, and has all singular values equal to 1. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="orthogonality"></a>**Orthogonality** — The property that sinusoids of different integer frequencies multiply to zero average over a common period; it makes Fourier coefficients computable and harmonic powers additive. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="osat"></a>**OSAT** — Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test, a company that packages and tests chips for others. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="out-of-order-execution"></a>**Out-of-order execution** — Executing instructions in the order their operands become ready rather than in program order, within a window of upcoming instructions, while retiring them in program order so that software sees sequential behaviour. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [Reorder buffer (ROB)](#reorder-buffer-rob), [Register renaming](#register-renaming).

<a id="output-resistance"></a>**Output resistance** — The Thévenin resistance seen looking into a circuit's output terminals; it sets how much the output voltage sags under load (load regulation) and forms a divider with the next stage's input resistance. *First defined in* [06-08](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-08-thevenin-and-norton.md). *See also:* [Thevenin equivalent](#thevenin-equivalent), [Loading effect](#loading-effect).

<a id="output-stationary"></a>**Output-stationary** — A dataflow in which each processing element holds one output's accumulator while inputs and weights stream past, suiting long accumulations. *First defined in* [14-14](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-14-ai-accelerators.md). *See also:* [Dataflow (accelerator)](#dataflow-accelerator).

<a id="overdamped"></a>**Overdamped** — A second-order system with ζ > 1, whose two real negative roots give a sum of decaying exponentials with no overshoot; more damping makes it slower. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="overdrive-voltage"></a>**Overdrive voltage** — The amount by which the gate-source voltage exceeds threshold, V_ov = V_GS − V_TH; drive current, transconductance efficiency (2/V_ov) and V_Dsat all depend on it. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="overkill"></a>**Overkill** — Good parts wrongly rejected by a production test, the false positives of the test. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="overlap-capacitance"></a>**Overlap capacitance** — The capacitance between a MOSFET's gate and the source or drain diffusion it slightly overlaps, proportional to the device width; it is essentially all of C_gd in saturation, the capacitance the Miller effect multiplies. *First defined in* [12-03](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-03-frequency-response-miller-poles-zeros.md). *See also:* [Miller effect](#miller-effect), [Junction capacitance](#junction-capacitance).

<a id="overlap-add"></a>**Overlap-add** — Block convolution that splits the input into blocks of L samples, convolves each with the filter by N-point DFTs (N ≥ L + M − 1), and adds the overlapping M − 1 samples of consecutive block outputs. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Overlap-save](#overlap-save), [Circular convolution](#circular-convolution).

<a id="overlap-save"></a>**Overlap-save** — Block convolution that takes overlapping input blocks of N samples, computes each block's N-point circular convolution with the filter, and keeps only the last N − M + 1 outputs, discarding those corrupted by wrap-around. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Overlap-add](#overlap-add), [Circular convolution](#circular-convolution).

<a id="oversampling"></a>**Oversampling** — Sampling far above the Nyquist rate, which relaxes the analog anti-aliasing filter and spreads quantization noise thinly (10 log₁₀ OSR dB less in band after digital filtering), followed by digital filtering and decimation. *First defined in* [11-10](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-10-sampling-aliasing-reconstruction.md). *See also:* [Decimation](#decimation), [Anti-aliasing filter](#anti-aliasing-filter).

<a id="overshoot"></a>**Overshoot** — The amount by which a step response exceeds its final value, as a fraction of the step; exp(−πζ/√(1 − ζ²)) for a second-order system (16.3% at ζ = 0.5, 4.3% at ζ = 0.707). *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="oxide-capacitance"></a>**Oxide capacitance** — The gate-dielectric capacitance per area, C_ox = ε_ox/T_ox, 345 nF/cm² for 10 nm of SiO₂; it sets how much channel charge each volt of gate overdrive induces. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="oxide-charge"></a>**Oxide charge** — Charge in or at the edge of a gate dielectric (fixed charge, mobile ions such as sodium, trapped charge) that shifts the flat-band and threshold voltages by −Q_ox/C_ox; about 10¹⁰ cm⁻² at a high-quality Si–SiO₂ interface. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="letter-p"></a>

## P

<a id="p-value"></a>**p-value** — The probability, if the null hypothesis is true, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed; not the probability that the null hypothesis is true. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="page-memory"></a>**Page (memory)** — The fixed-size unit (typically 4 KiB) in which virtual memory maps addresses; a virtual page number is translated to a physical page (frame) number while the page offset passes through unchanged. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Virtual memory](#virtual-memory), [Huge page](#huge-page).

<a id="page-fault"></a>**Page fault** — The exception raised when a translation finds no valid mapping or a forbidden access; the operating system's handler may fix the cause (demand paging, copy-on-write) and re-execute the instruction. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Demand paging](#demand-paging), [Trap (processor)](#trap-processor).

<a id="page-table"></a>**Page table** — The per-process data structure, usually a multilevel radix tree, that maps virtual page numbers to physical page numbers and permissions; the hardware walks it on a TLB miss. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Page-table entry (PTE)](#page-table-entry-pte), [Translation lookaside buffer (TLB)](#translation-lookaside-buffer-tlb).

<a id="page-table-entry-pte"></a>**Page-table entry (PTE)** — One entry of a page table, holding a physical page number and flag bits (valid, read, write, execute, user, global, accessed, dirty); a PTE with no read, write or execute permission points to the next level. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Page table](#page-table).

<a id="pairwise-summation"></a>**Pairwise summation** — Adding numbers in a balanced binary tree, so that each value passes through about log₂ n roundings instead of up to n; the shape of parallel reductions. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md). *See also:* [Kahan summation](#kahan-summation).

<a id="pam4"></a>**PAM4** — Four-level pulse-amplitude modulation, carrying two bits per symbol; it doubles a link's bit rate at the same symbol rate and Nyquist frequency as two-level signaling, at the cost of eyes a third as tall for the same swing (PCIe 6.0). *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md).

<a id="parallel-connection"></a>**Parallel connection** — Elements connected between the same two nodes, so they share the same voltage; parallel conductances add (R1 ∥ R2 = R1R2/(R1 + R2)). *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md). *See also:* [Current divider](#current-divider).

<a id="parallel-termination"></a>**Parallel termination** — A resistor equal to Z₀ at the receiver end of a line (to ground, a supply or a mid-rail), which absorbs the incident wave so nothing reflects, at the cost of DC current whenever the line is driven away from the termination voltage. *First defined in* [13-07](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-07-transmission-lines-time-domain.md). *See also:* [Series termination](#series-termination).

<a id="parallel-prefix-adder"></a>**Parallel-prefix adder** — An adder that computes every carry as a prefix of (generate, propagate) pairs combined by an associative operator in a tree, giving a delay that grows with log2 n; Kogge–Stone, Sklansky and Brent–Kung are classic networks. *First defined in* [08-09](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-09-arithmetic-circuits.md). *See also:* [Kogge–Stone adder](#kogge-stone-adder), [Brent–Kung adder](#brent-kung-adder).

<a id="parasitic-series-resistance"></a>**Parasitic series resistance** — The source and drain resistance (extensions, silicide, contacts) in series with a MOSFET channel; the source part lowers the internal overdrive by I_D R_S and can cost 10% or more of drive current. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="parity-bit"></a>**Parity bit** — A bit appended so that the number of 1s in a word is even (or odd); it detects any odd number of bit errors and no even number. *First defined in* [08-01](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-01-number-systems-and-codes.md). *See also:* [Hamming distance](#hamming-distance).

<a id="parsevals-relation"></a>**Parseval's relation** — For a periodic signal, average power equals the sum of the harmonic powers, (1/T₀)∫|x|² dt = Σ|c_k|²; RMS values of different harmonics therefore add in quadrature. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md). *See also:* [Orthogonality](#orthogonality), [Total harmonic distortion (THD)](#total-harmonic-distortion-thd).

<a id="part-average-testing-pat"></a>**Part Average Testing (PAT)** — An automotive outlier screen (AEC-Q001) that rejects parts passing specification but lying beyond the median ± 6 robust sigma (interquartile range/1.35) of their population. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="partial-derivative"></a>**Partial derivative** — The rate of change of a function of several variables with respect to one of them, all others held fixed, ∂f/∂x; a sensitivity. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="partial-fractions"></a>**Partial fractions** — Writing a proper rational function as a sum of simple terms, one per factor of the denominator; in circuit analysis each term is a natural mode (pole) of the response. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="partial-inductance"></a>**Partial inductance** — The share of a closed loop's inductance assigned to one segment of it, so that the loop inductance is the signed sum of the segments' partial self- and mutual inductances; the only meaningful inductance of an isolated wire such as a bond wire, about 1 nH/mm. *First defined in* [13-03](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-03-magnetostatics-and-inductance.md). *See also:* [Inductance](#inductance), [Mutual inductance](#mutual-inductance).

<a id="partial-pivoting"></a>**Partial pivoting** — Exchanging rows at each elimination step so that the largest-magnitude entry in the column becomes the pivot; it keeps every multiplier at most 1 in magnitude and prevents roundoff from swamping the solution. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="partial-product"></a>**Partial product** — One shifted row of a multiplication, the multiplicand ANDed with a single bit (or Booth digit) of the multiplier; a multiplier's job is to add all its partial products. *First defined in* [08-09](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-09-arithmetic-circuits.md). *See also:* [Dadda tree](#dadda-tree), [Booth recoding](#booth-recoding).

<a id="particular-solution"></a>**Particular solution** — Any one solution of a forced (nonhomogeneous) linear ODE; the general solution is a particular solution plus the general homogeneous solution. *First defined in* [02-04](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-04-forced-response-and-resonance.md).

<a id="partition-refinement"></a>**Partition refinement** — The state-minimization algorithm that groups states by output and repeatedly splits groups whose members' next states fall in different groups, until nothing changes; the final groups are the equivalence classes. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [Equivalent states](#equivalent-states).

<a id="passive-element"></a>**Passive element** — An element that can never deliver net energy to the rest of a circuit, such as a resistor; sources, which can, are active. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="passive-sign-convention"></a>**Passive sign convention** — Referencing an element's current into the terminal marked +, so that p = vi is the power the element absorbs (negative means it delivers power); SPICE applies it to sources as well. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md). *See also:* [Electric power](#electric-power).

<a id="pci-express-pcie"></a>**PCI Express (PCIe)** — The serial, packet-based expansion interconnect of PCs and servers, built from lanes of differential pairs; each generation has roughly doubled the per-lane rate, from 2.5 GT/s in 1.0 to 128 GT/s in 7.0. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [Lane (serial link)](#lane-serial-link), [Compute Express Link (CXL)](#compute-express-link-cxl).

<a id="peak-inverse-voltage"></a>**Peak inverse voltage** — The largest reverse voltage a diode must block in a circuit, which sets its voltage rating; about twice the peak input in a half-wave peak rectifier or a center-tapped full-wave rectifier. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="peak-rectifier"></a>**Peak rectifier** — A rectifier followed by a reservoir capacitor that charges to the peak of the waveform and supplies the load between peaks. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="peak-time"></a>**Peak time** — The time t_p at which an underdamped step response reaches its first maximum; for the standard second-order system t_p = π/ω_d, half a damped period. *First defined in* [15-03](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-03-time-response.md). *See also:* [Overshoot](#overshoot), [Damped natural frequency](#damped-natural-frequency).

<a id="peak-to-average-power-ratio-papr"></a>**Peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR)** — Peak power over average power, the square of the crest factor; for noise-like signals such as OFDM it must be quoted at a stated CCDF probability and convention. Instruments use envelope power, in which a constant-envelope carrier is 0 dB and a complex Gaussian is 9.64 dB at 1e-4; for real waveforms a sinusoid is 3.01 dB. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md). *See also:* [Crest factor](#crest-factor), [CCDF](#ccdf).

<a id="pelgroms-law"></a>**Pelgrom's law** — The empirical rule that the random threshold difference between two closely spaced, identically drawn MOSFETs has a standard deviation A_VT/√(WL), falling with the square root of gate area; A_VT is a process constant. *First defined in* [10-08](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-08-current-sources-and-mirrors.md).

<a id="per-phase-equivalent"></a>**Per-phase equivalent** — The single-phase circuit (one source phase voltage, one line impedance, one Y-equivalent load impedance) that represents a balanced three-phase system; the other phases follow by ∓120° shifts. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="perfect-induction"></a>**Perfect induction** — Proving a Boolean identity by evaluating both sides on every row of the truth table; complete because each variable has only two values, but the 2^n rows make it impractical beyond a few dozen inputs. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="performance-power-area-ppa"></a>**Performance, power, area (PPA)** — The three primary metrics traded off in chip design, almost always considered together with cost and schedule. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="periodically-time-varying-system"></a>**Periodically time-varying system** — A system that commutes with delays equal to multiples of a period but not with other delays, such as a mixer, a sampler, a chopper or a decimator; such linear systems create frequency-shifted outputs. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md). *See also:* [Time-invariant system](#time-invariant-system), [Chopper stabilization](#chopper-stabilization).

<a id="petricks-method"></a>**Petrick's method** — An exact way to choose a minimum cover from a prime implicant chart, by writing for each minterm the sum of the primes covering it, multiplying the sums out and picking the cheapest product. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md).

<a id="phase"></a>**Phase** — The angle φ in A cos(ωt + φ), fixing where in its cycle a sinusoid is at t = 0. A time delay t_d is a phase lag of ωt_d. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="phase-line"></a>**Phase line** — A one-dimensional picture of an autonomous equation y' = f(y), marking the equilibria and arrows showing where y rises or falls between them. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Equilibrium solution](#equilibrium-solution).

<a id="phase-margin"></a>**Phase margin** — 180° plus the phase of the loop gain at the crossover frequency, where its magnitude is 1; the distance from oscillation. For a two-pole loop, 65.5° gives a maximally flat closed loop and about 52° a 1.25 dB peak with 16% overshoot. *First defined in* [07-07](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-07-frequency-response-and-bode-plots.md). *See also:* [Loop gain](#loop-gain), [Bode plot](#bode-plot).

<a id="phase-noise"></a>**Phase noise** — An oscillator's single-sideband noise power in a 1 Hz band at an offset from the carrier, relative to the carrier, in dBc/Hz; integrating 2 × 10^(L/10) over an offset band gives the mean-square phase, and dividing the rms phase by 2πf gives rms jitter. *First defined in* [15-12](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-12-control-applications-pll-regulators-thermal.md). *See also:* [Jitter](#jitter).

<a id="phase-portrait"></a>**Phase portrait** — The family of trajectories of a two-state system drawn in the state plane; for linear systems it is a node, saddle, spiral or center, set by the trace and determinant of A. *First defined in* [02-09](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-09-systems-of-odes-and-matrix-exponential.md).

<a id="phase-sequence"></a>**Phase sequence** — The order in which the three phase voltages reach their peaks; positive (abc) sequence has phase b lagging a by 120° and c lagging b by 120°. Reversing it reverses a three-phase motor. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="phase-velocity"></a>**Phase velocity** — The speed ω/β at which points of constant phase move; 1/√(µε) in a lossless medium, and frequency-dependent (dispersive) in conductors, waveguides and real dielectrics. *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Group velocity](#group-velocity).

<a id="phase-locked-loop-pll"></a>**Phase-locked loop (PLL)** — A feedback loop that locks an oscillator's phase to a reference, usually multiplying its frequency by a divider ratio N; in the linear phase-domain model the VCO is an integrator of phase, and with a charge pump and an RC loop filter the loop is type 2. *First defined in* [15-12](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-12-control-applications-pll-regulators-thermal.md). *See also:* [Voltage-controlled oscillator](#voltage-controlled-oscillator), [Charge pump (PLL)](#charge-pump-pll), [Jitter transfer](#jitter-transfer).

<a id="phased-array"></a>**Phased array** — A row or grid of antennas fed with progressive phase steps so their waves add in a chosen direction, sin θ = Δφ/(kd); steers beams electronically and needs spacing near λ/2 to avoid grating lobes. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="phasor"></a>**Phasor** — The complex number V = V_m∠φ representing the sinusoid V_m cos(ωt + φ) at a known frequency ω, so that v(t) = Re{V e^{jωt}}. This curriculum uses peak-amplitude, cosine-reference phasors. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Sinusoidal steady state](#sinusoidal-steady-state), [Impedance](#impedance).

<a id="phasor-diagram"></a>**Phasor diagram** — A drawing of a circuit's voltage and current phasors as arrows in the complex plane; KVL makes the voltage arrows around a loop close into a polygon. *First defined in* [07-05](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-05-sinusoidal-steady-state-and-impedance.md).

<a id="phonon"></a>**Phonon** — A quantum of lattice vibration; phonons carry heat, scatter electrons (raising a metal's resistance with temperature) and supply the crystal momentum for light absorption or emission in indirect-gap semiconductors. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="photoconductive-decay"></a>**Photoconductive decay** — A lifetime measurement that excites carriers with a light pulse and records the exponential decay of the excess conductivity; it reports an effective lifetime that includes surface recombination. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="photoelectric-effect"></a>**Photoelectric effect** — Ejection of electrons from a surface by light, which occurs only if each photon's energy exceeds the work function; the maximum kinetic energy hf − φ grows with frequency, not intensity. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="photon"></a>**Photon** — The quantum of light, a packet of energy E = hf = hc/λ (1239.84 eV·nm divided by the wavelength) and momentum h/λ; light is emitted and absorbed one photon at a time. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="photon-detection-efficiency"></a>**Photon detection efficiency** — The probability that a photon arriving at a single-photon detector produces a counted avalanche (PDE), including absorption, triggering probability and fill factor. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="physical-design"></a>**Physical design** — Converting synthesized logic into a manufacturable layout (floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing) and closing timing, power and design-rule signoff. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="pid-controller"></a>**PID controller** — A controller whose output is a weighted sum of the error, its integral and its derivative, u = K_p e + K_i ∫e dt + K_d de/dt, or in standard form K_p(1 + 1/(T_i s) + T_d s); in practice the derivative is filtered and actuator limits are handled with anti-windup. *First defined in* [15-08](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-08-pid-control.md). *See also:* [Integral action](#integral-action), [Integrator windup](#integrator-windup).

<a id="piecewise-linear-diode-model"></a>**Piecewise-linear diode model** — A diode model that is open when off and a voltage V_D0 in series with a resistance r_D when on, fitted to the exponential curve near the expected current. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="pierce-oscillator"></a>**Pierce oscillator** — The standard crystal-oscillator circuit, an inverting amplifier with the crystal from output to input and a capacitor from each end to ground; it presents the crystal with a load capacitance and a negative resistance -g_m/(omega^2 C1 C2) that must exceed the crystal's ESR by a safety factor. *First defined in* [12-09](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-09-oscillators.md). *See also:* [Negative resistance](#negative-resistance), [Barkhausen criterion](#barkhausen-criterion).

<a id="piezoelectric-polarization"></a>**Piezoelectric polarization** — Electric polarization created by mechanical strain in a piezoelectric crystal; in AlGaN grown on GaN it adds to the spontaneous polarization and increases the 2DEG density. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="pinch-off"></a>**Pinch-off** — The vanishing of a MOSFET's inversion charge at the drain end of the channel when V_DS reaches V_Dsat; beyond it, the extra drain voltage drops across a short depleted region that carriers cross at high field. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="pipeline-hazard"></a>**Pipeline hazard** — A situation in which the next instruction cannot execute in the following cycle without giving a wrong result — a data, control or structural hazard — resolved by forwarding, stalling or flushing (distinct from a logic hazard, a glitch). *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Data hazard](#data-hazard), [Control hazard](#control-hazard), [Structural hazard](#structural-hazard).

<a id="pipeline-register"></a>**Pipeline register** — The register between two pipeline stages that holds an instruction's data and control signals from one clock edge to the next; its clock-to-Q and setup time are the pipeline's per-stage overhead. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Pipelining](#pipelining).

<a id="pipelined-fft"></a>**Pipelined FFT** — A streaming FFT architecture with one butterfly per stage and delay lines between stages, taking one sample per clock; the radix-2 single-path delay-feedback (R2SDF) form uses log₂N butterflies, log₂N − 2 general multipliers and N − 1 words of delay. *First defined in* [16-04](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-04-the-fft.md). *See also:* [Fast Fourier transform (FFT)](#fast-fourier-transform-fft).

<a id="pipelining"></a>**Pipelining** — Inserting registers to split long combinational paths into stages, raising the clock rate and throughput at the cost of latency and register overhead. *First defined in* [08-10](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-10-timing-metastability-cdc.md).

<a id="pivot"></a>**Pivot** — The diagonal entry used to eliminate the entries below it at each step of Gaussian elimination; it must be nonzero, and should not be small relative to the entries below it. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="placement"></a>**Placement** — The implementation step that assigns every primitive of a synthesized netlist to a physical site on the chip, keeping connected and timing-critical cells close; often randomized, so results depend on a seed. *First defined in* [08-12](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-12-fpga-implementation-flow.md). *See also:* [Routing](#routing).

<a id="planar-circuit"></a>**Planar circuit** — A circuit that can be drawn on a plane with no crossing branches; only planar circuits have meshes. By Kuratowski's theorem a circuit is planar unless it contains a subdivision of K5 or K3,3. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Mesh](#mesh), [Loop analysis](#loop-analysis).

<a id="plant"></a>**Plant** — In control engineering, the system being controlled (a motor, a heater, a converter, a chip's thermal path), described by a model of how its outputs respond to its inputs. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md). *See also:* [State-space model](#state-space-model).

<a id="pn-junction"></a>**PN junction** — The boundary between p-type and n-type regions of one crystal, where carrier diffusion leaves a depleted layer of fixed ions, an internal field and a built-in potential; the basis of diodes, bipolar transistors and the source and drain of MOSFETs. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md). *See also:* [Depletion region](#depletion-region), [Built-in potential](#built-in-potential).

<a id="pointer"></a>**Pointer** — A variable holding a memory address, with a type saying what is stored there (int \*p points to an int); &x gives an address and \*p the object at it. Pointers let functions modify caller data and pass buffers without copying. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md). *See also:* [Dereference](#dereference), [Null pointer](#null-pointer), [Pointer arithmetic](#pointer-arithmetic).

<a id="pointer-arithmetic"></a>**Pointer arithmetic** — Adding an integer to a pointer advances it by whole elements (sizeof the pointed-to type), so a[i] is \*(a + i); subtracting two pointers into one array gives the number of elements between them. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="poisson-distribution"></a>**Poisson distribution** — The count of rare independent events with mean λ: P(k) = e^(−λ) λ^k/k!, the limit of the binomial as n grows with np = λ fixed. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="poisson-process"></a>**Poisson process** — Events occurring independently at a constant average rate; counts in an interval are Poisson and the gaps between events are exponential. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="poissons-equation"></a>**Poisson's equation** — The relation d²V/dx² = −ρ/ε between electrostatic potential and charge density (or dE/dx = ρ/ε); solved across junctions and MOS structures to find fields and potentials. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="polar-form"></a>**Polar form** — Writing a complex number by its magnitude and angle, z = r∠θ = r(cos θ + j sin θ) = re^{jθ}. Convenient for multiplication, division, powers and roots. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Rectangular form](#rectangular-form), [Euler's formula](#eulers-formula).

<a id="polarization-dielectric"></a>**Polarization (dielectric)** — The dipole moment per unit volume P (C/m²) induced in a dielectric by electronic, ionic or orientational response; at the dielectric's faces it appears as bound surface charge σ_b = P. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="polarization-light"></a>**Polarization (light)** — The direction in which a transverse wave's electric field oscillates; a polarizer transmits I₀ cos²θ (Malus's law), and reflection at Brewster's angle tan θ_B = n₂/n₁ removes one polarization. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="pole-placement"></a>**Pole placement** — Choosing a state-feedback gain K so that the closed-loop matrix A − BK has prescribed eigenvalues; possible for any eigenvalues when (A, B) is controllable, for example with Ackermann's formula. *First defined in* [15-10](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-10-state-space-introduction.md). *See also:* [Controllability](#controllability).

<a id="pole-splitting"></a>**Pole splitting** — The separation of a two-stage amplifier's two poles by a capacitor bridging the inverting second stage: Miller multiplication pushes the lower pole down to about 1/(g_m2R_1R_2C_c), and the capacitor's shorting of the second stage at high frequency pushes the upper pole up to about g_m2/(C_1 + C_2). *First defined in* [12-04](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-04-high-frequency-analysis-methods.md). *See also:* [Miller effect](#miller-effect), [Right-half-plane zero](#right-half-plane-zero).

<a id="poles-and-zeros"></a>**Poles and zeros** — The roots of a rational transfer function's denominator (poles) and numerator (zeros). Each pole p gives a natural mode e^(pt), so all poles in the left half-plane means stable; zeros set how much of each mode appears. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Transfer function](#transfer-function), [Characteristic equation](#characteristic-equation).

<a id="pole-zero-cancellation"></a>**Pole–zero cancellation** — A zero that coincides with a pole, removing that mode from one transfer function; the mode still exists inside the system, so cancelling an unstable pole leaves a hidden instability that disturbances or initial conditions excite. *First defined in* [15-02](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-02-transfer-functions-and-block-diagrams.md). *See also:* [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros).

<a id="pole-zero-doublet"></a>**Pole–zero doublet** — A pole and a zero very close together; nearly invisible in the frequency response, it leaves a slow settling tail of amplitude about (z − p)/z decaying with the time constant 1/p, which dominates precision settling. *First defined in* [15-03](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-03-time-response.md). *See also:* [Settling time](#settling-time).

<a id="polling"></a>**Polling** — Checking a device's status register repeatedly in software to learn whether it needs service; simple and fast to respond, but every unproductive check wastes CPU time. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [Interrupt](#interrupt).

<a id="poly-gate-depletion"></a>**Poly-gate depletion** — The depletion of a thin layer of a polysilicon gate at its oxide interface in inversion, W_dpoly = ε_ox E_ox/(qN_poly), which adds W_dpoly/3 to the electrical oxide thickness; eliminated by metal gates. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="polysilicon-emitter"></a>**Polysilicon emitter** — A bipolar emitter made of a thick heavily doped polysilicon layer over a shallow single-crystal emitter, which raises the effective emitter Gummel number and current gain and avoids defects from deep emitter implants. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="population-inversion"></a>**Population inversion** — A state in which more electrons occupy the upper energy states than the lower ones, so stimulated emission outweighs absorption and light is amplified; in a diode it needs E_Fn − E_Fp > E_g. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="positive-definite-matrix"></a>**Positive definite matrix** — A symmetric matrix with xᵀAx > 0 for every nonzero x; equivalently all eigenvalues positive, or all pivots positive. Grounded conductance matrices, nonsingular covariance matrices and Hessians at strict minima are examples. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="positive-real-function"></a>**Positive-real function** — A function Z(s) that is real for real s and has Re Z ≥ 0 whenever Re s ≥ 0; exactly the driving-point impedances realizable from passive R, L, C (and transformers), as shown by Brune (1931). *First defined in* [07-04](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-04-laplace-domain-circuit-analysis.md).

<a id="potential-energy"></a>**Potential energy** — Energy stored by position against a conservative force, with F = −dU/dx; mgh for gravity near the Earth and ½k_s x² for a spring. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="power-delivery-network"></a>**Power delivery network** — The regulators, board and package wiring, and decoupling capacitors that carry current from the supply to the transistors; its inductance and the die's capacitance form a resonant tank that causes supply droop on load steps. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="power-factor"></a>**Power factor** — Real power divided by apparent power; cos φ for sinusoids with phase difference φ, and lower still when the current is distorted. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="power-law"></a>**Power law** — A relation y = kxⁿ; doubling x multiplies y by 2ⁿ, and on log-log axes it is a straight line with slope n. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md). *See also:* [Log-log plot](#log-log-plot).

<a id="power-over-ethernet-poe"></a>**Power over Ethernet (PoE)** — Delivering DC power over Ethernet cabling (IEEE 802.3af, at and bt) at up to 57 V; the device receives the source's class power minus the cable's I²R loss (90 W at the source gives 71.3 W at the device for Type 4). *First defined in* [06-08](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-08-thevenin-and-norton.md). *See also:* [Thevenin equivalent](#thevenin-equivalent).

<a id="power-rating"></a>**Power rating** — The power a component can dissipate continuously at a stated ambient temperature, derated above it; designers usually run parts well below it. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="power-rule"></a>**Power rule** — d/dx xⁿ = n xⁿ⁻¹, valid for every real exponent n (for x > 0). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="power-series"></a>**Power series** — Σ c_k (x − a)^k; it converges inside a radius of convergence, where it can be differentiated and integrated term by term. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="power-signal"></a>**Power signal** — A signal with finite, nonzero average power P = lim (1/2T)∫|x|² dt over [−T, T], and hence infinite energy; periodic signals are power signals, with P equal to the average over one period. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Energy signal](#energy-signal), [RMS value](#rms-value).

<a id="power-spectral-density"></a>**Power spectral density** — The distribution of a stationary process's average power over frequency, in power per hertz; the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation. Circuit noise densities are usually one-sided. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="power-wall"></a>**Power wall** — The limit on clock frequency set by power density and cooling once supply voltages stopped scaling; processors reached it around 2004 and turned to multicore designs. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="power-factor-correction"></a>**Power-factor correction** — Raising a load's power factor, by parallel capacitors that supply the lagging reactive current locally (C = P(tan θ₁ − tan θ₂)/(ωV_rms²)), or, for distorted currents, by an active converter stage that draws sinusoidal current. *First defined in* [07-06](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-06-ac-power-and-power-factor.md). *See also:* [Power factor](#power-factor).

<a id="power-supply-rejection-ratio-psrr"></a>**Power-supply rejection ratio (PSRR)** — The ratio of a change in supply voltage to the input-referred offset change it causes, in dB or µV/V; it falls with frequency, so supply ripple leaks through more at high frequency. *First defined in* [10-09](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-09-real-op-amps-nonidealities.md).

<a id="poynting-vector"></a>**Poynting vector** — S = E × B/µ₀ (W/m²), the power flow per unit area in an electromagnetic field; it shows energy entering resistors and capacitors through the surrounding fields, and gives a plane wave's intensity E₀²/(2η₀). *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="ppk"></a>**Ppk** — The process performance index, Cpk's formula with the overall standard deviation of all the data (including drift and lot-to-lot shifts) instead of the within-subgroup σ; equal to Cpk only for a process in statistical control. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="precise-exception"></a>**Precise exception** — An exception taken so that the architectural state is exactly as if every instruction before the faulting one had completed and none after it had started, which lets the operating system handle it and resume the program. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [Reorder buffer (ROB)](#reorder-buffer-rob).

<a id="precision-rectifier"></a>**Precision rectifier** — A rectifier with its diode inside an op-amp's feedback loop, so the diode's forward drop is divided by the loop gain; its accuracy at high frequency is limited by the op-amp's slew through about two diode drops at each zero crossing. *First defined in* [10-10](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-10-op-amp-application-circuits.md).

<a id="precursor-tap"></a>**Precursor tap** — An equalizer tap that weights a sample received after the one being decided, cancelling energy that the channel delivers before the main pulse; needed because channels are generally not minimum phase, so their stable inverse is partly anticausal. *First defined in* [16-02](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-02-dtft-and-z-transform-for-dsp.md). *See also:* [Feed-forward equalizer (FFE)](#feed-forward-equalizer-ffe), [Minimum-phase system](#minimum-phase-system).

<a id="prefetching"></a>**Prefetching** — Fetching blocks into a cache before they are requested, by hardware that predicts the access pattern (next-line, stride) or by software hints; judged by coverage, accuracy and timeliness. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Memory-level parallelism (MLP)](#memory-level-parallelism-mlp).

<a id="preprocessor"></a>**Preprocessor** — The first stage of a C build, which rewrites source text according to lines starting with *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="prime-implicant"></a>**Prime implicant** — An implicant that cannot be enlarged by removing a literal without covering a 0 of the function; some minimal sum of products always consists of prime implicants only. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md). *See also:* [Essential prime implicant](#essential-prime-implicant), [Implicant](#implicant).

<a id="primitive-polynomial"></a>**Primitive polynomial** — An irreducible polynomial of degree n over GF(2) whose root generates all 2^n - 1 nonzero field elements; used as an LFSR's feedback, it gives maximal length. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Linear-feedback shift register (LFSR)](#linear-feedback-shift-register-lfsr).

<a id="principal-component-analysis"></a>**Principal component analysis** — Finding the eigenvectors of a data set's covariance matrix (equivalently the singular vectors of the centered data), ordered by the variance they carry, to describe or compress the data with a few uncorrelated components. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="priority-encoder"></a>**Priority encoder** — A block that outputs the number of the highest-priority active input, plus a valid flag that is 0 when no input is active; used for interrupt arbitration and leading-one detection. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="privilege-mode"></a>**Privilege mode** — The level of authority at which code runs (RISC-V machine, supervisor and user modes), determining which instructions, registers and pages it may use. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Trap (processor)](#trap-processor).

<a id="probability-density-function"></a>**Probability density function** — A non-negative function f(x) with total area 1, whose area over an interval is the probability of landing in it; the density itself is not a probability and can exceed 1. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="probability-mass-function-pmf"></a>**Probability mass function (PMF)** — For a discrete random variable, p_X(k) = P(X = k); the values are non-negative and sum to 1. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="process-capability-cp-cpk"></a>**Process capability (Cp, Cpk)** — Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ) compares the specification window with the process spread; Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/(3σ) also charges for an off-center mean. Automotive defaults (AIAG, 1995 manuals): Cpk ≥ 1.33 for stable ongoing production; preliminary studies and significant characteristics are judged on Ppk, expecting ≥ 1.67. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="process-design-kit-pdk"></a>**Process design kit (PDK)** — The files a foundry gives designers to use its process, including device models, design rules, layer definitions and often standard-cell libraries, abstracting the fab's recipes. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="processing-element-pe"></a>**Processing element (PE)** — One cell of an accelerator array, typically a multiply-accumulate unit with a few registers, connected to its neighbours. *First defined in* [14-14](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-14-ai-accelerators.md). *See also:* [Systolic array](#systolic-array), [Multiply-accumulate (MAC)](#multiply-accumulate-mac).

<a id="product-of-sums-pos"></a>**Product of sums (POS)** — An AND of OR terms; the canonical POS ANDs the maxterms of the rows where the function is 0, and it maps onto two-level OR-AND or NOR-NOR logic. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="product-rule"></a>**Product rule** — (fg)' = f'g + fg'; the derivative of a product has one term for each factor's change. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="program-counter-pc"></a>**Program counter (PC)** — The register holding the address of the instruction being executed; it advances by 4 or is loaded with a branch or jump target each instruction. *First defined in* [14-05](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-05-single-cycle-datapath.md).

<a id="programmable-logic-array-pla"></a>**Programmable logic array (PLA)** — A two-level logic structure with a programmable AND plane forming product terms and a programmable OR plane summing them into outputs; its size grows with the number of products rather than with 2^n. *First defined in* [08-11](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-11-memories-and-programmable-logic.md).

<a id="projection"></a>**Projection** — The closest point to b on the line through a, p = (a·b / a·a) a, characterized by the error b − p being perpendicular to a; the basis of least squares. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="proof-mass"></a>**Proof mass** — The suspended mass in an accelerometer or gyroscope whose displacement relative to its package measures acceleration (deflection a/ω₀² below resonance) or rotation. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="propagation-constant"></a>**Propagation constant** — γ = α + jβ, with a wave varying as e^(−γz); α (Np/m) is the attenuation and β (rad/m) the phase constant. For a plane wave γ = √(jωµ(σ + jωε)); for a transmission line γ = √((R + jωL)(G + jωC)). *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Neper](#neper).

<a id="propagation-delay"></a>**Propagation delay** — The time from an input transition to the output crossing 50 % of its swing; for an RC model, τ·ln 2 ≈ 0.69τ. In digital timing, t_pd is the longest such delay from any input change until the output is final, and the delays along a path add (08-04). *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Contamination delay](#contamination-delay), [Critical path](#critical-path).

<a id="pseudo-instruction"></a>**Pseudo-instruction** — An assembler mnemonic that expands into one or more real instructions, such as li, mv, j, ret and call in RISC-V. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="pseudo-random-bit-sequence-prbs"></a>**Pseudo-random bit sequence (PRBS)** — A deterministic, periodic bit stream with noise-like statistics, normally the output of a maximal-length LFSR, used as a standard test pattern for links (PRBS7, PRBS15, PRBS23, PRBS31). *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Linear-feedback shift register (LFSR)](#linear-feedback-shift-register-lfsr), [Scrambler](#scrambler).

<a id="ptat-voltage"></a>**PTAT voltage** — A voltage proportional to absolute temperature, such as the difference (kT/q) ln(I_1/I_2) between two diodes or transistors at different current densities; the basis of on-chip temperature sensors and bandgap references. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="pull-up-and-pull-down-networks"></a>**Pull-up and pull-down networks** — The pMOS switch network connecting a CMOS gate's output to the supply and the nMOS network connecting it to ground; series connections in one are parallel in the other, the circuit form of De Morgan's theorem. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="pwm-dac"></a>**PWM DAC** — A digital-to-analog converter made from a pulse-width-modulated output and a low-pass filter; the filter keeps the average A·D and attenuates the switching harmonics, leaving a ripple set by the PWM frequency and filter order. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md). *See also:* [Duty cycle](#duty-cycle).

<a id="letter-q"></a>

## Q

<a id="q-format"></a>**Q format** — Notation Qm.f for fixed-point numbers with m integer and f fractional bits; Q15 is a 16-bit signed fraction in [−1, 1 − 2^−15] with resolution 3.05×10^−5. *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="q-function"></a>**Q-function** — Q(x), the probability that a standard normal random variable exceeds x; it gives error probabilities for decisions in Gaussian noise and falls off extremely fast (Q(6) ≈ 1e-9). *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="quadratic-convergence"></a>**Quadratic convergence** — Convergence in which each error is proportional to the square of the previous one, so the number of correct digits roughly doubles per step. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="quality-factor"></a>**Quality factor** — Q = 1/(2ζ) = ω₀ × energy stored / power dissipated; the amplitude decays by a factor e in Q/π cycles, and Q also sets the sharpness of resonance. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Damping ratio](#damping-ratio).

<a id="quantization-neural-networks"></a>**Quantization (neural networks)** — Representing a model's weights or activations in a narrow format (INT8, FP8, FP4) with scale factors, x ≈ s(q − z), to cut memory, bandwidth and arithmetic cost at some loss of accuracy. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md). *See also:* [Block floating point](#block-floating-point), [Requantization](#requantization).

<a id="quantization-noise"></a>**Quantization noise** — The rounding error of an ADC, modeled as uniform over ±½ LSB, with RMS Δ/√12 ≈ 0.29 LSB; it sets the ideal SNR of 6.02N + 1.76 dB. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="quantum-confinement"></a>**Quantum confinement** — The rise and spreading of energy levels when a particle is squeezed into a region comparable to its de Broglie wavelength, E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) for an infinite well; it tunes quantum-well lasers and quantum-dot colors. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="quantum-efficiency"></a>**Quantum efficiency** — The number of electrons collected per incident photon (or, for an emitter, photons out per injected electron), combining reflection, absorption and collection or extraction losses. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="quantum-tunneling"></a>**Quantum tunneling** — Passage of a particle through a barrier higher than its energy, with probability falling roughly as e^(−2κd), κ = √(2m(V₀ − E))/ħ; it causes gate-oxide leakage and enables flash memory, STM and tunnel diodes. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="quarter-wave-transformer"></a>**Quarter-wave transformer** — A layer (or transmission-line section) a quarter wavelength thick whose impedance is the geometric mean of those on either side, √(η₁η₃); it cancels reflection at its design frequency, as in antireflection coatings. *First defined in* [13-06](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-06-reflection-and-transmission.md). *See also:* [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="quasi-fermi-level"></a>**Quasi-Fermi level** — A separate Fermi level for electrons (E_Fn) or holes (E_Fp) when a semiconductor is out of equilibrium but each carrier population is in equilibrium with itself; np = n_i² e^((E_Fn − E_Fp)/kT), and each current flows down its own quasi-Fermi-level gradient. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="quasi-neutral-region"></a>**Quasi-neutral region** — The part of a doped region outside a depletion layer, where majority carriers balance the dopant charge and the field is small. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="quasi-static-approximation"></a>**Quasi-static approximation** — Treating time-varying fields as if static at each instant, valid when the structure is much smaller than a wavelength (a common rule is below λ/10); it is the assumption behind lumped circuit theory. *First defined in* [13-04](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-04-maxwells-equations.md). *See also:* [Maxwell's equations](#maxwells-equations).

<a id="qubit"></a>**Qubit** — A two-level quantum system in a superposition α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ with |α|² + |β|² = 1; measurement returns 0 or 1 with probabilities |α|² and |β|², and n qubits need 2ⁿ amplitudes to describe classically. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="queue"></a>**Queue** — A first-in-first-out collection with enqueue at the back and dequeue at the front, O(1) each; implemented with a ring buffer or a linked list. A priority queue instead removes the smallest key first. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).
