<a id="source-degeneration"></a>**Source degeneration** — A resistor R_S in a transistor's source (or R_E in a bipolar emitter) that feeds back a voltage opposing the input, cutting the gain to about −R_D/(R_S + 1/g_m) but making it set by resistors rather than by the device. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Transconductance](#transconductance).

<a id="source-follower"></a>**Source follower** — The common-drain MOSFET stage, with the input at the gate and the output at the source; a voltage buffer with gain g_mR_eq/(1 + g_mR_eq), below 1/(1 + χ) with the body effect, and output resistance about 1/(g_m + g_mb). *First defined in* [10-06](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-06-mos-single-stage-amplifiers.md). *See also:* [Buffer amplifier](#buffer-amplifier), [Body transconductance](#body-transconductance).

<a id="source-injection-velocity"></a>**Source injection velocity** — The x-directed thermal velocity v_thx (about 1.6 × 10⁷ cm/s for electrons in silicon MOSFETs) with which carriers enter the channel from the source; it sets the ceiling I_Dsat = W B v_thx C_ox (V_GS − V_TH), where B is the fraction not scattered back. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md). *See also:* [Ballistic transport](#ballistic-transport), [Velocity saturation](#velocity-saturation).

<a id="source-transformation"></a>**Source transformation** — Replacing a voltage source V_s in series with R by a current source V_s/R in parallel with R, or the reverse; the two are equivalent at their terminals but not internally. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Millman's theorem](#millmans-theorem).

<a id="spaced-repetition"></a>**Spaced repetition** — A review method, often implemented in flashcard software such as Anki, that schedules each item at expanding intervals just before it would be forgotten. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md).

<a id="spacing-effect"></a>**Spacing effect** — The finding that practice distributed over time produces more durable learning than the same practice massed together; the best gap grows with how long the material must be retained. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md). *See also:* [Spaced repetition](#spaced-repetition).

<a id="spanning-tree"></a>**Spanning tree** — A set of n − 1 branches that connects all n nodes of a circuit without forming a loop; each remaining branch (a link) closes one independent loop, giving b − n + 1 independent KVL equations. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="sparse-matrix"></a>**Sparse matrix** — A matrix whose entries are almost all zero, stored and factored by keeping only the nonzeros; circuit and power-grid matrices have a few nonzeros per row. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="spec-cpu"></a>**SPEC CPU** — The Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation's processor benchmark suites (SPECspeed and SPECrate, integer and floating point), scored as the geometric mean of reference-time ratios, with mandatory base and optional peak results; SPEC CPU 2026 replaced SPEC CPU 2017 in 2026. *First defined in* [14-15](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-15-roofline-and-benchmarks.md). *See also:* [Benchmark](#benchmark), [Geometric mean](#geometric-mean).

<a id="specific-absorption-rate-sar"></a>**Specific absorption rate (SAR)** — RF power absorbed per kilogram of tissue (W/kg); exposure limits include 1.6 W/kg averaged over 1 g (US FCC) and 2 W/kg over 10 g (ICNIRP), so limits must be compared with their averaging mass. *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="specific-contact-resistivity"></a>**Specific contact resistivity** — The resistance of a contact times its area, ρ_c in Ω·cm², which falls exponentially with √N and with barrier height; about 10⁻⁷ Ω·cm² for Hu's measured TiSi₂ contact, and much lower values are needed as contacts shrink. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="specific-on-resistance"></a>**Specific on-resistance** — A power device's on-resistance multiplied by its active area (Ω·cm²), the area-independent figure for comparing technologies; Baliga's limit for a drift layer is 4V_B²/(εμE_c³). *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="spectral-leakage"></a>**Spectral leakage** — The spreading of an off-bin tone's energy across all DFT bins, because a sinusoid that does not complete a whole number of cycles in the record is not orthogonal to any DFT basis vector; controlled with windows. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Scalloping loss](#scalloping-loss).

<a id="spectral-theorem"></a>**Spectral theorem** — Every real symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors, A = QΛQᵀ = Σ λᵢqᵢqᵢᵀ. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="spectre"></a>**Spectre** — A family of attacks, disclosed in January 2018, that use speculatively executed instructions to leave secret-dependent traces in caches and other microarchitectural state, read back by timing (CVE-2017-5753 and CVE-2017-5715). *First defined in* [14-07](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-07-branch-prediction-and-speculation.md). *See also:* [Side channel](#side-channel), [Speculative execution](#speculative-execution).

<a id="spectrum"></a>**Spectrum** — A signal's content as a function of frequency: lines at the harmonics for a periodic signal (Fourier series), a continuous function for an aperiodic one (Fourier transform). *First defined in* [11-06](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-06-continuous-time-fourier-transform.md).

<a id="speculative-execution"></a>**Speculative execution** — Executing instructions beyond an unresolved branch (or other prediction) before it is known that they should run, discarding their results without trace in architectural state if the prediction was wrong. *First defined in* [14-07](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-07-branch-prediction-and-speculation.md). *See also:* [Branch prediction](#branch-prediction), [Spectre](#spectre).

<a id="speedup"></a>**Speedup** — The ratio of old to new execution time for the same work; "30% faster" means a speedup of 1.3, so the new time is 77% of the old. *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md).

<a id="spice"></a>**SPICE** — Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis, the standard family of circuit simulators that solve a netlist's nodal equations for DC, AC and transient behavior; ngspice is an open-source version. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md). *See also:* [Netlist](#netlist), [Modified nodal analysis](#modified-nodal-analysis).

<a id="spin-lock"></a>**Spin lock** — A lock acquired by repeatedly attempting an atomic operation until it succeeds; spinning on ordinary reads first (test-and-test-and-set) avoids flooding the interconnect with coherence traffic. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Load-reserved/store-conditional (LR/SC)](#load-reserved-store-conditional-lr-sc).

<a id="spontaneous-polarization"></a>**Spontaneous polarization** — The built-in electric polarization of an unstrained polar crystal such as wurtzite GaN or AlN along its c-axis; its change at a heterojunction leaves a fixed bound sheet charge. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="spread-spectrum-clocking"></a>**Spread-spectrum clocking** — Varying a clock's frequency slightly over time so that each harmonic is smeared over a band, lowering the peak that narrow-band emissions measurements report; the total harmonic energy is unchanged. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md).

<a id="square-law"></a>**Square law** — The long-channel saturation current I_Dsat = (W/2mL)μC_ox(V_GS − V_TH)², with m = 1 in its simplest form; the first-order model of analog design and the basis of SPICE level 1. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="squeeze-theorem"></a>**Squeeze theorem** — If g(x) ≤ f(x) ≤ h(x) near a and g and h share the limit L, then f also tends to L. Used to prove sin θ/θ → 1. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="sr-latch"></a>**SR latch** — A bistable built from two cross-coupled NOR (or NAND) gates with set and reset inputs; it holds when both are inactive, and both active at once is forbidden because it forces equal outputs and an unpredictable release. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md).

<a id="stability-of-a-circuit"></a>**Stability (of a circuit)** — The property that every bounded input gives a bounded output; for a linear circuit, every pole of its transfer functions lies in the open left half-plane. Passive RLC circuits cannot be unstable; circuits with gain can. *First defined in* [07-04](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-04-laplace-domain-circuit-analysis.md).

<a id="stability-triangle"></a>**Stability triangle** — The region |a₂| < 1, |a₁| < 1 + a₂ of the coefficient plane in which a second-order denominator 1 + a₁z^{−1} + a₂z^{−2} has both poles inside the unit circle; poles are complex above the parabola a₁² = 4a₂. *First defined in* [11-09](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-09-z-transform.md). *See also:* [Biquad](#biquad).

<a id="stack-data-structure"></a>**Stack (data structure)** — A last-in-first-out collection with push and pop at one end, O(1) each; used for function calls, undo histories, expression evaluation and bracket matching. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="stack-memory"></a>**Stack (memory)** — The region holding local variables and function call frames, allocated on function entry and released on return; fast but small (megabytes on desktops, kilobytes on MCUs), and a pointer to a returned function's local dangles. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="stack-frame"></a>**Stack frame** — The block of stack memory a function reserves on entry, by moving the stack pointer down, for its saved registers, return address and local data; RISC-V frames are multiples of 16 bytes. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="stall"></a>**Stall** — Holding an instruction (and those behind it) in its pipeline stage for a cycle while a bubble moves ahead, to wait out a hazard. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Bubble](#bubble).

<a id="stamp"></a>**Stamp** — The fixed pattern of matrix entries one circuit element contributes to the nodal or MNA equations; a resistor of conductance g between nodes a and b adds +g at (a, a) and (b, b) and −g at (a, b) and (b, a). *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="standard-deviation"></a>**Standard deviation** — The square root of the variance, σ, in the units of the random variable; for a signal it is the AC RMS value. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="standard-error"></a>**Standard error** — The standard deviation of an estimate; for the mean of n independent samples, σ/√n. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="standing-wave"></a>**Standing wave** — The sum of equal waves travelling in opposite directions, 2A cos(kx) cos(ωt), with fixed nodes half a wavelength apart; confined between reflectors it sets resonant modes such as f_n = nv/(2L). *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="star-ground"></a>**Star ground** — A grounding layout in which each circuit has its own return conductor to a single common point at the supply, so that no return impedance is shared between noisy and sensitive circuits. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Common-impedance coupling](#common-impedance-coupling).

<a id="state-assignment"></a>**State assignment** — The choice of binary code for each state of an FSM (binary, Gray-ordered, one-hot, output-encoded), which sets the number of flip-flops and strongly affects the size and speed of the next-state logic. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [One-hot encoding](#one-hot-encoding).

<a id="state-diagram"></a>**State diagram** — A drawing of an FSM with states as circles and transitions as arrows labeled with the input condition (and, for a Mealy machine, the output). *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [State table](#state-table).

<a id="state-equations"></a>**State equations** — A circuit's first-order differential equations written for its state variables (capacitor voltages and inductor currents), ẋ = Ax + g·u; the eigenvalues of the state matrix A are the circuit's natural frequencies. *First defined in* [07-03](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-03-second-order-rlc-transients.md). *See also:* [State variable](#state-variable).

<a id="state-observer"></a>**State observer** — A model of the plant run in parallel with it and corrected by the output error, x̂' = A x̂ + B u + L(y − C x̂); its estimation error decays with the eigenvalues of A − LC, which L places when (A, C) is observable. Also called a Luenberger observer. *First defined in* [15-10](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-10-state-space-introduction.md). *See also:* [Observability](#observability), [Separation principle](#separation-principle).

<a id="state-table"></a>**State table** — A table listing, for each present state and input value, the next state and the output of an FSM; the starting point for deriving its logic. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [State diagram](#state-diagram), [State assignment](#state-assignment).

<a id="state-variable"></a>**State variable** — A variable that fully captures a circuit's stored energy and memory, namely capacitor voltages and inductor currents. Knowing them at one instant (plus the inputs) determines the future response. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="state-space-model"></a>**State-space model** — The description x' = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du of a linear system, with state vector x (for circuits, capacitor voltages and inductor currents); the eigenvalues of A are the system's poles. *First defined in* [02-09](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-09-systems-of-odes-and-matrix-exponential.md). *See also:* [State variable](#state-variable), [Matrix exponential](#matrix-exponential), [Transfer function](#transfer-function).

<a id="static-cmos"></a>**Static CMOS** — The standard logic style in which each gate has a pMOS pull-up network and a dual nMOS pull-down network, exactly one conducting for every input, so the output is always driven to a rail and no current flows once it settles. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md). *See also:* [Pull-up and pull-down networks](#pull-up-and-pull-down-networks).

<a id="static-discipline"></a>**Static discipline** — The rule defining valid digital levels with separate output (V_OL, V_OH) and input (V_IL, V_IH) thresholds, so that every gate restores clean levels and leaves noise margins. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Noise margin](#noise-margin).

<a id="static-error-constants"></a>**Static error constants** — K_p = lim L(s), K_v = lim sL(s) and K_a = lim s²L(s) as s → 0; a stable unity-feedback loop's steady errors to a unit step, ramp and parabola are 1/(1 + K_p), 1/K_v and 1/K_a. *First defined in* [15-04](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-04-feedback-and-steady-state-error.md). *See also:* [System type](#system-type), [Steady-state error](#steady-state-error).

<a id="static-power"></a>**Static power** — The power a circuit draws when it is not switching, V_DD times the total leakage current; it dominates idle and standby energy. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="static-timing-analysis-sta"></a>**Static timing analysis (STA)** — Checking every timing path of a synchronous design against setup and hold constraints by propagating worst-case and best-case arrival times through the circuit graph, without simulating input vectors. *First defined in* [08-10](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-10-timing-metastability-cdc.md). *See also:* [Critical path](#critical-path), [Slack](#slack).

<a id="statistical-independence"></a>**Statistical independence** — Events A and B are independent if P(A ∩ B) = P(A) P(B), so learning one tells nothing about the other; several events are independent only if every subcollection satisfies the product rule. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="statistical-power"></a>**Statistical power** — The probability that a test rejects the null hypothesis when a specified alternative is true, 1 − β; it grows with sample size and effect size. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="statistical-process-control-spc"></a>**Statistical process control (SPC)** — Monitoring a process with control charts, plots of subgroup statistics against limits (typically ±3 standard errors around the grand mean), to detect drift or shifts; a process whose points stay inside the limits is "in statistical control". *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="status-flags"></a>**Status flags** — The Z (zero), N (negative, the result's sign bit), C (carry out) and V (signed overflow) bits produced by an ALU; unsigned A < B is a borrow (C = 0 after A − B) and signed A < B is N XOR V. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="steady-state-error"></a>**Steady-state error** — The error r − y that remains after the transient of a stable loop has died out, found with the final-value theorem as lim sE(s); it depends on the input class, the system type and where disturbances enter. *First defined in* [15-04](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-04-feedback-and-steady-state-error.md). *See also:* [Final-value theorem](#final-value-theorem).

<a id="steady-state-response"></a>**Steady-state response** — The part of a stable linear system's response that remains after the transient decays, set by the input alone; for a sinusoidal input it is the phasor answer. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Transient](#transient).

<a id="steep-slope-transistor"></a>**Steep-slope transistor** — A proposed switch, such as a tunneling FET or negative-capacitance FET, designed to turn on more sharply than the 59.5 mV/decade Boltzmann limit at 300 K by changing how carriers are injected; not yet a mainstream logic technology. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="step-junction"></a>**Step junction** — A PN junction whose doping changes abruptly from N_A to N_D, with depletion width W = √(2ε(V_bi − V_A)(1/N_A + 1/N_D)/q). *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md). *See also:* [One-sided junction](#one-sided-junction), [Linearly graded junction](#linearly-graded-junction).

<a id="step-response"></a>**Step response** — The response of a circuit to a source that switches from one constant value to another; for a first-order circuit, an exponential approach to the new final value. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="stepping"></a>**Stepping** — A silicon revision of a chip (e.g., A0, A1, B0); commonly the number changes for metal-only revisions and the letter for full-layer revisions, though conventions vary. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="stiff-system"></a>**Stiff system** — A system of differential equations whose time constants span many orders of magnitude, so explicit methods need steps set by the fastest one; circuit simulators therefore use implicit methods. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Euler's method](#eulers-method).

<a id="stokes-theorem"></a>**Stokes' theorem** — The circulation of a field around a closed loop equals the flux of its curl through any surface bounded by the loop; Green's theorem is its flat, two-dimensional case. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Curl](#curl).

<a id="storage-time"></a>**Storage time** — The duration of the storage phase of reverse recovery, until the excess density at the junction edge reaches zero; exactly τ_p times the solution of erf√(t_s/τ_p) = I_F/(I_F + I_R) for a long diode, shorter than the charge-control estimate τ_p ln(1 + I_F/I_R). *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="store-buffer"></a>**Store buffer** — A queue that holds a core's retired stores until they are written to the cache, letting the core continue; its contents are visible to the core's own loads but not yet to other cores. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Total store ordering (TSO)](#total-store-ordering-tso).

<a id="strained-silicon"></a>**Strained silicon** — Silicon whose lattice is deliberately stretched or compressed, by a SiGe substrate or by local stressors, to reshape its bands and raise carrier mobility; introduced into production logic processes at the 90 nm generation. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md).

<a id="streaming-multiprocessor-sm"></a>**Streaming multiprocessor (SM)** — The repeated core of an NVIDIA GPU, containing warp schedulers, arithmetic lanes, tensor cores, a large register file and shared memory; H100 has 132. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [Graphics processing unit (GPU)](#graphics-processing-unit-gpu), [Occupancy](#occupancy).

<a id="struct-padding"></a>**Struct padding** — Unused bytes a compiler inserts between and after struct fields so that each field is aligned to its size; field order changes a struct's size (uint8, uint32, uint16 is 12 bytes; uint32, uint16, uint8 is 8). *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="structural-hazard"></a>**Structural hazard** — A pipeline hazard in which two instructions need the same hardware resource (a memory port, a register-file port, an unpipelined unit) in the same cycle. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md).

<a id="structure-padding"></a>**Structure padding** — Unused bytes a compiler inserts between or after structure members so that each member sits at a multiple of its alignment; member order changes how much padding is needed. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="structured-sparsity"></a>**Structured sparsity** — A pruning pattern (such as 2:4, two zeros in every four weights) that tensor cores can exploit to skip zeros, doubling peak throughput; vendors' headline figures often assume it. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [Tensor core](#tensor-core).

<a id="stub"></a>**Stub** — A short- or open-circuited length of transmission line used as a reactance, jZ₀ tan βℓ or −jZ₀ cot βℓ; short stubs act as inductors or capacitors at microwave frequencies where lumped parts misbehave. *First defined in* [13-08](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-08-transmission-lines-sinusoidal-steady-state.md). *See also:* [Input impedance](#input-impedance).

<a id="student-t-distribution"></a>**Student t distribution** — The distribution of (X̄ − μ)/(S/√n) for Gaussian data, with n − 1 degrees of freedom; heavier-tailed than the Gaussian, so small-sample intervals use larger multipliers (2.776 for ν = 4 at 95%). *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="subspace"></a>**Subspace** — A subset of a vector space that contains 0 and is closed under addition and scalar multiplication, such as a line or plane through the origin, a column space or a null space. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="substitution-integration"></a>**Substitution (integration)** — Evaluating ∫ f(g(x)) g'(x) dx as ∫ f(u) du with u = g(x), the chain rule in reverse; for definite integrals the limits change to g(a) and g(b). *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="subthreshold-conduction"></a>**Subthreshold conduction** — MOSFET current below threshold, carried by diffusion in a weak inversion layer and rising exponentially with gate voltage, I_D ∝ e^((V_GS − V_TH)/mV_T); it sets off-state leakage. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="subthreshold-swing"></a>**Subthreshold swing** — The gate-voltage change per decade of subthreshold current, S = mV_T ln 10, which cannot fall below 59.5 mV/decade at 300 K for a conventional transistor. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="sum-of-products-sop"></a>**Sum of products (SOP)** — An OR of AND terms; the canonical SOP ORs the minterms of the rows where the function is 1, and it maps onto two-level AND-OR or NAND-NAND logic. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="superheterodyne-receiver"></a>**Superheterodyne receiver** — A receiver that mixes the wanted signal with a tunable local oscillator to a fixed intermediate frequency (IF), where a fixed, sharp filter selects it; it must reject the image frequency before the mixer. *First defined in* [11-11](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-11-modulation-and-filtering-applications.md). *See also:* [Mixer](#mixer), [Image frequency](#image-frequency).

<a id="supermesh"></a>**Supermesh** — The loop around two meshes that share a current source, avoiding the source's branch; KVL around it does not involve the source's unknown voltage, and the source supplies the constraint i_a − i_b = ±I_s. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Supernode](#supernode), [Mesh analysis](#mesh-analysis).

<a id="supernode"></a>**Supernode** — A closed surface around a floating voltage source and its two nodes; KCL holds for the surface as a whole (the source's unknown current cancels), and the source supplies the constraint v_a − v_b = V_s. *First defined in* [06-04](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-04-nodal-analysis.md). *See also:* [Nodal analysis](#nodal-analysis).

<a id="superposition"></a>**Superposition** — In a linear circuit, any response to several independent sources equals the sum of the responses to each source acting alone, with the others switched off (voltage sources shorted, current sources opened) and dependent sources left in place. It does not apply to power. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Linearity](#linearity), [Dependent source](#dependent-source).

<a id="superposition-electrostatics"></a>**Superposition (electrostatics)** — The principle that the field (or force) of many charges is the vector sum of their individual fields; for continuous charge the sum becomes an integral. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="superscalar"></a>**Superscalar** — A processor that fetches, decodes, issues and retires more than one instruction per cycle; its width is the maximum per cycle. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [Out-of-order execution](#out-of-order-execution).

<a id="surface-charge-density"></a>**Surface charge density** — Charge per unit area, σ (C/m²); on a conductor it is largest where the surface curves most sharply, and the field just outside is σ/ε₀. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="surface-depletion"></a>**Surface depletion** — The MOS bias regime in which majority carriers are pushed from the surface, leaving ionized dopants to a depth W_dep that grows with gate voltage until threshold. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="surface-mobility"></a>**Surface mobility** — The carrier mobility in a MOSFET inversion layer, several times below bulk mobility because of surface-roughness and phonon scattering, and falling as the vertical field rises. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="surface-potential"></a>**Surface potential** — The band bending φ_s at a semiconductor surface relative to the bulk, positive when the bands bend down; it is zero at flat band and reaches about 2φ_B at threshold in a MOS structure. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="surface-recombination-velocity"></a>**Surface recombination velocity** — The parameter S (cm/s) that sets recombination at a surface through the boundary condition D dΔp/dx = SΔp; 10² to about 10⁵ cm/s for bare silicon surfaces, below 1 cm/s at a well-passivated oxide interface. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="surface-resistance"></a>**Surface resistance** — R_s = 1/(σδ) = √(πfµ/σ), the resistance per square of a conductor at high frequency (8.25 mΩ for copper at 1 GHz); the loss per area is ½R_s|H_t|², and it rises as √f. *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Skin depth](#skin-depth).

<a id="susceptance"></a>**Susceptance** — B, the imaginary part of an admittance (siemens); positive for a capacitor (ωC), negative for an inductor (−1/(ωL)). *First defined in* [07-05](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-05-sinusoidal-steady-state-and-impedance.md).

<a id="switching-threshold"></a>**Switching threshold** — The input voltage V_M at which a CMOS inverter's output equals its input; for square-law devices V_M = (V_TN√r + V_DD − |V_TP|)/(1 + √r) with r = k_n/k_p. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="symbolic-computation"></a>**Symbolic computation** — Manipulating formulas exactly, with symbols rather than numbers (SymPy solves, simplifies, differentiates and integrates); used to derive or check hand results and to keep exact rationals such as 470000/53. *First defined in* [05-03](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-03-scipy-sympy-matplotlib.md).

<a id="synchronizer"></a>**Synchronizer** — A chain of flip-flops (usually two or three) with nothing between them that samples an asynchronous signal and gives any metastability a clock period per stage to resolve; its reliability is quantified by MTBF = e^(S/tau)/(T_W F_C F_D). *First defined in* [08-10](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-10-timing-metastability-cdc.md). *See also:* [Metastability](#metastability), [Mean time between failures (MTBF)](#mean-time-between-failures-mtbf).

<a id="synchronous-counter"></a>**Synchronous counter** — A counter whose flip-flops all share one clock, each bit toggling when the bits below it say so (all 1s when counting up), so every output changes at the same edge. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Ripple counter](#ripple-counter), [Modulo-N counter](#modulo-n-counter).

<a id="synchronous-design"></a>**Synchronous design** — A discipline in which all state is held in flip-flops clocked by a common clock, every feedback loop contains a register and asynchronous inputs are synchronized, so correctness reduces to setup and hold checks on each register-to-register path. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md).

<a id="synchronous-reset"></a>**Synchronous reset** — A reset that is sampled like data and takes effect at the next active clock edge; simple to time but requires a running clock. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md). *See also:* [Asynchronous reset](#asynchronous-reset).

<a id="synthesizable-subset"></a>**Synthesizable subset** — The part of an HDL that synthesis tools turn into hardware (continuous assignments, combinational and clocked always blocks, case, constant-bound loops, parameters); delays, system tasks, file I/O and most initial blocks are simulation-only. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="system-signals-and-systems"></a>**System (signals and systems)** — A rule y = T{x} that maps a whole input signal to a whole output signal, such as a circuit, a filter, a channel or an algorithm; its properties (memory, linearity, time invariance, causality, stability, invertibility) decide which analysis tools apply. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md). *See also:* [LTI system](#lti-system).

<a id="system-function"></a>**System function** — The eigenvalue of an LTI system for the exponential input, H(z) = Σ h[k]z^{−k} or H(s) = ∫ h(τ)e^{−sτ} dτ; for a constant-coefficient equation it is a ratio of polynomials whose denominator roots are the poles. *First defined in* [11-04](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-04-lti-systems-and-differential-equations.md).

<a id="system-type"></a>**System type** — The number N of integrators (poles at s = 0) in a loop gain L(s); type 0 leaves a finite error to a step, type 1 to a ramp, type 2 to a parabola. *First defined in* [15-04](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-04-feedback-and-steady-state-error.md). *See also:* [Static error constants](#static-error-constants).

<a id="systematic-offset"></a>**Systematic offset** — An offset that results from the design rather than from random mismatch, such as unequal drain voltages or a second stage whose current does not match its width ratio; it is the same on every chip and is removed by design, not by device area. *First defined in* [12-02](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-02-active-loads-cascodes-multistage.md). *See also:* [Input offset voltage](#input-offset-voltage), [Multistage amplifier](#multistage-amplifier).

<a id="systemverilog"></a>**SystemVerilog** — The IEEE 1800 hardware design and verification language (current edition 1800-2023), a superset of Verilog adding the logic type, always_comb/always_ff, enums, assertions, classes, constrained randomization and coverage. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="systolic-array"></a>**Systolic array** — A grid of simple processing elements that pass operands to their neighbours each cycle, so that every value fetched at the edge is reused by a whole row or column; used for matrix multiplication in accelerators. *First defined in* [14-14](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-14-ai-accelerators.md). *See also:* [Processing element (PE)](#processing-element-pe), [Dataflow (accelerator)](#dataflow-accelerator).

<a id="letter-t"></a>

## T

<a id="t-flip-flop"></a>**T flip-flop** — A toggle flip-flop, Q⁺ = T ⊕ Q, which inverts its output at each clock edge when T = 1 and holds it when T = 0; a JK flip-flop with J = K = T behaves the same way. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md). *See also:* [JK flip-flop](#jk-flip-flop).

<a id="t-model"></a>**T model** — A small-signal transistor model with the emitter (or source) resistance r_e = α/g_m (1/g_m for a MOSFET) in the emitter lead and a controlled source αi_e from collector to the internal base; equivalent to the hybrid-π model and convenient when the emitter has series resistance. *First defined in* [10-04](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-04-small-signal-models.md). *See also:* [Hybrid-π model](#hybrid-model).

<a id="tag-cache"></a>**Tag (cache)** — The high-order address bits stored with each cache line, compared on a lookup to tell which of the memory blocks that map to the set is present. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Cache block](#cache-block).

<a id="tail-current-source"></a>**Tail current source** — The current source feeding a differential pair's shared emitter or source node; its value sets the pair's total current and its output resistance sets the single-ended common-mode rejection. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Differential pair](#differential-pair), [Common-mode gain](#common-mode-gain).

<a id="tapeout"></a>**Tapeout** — The milestone at which a chip's final design database is sent to manufacturing to make masks; after it, design changes require new masks and another fab cycle. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md). *See also:* [Respin](#respin).

<a id="target-impedance"></a>**Target impedance** — The highest impedance a power-delivery network may present to the load, V_DD × allowed ripple / current step; designers keep the network's impedance below it across frequency. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Power delivery network](#power-delivery-network).

<a id="taylor-series"></a>**Taylor series** — f(x) = Σ f^(k)(a)(x − a)^k / k!, the power series matching every derivative of f at a (a Maclaurin series when a = 0). *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md). *See also:* [Lagrange remainder](#lagrange-remainder).

<a id="technology-mapping"></a>**Technology mapping** — The synthesis step that covers an optimized logic network with the cells of a target library (or with FPGA lookup tables), choosing covers that minimize area subject to timing constraints. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md).

<a id="technology-node"></a>**Technology node** — A generation of a fabrication process, historically shrinking features by about 0.7× (halving area) every two to three years; modern node names are labels, not physical lengths. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="telegraphers-equations"></a>**Telegrapher's equations** — The pair ∂v/∂z = −L′∂i/∂t − R′i and ∂i/∂z = −C′∂v/∂t − G′v for voltage and current on a transmission line, from the distributed model; for a TEM line they are Faraday's and Ampère–Maxwell's laws integrated across the cross-section. *First defined in* [13-07](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-07-transmission-lines-time-domain.md). *See also:* [Characteristic impedance](#characteristic-impedance), [Transmission line](#transmission-line).

<a id="telescopic-cascode-amplifier"></a>**Telescopic cascode amplifier** — A differential pair with cascode transistors stacked on its drains and cascode current-source loads, giving gain near (g_mr_o)²/2 in one stage at the cost of output swing, about V_DD minus five overdrives per side. *First defined in* [12-02](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-02-active-loads-cascodes-multistage.md). *See also:* [Cascode](#cascode), [Multistage amplifier](#multistage-amplifier).

<a id="tellegens-theorem"></a>**Tellegen's theorem** — In any lumped circuit the branch voltage–current products, with the passive sign convention, sum to zero; it follows from KCL and KVL alone, so it holds for nonlinear circuits and even across two circuits sharing a graph. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md).

<a id="temperature-coefficient-of-resistance"></a>**Temperature coefficient of resistance** — The fractional change of resistance per degree, α in ρ = ρ₀[1 + α(T − T₀)]; 0.00393 /°C for annealed copper at 20 °C, negative for semiconductors and thermistors. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="tensor-core"></a>**Tensor core** — A GPU execution unit that performs a small matrix multiply-accumulate per instruction in low-precision formats, giving an order of magnitude more throughput than ordinary arithmetic lanes on matrix math. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [Structured sparsity](#structured-sparsity).

<a id="test-source"></a>**Test source** — A voltage or current source applied at a port, with all independent sources turned off but dependent sources left in place, to find the resistance seen there as v_t/i_t. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Dependent source](#dependent-source).

<a id="testbench"></a>**Testbench** — Simulation-only code that instantiates a design, applies inputs and checks outputs; the executable form of a design's specification. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md). *See also:* [Self-checking testbench](#self-checking-testbench).

<a id="thermal-capacitance"></a>**Thermal capacitance** — The heat a body stores per kelvin of temperature rise, C_th = mc (J/K); the thermal analogue of a capacitor to ground. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md). *See also:* [Thermal resistance](#thermal-resistance).

<a id="thermal-impedance"></a>**Thermal impedance** — Z_th(t), the temperature rise per watt in response to a power step; it rises from near zero for very short pulses to the steady thermal resistance, and datasheets give it as a Foster RC network. *First defined in* [02-09](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-09-systems-of-odes-and-matrix-exponential.md). *See also:* [Foster network](#foster-network), [Cauer network](#cauer-network), [Thermal resistance](#thermal-resistance).

<a id="thermal-noise"></a>**Thermal noise** — Johnson–Nyquist noise of a resistor at temperature T, white and Gaussian with one-sided density 4kTR (V²/Hz); 4.07 nV/√Hz for 1 kΩ at 300 K. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="thermal-resistance"></a>**Thermal resistance** — R_th (K/W), the temperature rise per watt of heat flowing along a path; with heat capacity C_th it forms a thermal time constant R_th C_th, the thermal analog of an RC circuit. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="thermal-runaway"></a>**Thermal runaway** — Positive feedback in which rising temperature raises power dissipation (for example leakage), which raises temperature further; it runs away when the loop gain R_th·dP/dT reaches 1. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Thermal resistance](#thermal-resistance).

<a id="thermal-throttling"></a>**Thermal throttling** — Limiting a chip's power, usually through DVFS, to keep its junction temperature below a limit; the controller (typically a clamped PI) holds the temperature at the limit while the permitted power decays from a burst level to the sustained level with the heat sink's time constant. *First defined in* [15-12](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-12-control-applications-pll-regulators-thermal.md). *See also:* [Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS)](#dynamic-voltage-and-frequency-scaling-dvfs), [Thermal resistance](#thermal-resistance).

<a id="thermal-velocity"></a>**Thermal velocity** — The root-mean-square speed of carriers from thermal energy, √(3kT/m\*), about 2.3×10⁷ cm/s for electrons in silicon at 300 K; drift is a small bias on this random motion. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md).

<a id="thermal-voltage"></a>**Thermal voltage** — V_T = kT/q, the voltage scale of thermal energy per unit charge; about 25.85 mV at 300 K. It sets the ~60 mV/decade slope of diode and subthreshold transistor currents. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="thermionic-emission"></a>**Thermionic emission** — Current carried by carriers energetic enough to pass over a barrier, J = KT²e^(−qφ_B/kT)(e^(qV/kT) − 1) for a Schottky diode; it involves only majority carriers. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md). *See also:* [Richardson constant](#richardson-constant).

<a id="thermomechanical-noise"></a>**Thermomechanical noise** — The random force 4kTb (N²/Hz) that the damping gas exerts on a mechanical structure, the twin of a resistor's 4kTR; it sets an accelerometer's noise floor √(4kTω₀/(mQ)). *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="thevenin-equivalent"></a>**Thevenin equivalent** — A voltage source V_th (the open-circuit voltage) in series with R_th, equivalent at two terminals to any linear network; R_th is found with independent sources switched off and dependent sources kept. *First defined in* [06-08](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-08-thevenin-and-norton.md). *See also:* [Norton equivalent](#norton-equivalent), [Thevenin resistance](#thevenin-resistance), [Open-circuit voltage](#open-circuit-voltage).

<a id="thevenin-resistance"></a>**Thevenin resistance** — R_Th, the resistance seen looking into two terminals of a linear circuit with its independent sources turned off; it sets the time constant seen by a capacitor or inductor connected there. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="thrashing"></a>**Thrashing** — The collapse in performance when a program's working set exceeds the available physical frames, so that nearly every access causes a page fault. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Demand paging](#demand-paging).

<a id="three-cs-compulsory-capacity-conflict"></a>**Three Cs (compulsory, capacity, conflict)** — A classification of cache misses into compulsory (first access to a block), capacity (the working set exceeds the cache, so a fully associative cache of the same size also misses) and conflict (too many blocks map to one set). *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Miss rate](#miss-rate).

<a id="three-phase-system"></a>**Three-phase system** — AC power as three sinusoidal voltages of equal amplitude 120° apart; a balanced three-phase load draws constant instantaneous power, needs 75% of the copper of single phase for the same power and loss, and produces rotating fields for motors. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="threshold-gain"></a>**Threshold gain** — The material gain at which a laser's round-trip gain equals its losses, g_th = α_i + (1/2L) ln(1/R₁R₂); above it the laser oscillates. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="threshold-roll-off"></a>**Threshold roll-off** — The fall of threshold voltage as channel length shrinks, because the source and drain help lower the channel barrier; in Hu's model ΔV_TH = (V_DS + 0.4 V) e^(−L/l_d). *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="threshold-voltage"></a>**Threshold voltage** — The gate voltage at which a MOS surface becomes inverted, conventionally where the surface electron density equals the body doping, V_TH = V_FB + 2φ_B + √(2qN_Aε_s 2φ_B)/C_ox; foundries define it by a drain current. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="throughput"></a>**Throughput** — The amount of work completed per unit time (tasks per second, operations per second), as distinct from latency, the time one task takes. *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md). *See also:* [Latency](#latency).

<a id="time-aliasing"></a>**Time aliasing** — The folding of a sequence onto itself every N samples, x̃[n] = Σ x[n + rN], when its DTFT is sampled at only N frequencies; absent when the sequence is no longer than N. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Aliasing (sampling)](#aliasing-sampling).

<a id="time-constant"></a>**Time constant** — τ, the characteristic time of a first-order exponential response e^{−t/τ}; τ = R_Th·C for an RC circuit and τ = L/R_Th for an RL circuit. After one τ, 63.2 % of the change is complete. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Thevenin resistance](#thevenin-resistance), [Settling time](#settling-time).

<a id="time-scaling"></a>**Time scaling** — Replacing x(t) by x(at); a > 1 compresses the signal and divides its energy by a, 0 < a < 1 stretches it. Combined with a shift, x(at − b) is x(at) delayed by b/a, not by b. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md).

<a id="time-bandwidth-product"></a>**Time-bandwidth product** — The product of a signal's duration and bandwidth, independent of time scaling and fixed by its shape; for RMS widths σ_t σ_ω ≥ 1/2, with equality only for the Gaussian (the uncertainty principle). *First defined in* [11-06](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-06-continuous-time-fourier-transform.md).

<a id="time-dependent-dielectric-breakdown"></a>**Time-dependent dielectric breakdown** — The wear-out of a gate dielectric under prolonged field stress, which makes the breakdown field depend on stress time (about 15 MV/cm for 1 s on 10 nm SiO₂, lower for years); lifetimes are extrapolated from accelerated tests. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="time-domain-reflectometry"></a>**Time-domain reflectometry** — (TDR.) Measuring a line's impedance profile by launching a fast step and recording the reflections at the input; the round-trip time locates each discontinuity, the reflection's height gives its impedance, and a dip's or bump's area gives a shunt capacitance or series inductance. *First defined in* [13-07](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-07-transmission-lines-time-domain.md). *See also:* [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="time-invariant-system"></a>**Time-invariant system** — A system for which delaying the input by any t₀ only delays the output by t₀; tested by comparing "delay, then system" with "system, then delay" for every input. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md). *See also:* [LTI system](#lti-system).

<a id="timing-closure"></a>**Timing closure** — The iterative process of changing RTL, constraints, tool options or placement until every timing path in a design meets its constraints with non-negative slack. *First defined in* [08-12](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-12-fpga-implementation-flow.md). *See also:* [Timing constraint](#timing-constraint), [Slack](#slack).

<a id="timing-constraint"></a>**Timing constraint** — A statement to the implementation tools of a design's timing requirements, such as clock periods, I/O delays, and false or multicycle paths; the tools check only what the constraints describe. *First defined in* [08-12](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-12-fpga-implementation-flow.md). *See also:* [Timing closure](#timing-closure).

<a id="tlb-reach"></a>**TLB reach** — The amount of memory a TLB can map without missing, equal to its number of entries times the page size. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Huge page](#huge-page).

<a id="toeplitz-matrix"></a>**Toeplitz matrix** — A matrix whose entries are constant along every diagonal; writing a convolution as y = Hx gives a Toeplitz H, which lets convolution be computed with matrix-multiplication hardware and libraries. *First defined in* [11-03](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-03-convolution.md).

<a id="tolerance"></a>**Tolerance** — For a component, the maximum allowed deviation of its value from nominal when made, such as ±5% (950 to 1050 Ω for 1 kΩ); temperature drift and ageing come on top. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md). *See also:* [Worst-case analysis](#worst-case-analysis).

<a id="torque"></a>**Torque** — The turning effect of a force, τ = rF⊥ (N·m); for rotation it plays the role of force, and mechanical power is P = τω. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="torque-constant"></a>**Torque constant** — The ratio K_t of a DC motor's torque to its current (N·m/A); by energy conservation it equals the back-EMF constant K_e (V·s/rad) in SI units. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md). *See also:* [Back-EMF](#back-emf).

<a id="total-addressable-market-tam"></a>**Total addressable market (TAM)** — The total revenue opportunity for a product if it won every possible customer; credible only when rebuilt bottom-up from units, attach rates and prices. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="total-differential"></a>**Total differential** — df = (∂f/∂x)dx + (∂f/∂y)dy + …, the linear approximation of a change in f from small changes in all its inputs; the basis of small-signal models and tolerance analysis. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="total-harmonic-distortion-thd"></a>**Total harmonic distortion (THD)** — The RMS of all harmonics above the fundamental divided by the fundamental's amplitude; a ±1 square wave has THD of 48 %. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="total-internal-reflection"></a>**Total internal reflection** — Complete reflection of light going from higher to lower index at angles beyond the critical angle sin θ_c = n₂/n₁; it guides light in optical fibers and silicon waveguides. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="total-probability-theorem"></a>**Total probability theorem** — For events B1, …, Bm that partition the sample space, P(A) = Σ P(Bi) P(A | Bi), a weighted average over the cases. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="total-store-ordering-tso"></a>**Total store ordering (TSO)** — A memory model, like that of x86, in which each core's stores pass through a FIFO store buffer, so a later load may overtake an earlier store to a different address while stores stay in order. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Store buffer](#store-buffer), [Memory consistency model](#memory-consistency-model).

<a id="trace"></a>**Trace** — The sum of a square matrix's diagonal entries, equal to the sum of its eigenvalues. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="traceability"></a>**Traceability** — Two-way links from each requirement to the design elements that implement it and the tests that verify it, exposing untested requirements and orphan code or tests; mandatory in safety standards. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="traceback"></a>**Traceback** — The report Python prints when an exception is not handled, listing the chain of calls that led to the error and ending with the failing line and the exception message; read it from the bottom up. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="transconductance"></a>**Transconductance** — g_m = ∂I_out/∂V_in, the change in a device's output current per unit change of its controlling voltage; for a square-law MOSFET g_m = 2I_D/(V_GS − V_TH). *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="transconductance-amplifier"></a>**Transconductance amplifier** — An amplifier that senses a voltage and delivers a current, characterized by its short-circuit transconductance G_m (S); ideally both R_i and R_o are infinite. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md).

<a id="transconductance-efficiency"></a>**Transconductance efficiency** — The ratio g_m/I_D, the transconductance obtained per unit of bias current; 2/V_ov for a MOSFET in strong inversion, at most 1/(mV_T) in weak inversion, and 1/V_T for a bipolar transistor. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="transfer-function"></a>**Transfer function** — H(s) = Y(s)/X(s), the ratio of output to input transforms of a linear time-invariant system with zero initial conditions; it equals the transform of the impulse response, and H(jω) is the frequency response. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros), [Impulse response](#impulse-response).

<a id="transformer"></a>**Transformer** — Windings sharing a magnetic flux; ideally v₂/v₁ = N₂/N₁, i₂/i₁ = N₁/N₂ and impedances scale by (N₁/N₂)². It needs changing flux and provides galvanic isolation. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="transient"></a>**Transient** — The part of a circuit's response that dies out after a disturbance (such as a switching event), as the circuit moves from one steady state to another. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Time constant](#time-constant).

<a id="transient-analysis"></a>**Transient analysis** — A simulation of a circuit's voltages and currents versus time for arbitrary input waveforms, computed step by step with numerical integration. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="transimpedance-amplifier"></a>**Transimpedance amplifier** — A current-to-voltage converter, v_out = −R_f i_in, formed by feeding a current into an op-amp's virtual ground; it presents zero input resistance, and large R_f makes bias current a significant error. *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [Input bias current](#input-bias-current).

<a id="transition-band"></a>**Transition band** — The frequency range between a filter's passband and stopband; in a windowed FIR design its width shrinks in proportion to 1/N, while the ripple is set by the window's shape. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md).

<a id="translation-lookaside-buffer-tlb"></a>**Translation lookaside buffer (TLB)** — A small cache of recent virtual-to-physical page translations and their permissions, consulted on every memory access; a miss triggers a page-table walk. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [TLB reach](#tlb-reach), [Page table](#page-table).

<a id="translation-unit"></a>**Translation unit** — One C source file after preprocessing (with its included headers pasted in), compiled on its own into an object file. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="transmission-coefficient"></a>**Transmission coefficient** — The ratio τ of the transmitted to the incident electric field at an interface; 1 + Γ = 2η₂/(η₁ + η₂) at normal incidence. The transmitted power fraction is (η₁/η₂)|τ|², not |τ|². *First defined in* [13-06](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-06-reflection-and-transmission.md). *See also:* [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="transmission-gate"></a>**Transmission gate** — An nMOS and a pMOS transistor in parallel, driven by complementary control signals, that pass a signal in either direction without a threshold drop when on; the basic switch of CMOS latches and multiplexers. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md).

<a id="transmission-line"></a>**Transmission line** — A pair of conductors along which signals travel as waves with finite speed, so that voltage and current vary with position and reflections occur at impedance changes. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Characteristic impedance](#characteristic-impedance), [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="transpose"></a>**Transpose** — Aᵀ, the matrix with rows and columns exchanged, (Aᵀ)ᵢⱼ = aⱼᵢ. The transpose of a product reverses the order, (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ; a matrix equal to its transpose is symmetric. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="transresistance-amplifier"></a>**Transresistance amplifier** — An amplifier that senses a current and delivers a voltage, characterized by its open-circuit transresistance R_m (Ω); ideally both R_i and R_o are zero. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Transimpedance amplifier](#transimpedance-amplifier).

<a id="trap"></a>**Trap** — A localized electron state in the band gap, from an impurity or crystal defect, that captures and emits carriers; deep (near mid-gap) traps act as recombination and generation centers. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="trap-processor"></a>**Trap (processor)** — A transfer of control to a more privileged handler caused by an exception, a system call (ecall) or an interrupt; the hardware saves the PC and cause, and an xRET instruction returns. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Precise exception](#precise-exception), [Privilege mode](#privilege-mode), [Page fault](#page-fault).

<a id="trapezoidal-ringing"></a>**Trapezoidal ringing** — A numerical artifact of the trapezoidal rule, whose amplification factor tends to −1 for very fast modes, so stiff components flip sign every step instead of decaying; it is damped by Gear methods or by mixing in backward Euler. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md).

<a id="trapezoidal-rule"></a>**Trapezoidal rule** — Numerical integration joining samples with straight lines; its error falls as the square of the step. SPICE's default transient integration method. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="triangular-distribution"></a>**Triangular distribution** — A probability distribution defined by a minimum, most-likely and maximum value, with mean (a + m + b)/3; a simple model of skewed task-duration risk. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="trigonometric-substitution"></a>**Trigonometric substitution** — Replacing x by a sin θ, a tan θ or a sec θ so that a Pythagorean identity collapses √(a² − x²), a² + x² or √(x² − a²); the reference triangle converts the answer back to x. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="triple-modular-redundancy-tmr"></a>**Triple modular redundancy (TMR)** — Running three copies of a module with a majority voter, giving reliability 3R² − 2R³, better than one module only when R > 0.5. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="triplen-harmonics"></a>**Triplen harmonics** — Harmonics of order 3, 6, 9, …; in a three-phase system they are in phase in all three lines, so they add in the neutral (three times the per-phase value) instead of cancelling. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md). *See also:* [Neutral current](#neutral-current), [Total harmonic distortion (THD)](#total-harmonic-distortion-thd).

<a id="tristate-buffer"></a>**Tristate buffer** — A buffer whose output is either driven to the input value or disconnected (high impedance, Z), so that several drivers can share one wire as long as exactly one is enabled. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="true-dependence"></a>**True dependence** — A read-after-write (RAW) dependence, in which a later instruction needs the value an earlier one produces; it carries data and cannot be removed, only waited for. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [Name dependence](#name-dependence), [Data hazard](#data-hazard).

<a id="true-rms-meter"></a>**True-RMS meter** — A meter that computes the square root of the mean square of the signal, reading correctly for any waveform within its bandwidth and crest-factor limits, unlike average-responding meters calibrated for sines. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md). *See also:* [RMS value](#rms-value), [Form factor](#form-factor).

<a id="truth-table"></a>**Truth table** — A list of a function's output for every combination of its n inputs, 2^n rows; read as a binary number (row i's output as bit i) it is the integer that programs an FPGA lookup table. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="tunneling-breakdown"></a>**Tunneling breakdown** — Reverse breakdown of a junction heavily doped on both sides, in which electrons tunnel from the valence band to the conduction band across a gap of E_g/qE; it occurs at fields near 10⁶ V/cm in silicon, at low voltages, and its voltage falls with temperature. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="turns-ratio"></a>**Turns ratio** — N1:N2, the ratio of primary to secondary turns of a transformer; it sets the voltage ratio (directly), the current ratio (inversely) and the impedance ratio (squared). *First defined in* [07-09](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-09-mutual-inductance-and-transformers.md).

<a id="tustin-transformation"></a>**Tustin transformation** — The control engineer's name for the bilinear transform used to discretize a controller, s ← (2/T)(z − 1)/(z + 1); it keeps stable controllers stable and preserves gain and phase values but warps the frequencies at which they occur. *First defined in* [15-11](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-11-digital-control.md). *See also:* [Bilinear transform](#bilinear-transform), [Frequency prewarping](#frequency-prewarping).

<a id="twiddle-factor"></a>**Twiddle factor** — A root of unity W_N^k = e^{−j2πk/N} by which an FFT butterfly multiplies one of its inputs; W = 1 and W = −j need no multiplier, and the radix-2 FFT has (N/2)log₂N − 3N/2 + 2 non-trivial twiddle products. *First defined in* [16-04](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-04-the-fft.md). *See also:* [Butterfly](#butterfly).

<a id="twos-complement"></a>**Two's complement** — The standard binary representation of signed integers, in which an n-bit pattern with top bit set represents its unsigned value minus 2^n; range −2^(n−1) to 2^(n−1) − 1. Mandatory in C23. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="two-bit-saturating-counter"></a>**Two-bit saturating counter** — A predictor entry with four states, predicting taken in the upper two; it needs two consecutive wrong outcomes to change its prediction, so a loop branch is mispredicted only at the exit. *First defined in* [14-07](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-07-branch-prediction-and-speculation.md).

<a id="two-dimensional-channel-material"></a>**Two-dimensional channel material** — An atomically thin semiconductor, such as a transition-metal dichalcogenide, proposed as a transistor channel for its ultimate thinness; the IRDS judges it not yet mature for manufacturing. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="two-dimensional-electron-gas"></a>**Two-dimensional electron gas** — A sheet of electrons confined in a thin quantum well at a heterojunction (2DEG), free to move along the interface; the channel of a HEMT, with densities of order 10¹³ cm⁻² in AlGaN/GaN. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="two-load-method"></a>**Two-load method** — Finding a source's Thévenin equivalent from its terminal voltage with two known loads, using 1/v = 1/V_th + (R_th/V_th)(1/R_L); a meter's input resistance is part of each load. *First defined in* [06-08](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-08-thevenin-and-norton.md). *See also:* [Thevenin equivalent](#thevenin-equivalent).

<a id="two-port-loading-method"></a>**Two-port loading method** — The classical way to analyse a feedback amplifier by absorbing the feedback network's loading into the amplifier (its input-port resistance with the other port shorted for shunt or opened for series connections) and then applying A/(1 + Aβ); it neglects forward transmission through the network and reverse transmission through the amplifier. *First defined in* [12-05](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-05-feedback-topologies.md). *See also:* [Return ratio](#return-ratio), [Feedback topology](#feedback-topology).

<a id="two-port-network"></a>**Two-port network** — A linear network with two terminal pairs (ports), each carrying equal and opposite currents, described by a 2 × 2 matrix relating its port voltages and currents at each frequency (z, y, h, ABCD or S parameters). *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md).

<a id="two-stage-op-amp"></a>**Two-stage op-amp** — The standard CMOS operational amplifier, a differential pair with a current-mirror load followed by a common-source second stage, Miller-compensated by a capacitor across the second stage; gain g_m1R_1·g_m6R_2 and gain-bandwidth product g_m1/(2πC_c). *First defined in* [12-08](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-08-op-amp-internals.md). *See also:* [Miller compensation](#miller-compensation), [Slew rate](#slew-rate), [Folded cascode](#folded-cascode).

<a id="two-wattmeter-method"></a>**Two-wattmeter method** — Measuring the total power of any three-wire system with two wattmeters whose current coils are in two lines and whose voltage coils return to the third; for a balanced load the readings also give Q = √3 (W2 − W1). *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="type-i-and-type-ii-errors"></a>**Type I and type II errors** — Rejecting a true null hypothesis (false alarm, probability α) and failing to reject a false one (missed detection, probability β). *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="type-iii-compensator"></a>**Type III compensator** — A switching-regulator compensator with an integrator, two zeros and two poles, ω_I(1 + s/ω_z)²/[s(1 + s/ω_p)²]; the zeros near the output LC resonance supply up to 180° of phase lead and the poles above crossover filter switching noise. *First defined in* [15-09](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-09-lead-lag-compensation.md). *See also:* [Lead compensator](#lead-compensator).

<a id="letter-u"></a>

## U

<a id="ultimate-gain"></a>**Ultimate gain** — The proportional gain K_u at which a loop sits on its stability boundary and oscillates steadily, with the ultimate period P_u; found by Routh, by experiment, or by relay feedback, and used by tuning rules. *First defined in* [15-08](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-08-pid-control.md). *See also:* [Ziegler–Nichols tuning](#ziegler-nichols-tuning), [Routh–Hurwitz criterion](#routh-hurwitz-criterion).

<a id="ultra-thin-body-transistor"></a>**Ultra-thin-body transistor** — A MOSFET built in a silicon film only a few nanometers thick on an insulator (UTB SOI); the thin body replaces the depletion and junction depths in the characteristic length, so short channels need no heavy doping. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="uncertainty-principle"></a>**Uncertainty principle** — Heisenberg's limit Δx·Δp ≥ ħ/2 on how sharply position and momentum can both be defined; confinement to a small region forces a momentum spread and hence a minimum kinetic energy. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="uncorrectable-codeword-ratio"></a>**Uncorrectable codeword ratio** — The fraction of codewords with more wrong symbols than the code can correct; for independent errors, the binomial tail P(N > t). *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="undefined-behavior"></a>**Undefined behavior** — In C, an operation (signed overflow, reading an uninitialized variable, out-of-bounds access, oversized shift) on which the standard imposes no requirements; compilers may assume it never happens, so results can be silently wrong. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Sanitizer](#sanitizer).

<a id="underdamped"></a>**Underdamped** — A second-order system with ζ < 1, whose complex characteristic roots −α ± jω_d give a sinusoidal response inside a decaying envelope. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).
