<a id="uniform-plane-wave"></a>**Uniform plane wave** — An electromagnetic wave whose fields are uniform over planes perpendicular to its direction of travel, with E, H and the direction mutually perpendicular and E/H equal to the medium's intrinsic impedance; the far-field model of every radiated wave. *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Intrinsic impedance](#intrinsic-impedance), [Helmholtz equation](#helmholtz-equation).

<a id="unilateral-amplifier"></a>**Unilateral amplifier** — An amplifier with no reverse transmission (y_12 = 0), so its input resistance does not depend on its load; a single stage without a feedback element is approximately unilateral. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Two-port network](#two-port-network).

<a id="union-bound"></a>**Union bound** — The inequality P(A1 ∪ … ∪ An) ≤ P(A1) + … + P(An), valid for any events: the probability that anything goes wrong is at most the sum of the individual probabilities; tight for rare, nearly disjoint events. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md). *See also:* [Inclusion–exclusion principle](#inclusion-exclusion-principle).

<a id="uniqueness-theorem"></a>**Uniqueness theorem** — Poisson's equation with the potential (or the normal field) given on every boundary has only one solution, so any function satisfying the equation and the boundary conditions, however found, is the solution. *First defined in* [13-02](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-02-electrostatics-boundary-value-problems.md). *See also:* [Laplace's equation](#laplaces-equation), [Method of images](#method-of-images).

<a id="unit-circle"></a>**Unit circle** — |z| = 1 in the z-plane, where z = e^{jω} and the system function becomes the frequency response; DC is z = 1, f_s/4 is z = j and half the sample rate is z = −1. A causal system is stable exactly when all its poles lie inside it. *First defined in* [11-09](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-09-z-transform.md).

<a id="unit-impulse"></a>**Unit impulse** — δ(t), the idealized pulse of zero width and unit area (a generalized function); ∫ δ(t) f(t) dt = f(0), its transform is 1, and it models a sudden kick such as a charge dumped onto a capacitor. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Unit step function](#unit-step-function), [Impulse response](#impulse-response).

<a id="unit-in-the-last-place-ulp"></a>**Unit in the last place (ulp)** — The gap between a floating-point number and the next representable number of the same binade; for FP32 values in [1, 2) it is 2⁻²³. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md). *See also:* [Unit roundoff](#unit-roundoff).

<a id="unit-roundoff"></a>**Unit roundoff** — u = ε/2, the largest relative error of rounding one real number to the nearest floating-point number; 2⁻⁵³ ≈ 1.1×10⁻¹⁶ in double precision, so each basic operation satisfies fl(x∘y) = (x∘y)(1 + δ) with |δ| ≤ u. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md). *See also:* [Machine epsilon](#machine-epsilon).

<a id="unit-sample"></a>**Unit sample** — δ[n], equal to 1 at n = 0 and 0 elsewhere; the discrete-time impulse, an ordinary sequence with δ[n] = u[n] − u[n − 1], from which every sequence is built as x[n] = Σ x[k] δ[n − k]. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Unit impulse](#unit-impulse).

<a id="unit-step-function"></a>**Unit step function** — u(t), equal to 0 for t < 0 and 1 for t ≥ 0; it models a switch closing at t = 0 and has a jump discontinuity there. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="unit-test"></a>**Unit test** — A small automated check that runs one function or module on chosen inputs and asserts the result (a hand-worked case, a symmetry, a bound or an expected error); pytest is the standard Python runner. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md). *See also:* [Regression test](#regression-test), [Self-checking testbench](#self-checking-testbench).

<a id="unit-output-method"></a>**Unit-output method** — For a single-source circuit, assume an output of 1 (volt or ampere), work backwards to the source value this requires, then scale by homogeneity; well suited to ladders. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Homogeneity](#homogeneity).

<a id="unity-gain-stable"></a>**Unity-gain stable** — Said of an op-amp whose compensation keeps it stable with 100% feedback (a buffer), the case of largest loop gain; a decompensated op-amp trades this for a higher gain-bandwidth product and a minimum stable closed-loop gain. *First defined in* [12-06](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-06-stability-and-compensation.md). *See also:* [Dominant-pole compensation](#dominant-pole-compensation), [Phase margin](#phase-margin).

<a id="universal-mobility"></a>**Universal mobility** — The observation that silicon MOSFET surface mobilities fall on one curve against the effective vertical field; Hu fits electrons with 540/[1 + (E_eff/0.9 MV/cm)^1.85] cm²/V·s. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="use-after-free"></a>**Use after free** — Accessing heap memory after it has been freed (or moved by realloc), through a dangling pointer; the memory may already belong to something else, so results are silently wrong or exploitable. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="utf-8"></a>**UTF-8** — The variable-length encoding of Unicode code points in 1 to 4 bytes, identical to ASCII for U+0000 to U+007F; continuation bytes start with 10, so a receiver can find character boundaries from any point in a stream. *First defined in* [08-01](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-01-number-systems-and-codes.md).

<a id="utilization"></a>**Utilization** — The fraction of a device's resources (logic cells, block RAMs, DSP blocks, I/O) that a design uses, as reported after synthesis or placement; high utilization makes routing harder. *First defined in* [08-12](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-12-fpga-implementation-flow.md).

<a id="letter-v"></a>

## V

<a id="v-model"></a>**V-model** — A development process in which each level of specification (requirements, architecture, module design) is paired with a matching level of verification (system, integration, unit tests); the backbone of automotive and avionics processes. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="v-number"></a>**V-number** — The normalized frequency of a step-index fibre, V = (2πa/λ)·NA; the fibre is single-mode when V < 2.405, the first zero of the Bessel function J₀. *First defined in* [13-10](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-10-waveguides-and-resonators.md). *See also:* [Numerical aperture](#numerical-aperture), [Mode field diameter](#mode-field-diameter).

<a id="vacuum-level"></a>**Vacuum level** — The energy of an electron at rest just outside a material, the reference from which electron affinity and work function are measured on a band diagram. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md).

<a id="vacuum-permeability"></a>**Vacuum permeability** — The constant µ₀ = 1.25663706127 × 10⁻⁶ N/A² (CODATA 2022), measured since the 2019 SI redefinition and within a part in 10⁹ of 4π × 10⁻⁷. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="vacuum-permittivity"></a>**Vacuum permittivity** — The constant ε₀ = 8.854 × 10⁻¹² F/m that sets the strength of electric forces in vacuum (k_e = 1/(4πε₀) ≈ 8.988 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²); measured, not exact, since the 2019 SI redefinition. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="valid-ready-handshake"></a>**Valid/ready handshake** — The flow-control rule of AXI and similar interfaces: the sender asserts VALID with the data, the receiver asserts READY when it can accept, and a transfer happens on each clock edge where both are high; a sender may not wait for READY before asserting VALID. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [AXI](#axi).

<a id="variance"></a>**Variance** — The expected squared deviation from the mean, Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²] = E[X²] − μ²; for a zero-mean voltage in 1 Ω it is the AC power. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md). *See also:* [Standard deviation](#standard-deviation).

<a id="variation-of-parameters"></a>**Variation of parameters** — A general method for particular solutions of linear ODEs, y_p = u₁y₁ + u₂y₂ with u₁′ = −y₂g/W and u₂′ = y₁g/W (W the Wronskian); it works for any continuous input. *First defined in* [02-04](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-04-forced-response-and-resonance.md). *See also:* [Wronskian](#wronskian).

<a id="vbe-multiplier"></a>**VBE multiplier** — A transistor with a resistor divider across its collector–base and base–emitter junctions that produces V_BE(1 + R1/R2); used to bias class AB output stages, and mounted on their heat sink so the bias falls as they heat. *First defined in* [12-07](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-07-output-stages.md). *See also:* [Class-AB amplifier](#class-ab-amplifier), [Thermal runaway](#thermal-runaway).

<a id="vccs"></a>**VCCS** — Voltage-controlled current source, i = g v_x, with transconductance g in siemens; SPICE element G. The core of a MOSFET's small-signal model. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Dependent source](#dependent-source), [Transconductance](#transconductance).

<a id="vcsel"></a>**VCSEL** — A vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser, whose cavity is formed by distributed Bragg reflector stacks above and below the active layer so that it emits from the wafer surface. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="vcvs"></a>**VCVS** — Voltage-controlled voltage source, v = μ v_x, with dimensionless voltage gain μ; SPICE element E. The first-order model of an op-amp. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Dependent source](#dependent-source).

<a id="vector"></a>**Vector** — An ordered list of n numbers, written as a column; pictured as an arrow in space, a set of related quantities (such as node voltages), or a sampled signal. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md). *See also:* [Linear combination](#linear-combination), [Dot product](#dot-product).

<a id="vector-field"></a>**Vector field** — A rule that assigns a vector to every point in space, such as an electric field E(x, y, z) or a current density J. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="vector-space"></a>**Vector space** — A set closed under addition and scalar multiplication obeying the usual algebra rules, such as Rⁿ, polynomials, or the solutions of a homogeneous linear ODE. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md). *See also:* [Subspace](#subspace), [Basis](#basis).

<a id="vectorization"></a>**Vectorization** — Writing a computation as operations on whole arrays so compiled library code does the looping, typically 10 to 100 times faster than an element-by-element Python loop. *First defined in* [05-02](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-02-numpy-and-vectorization.md).

<a id="vegards-law"></a>**Vegard's law** — The rule that an alloy's lattice constant varies linearly with composition between those of its end members, a(x) = (1 − x)a_A + x a_B; band gaps usually deviate from linearity (bowing). *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md).

<a id="velocity-overshoot"></a>**Velocity overshoot** — Carrier velocities above the saturation velocity in channels so short that carriers cross before they can lose their energy to optical phonons; it relaxes the velocity-saturation limit in very short transistors. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="velocity-saturation"></a>**Velocity saturation** — The levelling-off of carrier drift velocity at high fields (above about 10⁴ V/cm in silicon) near 10⁷ cm/s, because hot carriers lose energy by emitting optical phonons; it limits the current of short transistors. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md). *See also:* [Optical phonon](#optical-phonon), [Ballistic transport](#ballistic-transport).

<a id="velocity-form-pi"></a>**Velocity-form PI** — A discrete PI controller written as an update of its output, u_k = u_{k−1} + b₀e_k + b₁e_{k−1}; clamping u_k at the actuator limit stops integral accumulation without a separate integrator state, and it switches bumplessly from manual to automatic. *First defined in* [15-11](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-11-digital-control.md). *See also:* [Integrator windup](#integrator-windup).

<a id="verilog"></a>**Verilog** — A hardware description language created in 1984 and standardized as IEEE 1364 (1995, 2001, 2005); since 2009 it is formally part of SystemVerilog (IEEE 1800). *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md). *See also:* [SystemVerilog](#systemverilog), [Hardware description language (HDL)](#hardware-description-language-hdl).

<a id="version-control"></a>**Version control** — Recording every saved state of a project's files with author, date and reason, so changes can be compared, attributed and undone; git is the standard tool. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md). *See also:* [Commit](#commit).

<a id="view-numpy"></a>**View (NumPy)** — An array that shares memory with another, as produced by basic slicing, reshaping and transposing; writing through a view changes the original, unlike a copy. *First defined in* [05-02](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-02-numpy-and-vectorization.md).

<a id="virtual-environment"></a>**Virtual environment** — A per-project folder holding a Python interpreter and its own installed packages, so library versions can be pinned per project (created with python -m venv and filled from requirements.txt). *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="virtual-memory"></a>**Virtual memory** — The mechanism, shared by hardware and operating system, that gives each process its own address space by translating virtual addresses to physical ones page by page, providing isolation, protection, relocation and demand paging. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Page table](#page-table), [Translation lookaside buffer (TLB)](#translation-lookaside-buffer-tlb).

<a id="virtual-short"></a>**Virtual short** — The ideal op-amp rule v+ = v− (with no input current), valid only while negative feedback is active and the output is inside its range; with the + input grounded it makes the − input a virtual ground. *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [Operational amplifier](#operational-amplifier), [Negative feedback](#negative-feedback).

<a id="virtually-indexed-physically-tagged-vipt-cache"></a>**Virtually indexed, physically tagged (VIPT) cache** — A cache whose set index comes from untranslated page-offset bits, so it can be read in parallel with the TLB lookup and then compared against the physical tag; it requires size divided by associativity to be at most the page size. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Translation lookaside buffer (TLB)](#translation-lookaside-buffer-tlb), [Set-associative cache](#set-associative-cache).

<a id="volatile"></a>**Volatile** — A C type qualifier telling the compiler that every read and write of an object has effects it cannot see (hardware registers, variables shared with interrupts), so none may be removed, merged or reordered; it does not make operations atomic. *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="volt-second-balance"></a>**Volt-second balance** — In a periodic steady state the average voltage across an inductor is zero (and the average current into a capacitor, charge balance), because its current (voltage) returns to the same value each period; the starting point for analyzing switching converters. *First defined in* [07-01](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-01-capacitors-and-inductors.md). *See also:* [Inductance](#inductance).

<a id="voltage"></a>**Voltage** — The energy per unit charge gained in moving from one point to another (1 V = 1 J/C); it is always defined between two points, written v_AB = v_A − v_B. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md). *See also:* [Reference node (ground)](#reference-node-ground), [Passive sign convention](#passive-sign-convention).

<a id="voltage-amplifier"></a>**Voltage amplifier** — An amplifier that senses an input voltage and delivers an output voltage, modeled by its open-circuit voltage gain A_vo, input resistance R_i and output resistance R_o; ideally R_i → ∞ and R_o → 0. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Unilateral amplifier](#unilateral-amplifier).

<a id="voltage-divider"></a>**Voltage divider** — Series resistors sharing a voltage in proportion to their resistances, v_k = v R_k/ΣR; for two, v_out = v_in R2/(R1 + R2). *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md). *See also:* [Loading effect](#loading-effect).

<a id="voltage-doubler"></a>**Voltage doubler** — A clamp followed by a peak rectifier, giving a DC output near twice the input's peak minus two diode drops; cascading stages multiplies further. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="voltage-regulation"></a>**Voltage regulation** — The fractional change in a transformer's (or supply's) output voltage from no load to full load, about I(R_eq cos θ + X_eq sin θ)/V_rated for a lagging load. *First defined in* [07-09](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-09-mutual-inductance-and-transformers.md).

<a id="voltage-standing-wave-ratio-vswr"></a>**Voltage standing-wave ratio (VSWR)** — (1 + |Γ|)/(1 − |Γ|), the ratio of the largest to the smallest voltage amplitude along a line feeding a mismatched load; for a resistive load it equals the ratio of the larger to the smaller resistance. *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md). *See also:* [Return loss](#return-loss), [Mismatch loss](#mismatch-loss).

<a id="voltage-transfer-characteristic"></a>**Voltage transfer characteristic** — The plot of a logic gate's static output voltage against its input voltage (VTC); its steep middle region and flat rails give noise margins and regeneration. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="voltage-controlled-oscillator"></a>**Voltage-controlled oscillator** — An oscillator whose frequency is tuned by a control voltage, typically through a varactor in an LC tank or the bias of a ring oscillator's stages; the controlled element of a phase-locked loop. *First defined in* [12-09](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-09-oscillators.md). *See also:* [Ring oscillator](#ring-oscillator), [Negative resistance](#negative-resistance).

<a id="letter-w"></a>

## W

<a id="wafer-cycle-time"></a>**Wafer cycle time** — The time a wafer spends in the fab from start to finish, roughly 1–1.5 days per mask layer and 14–20 weeks for advanced processes. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="wall-plug-efficiency"></a>**Wall-plug efficiency** — Optical output power divided by electrical input power for a light source, the product of internal quantum efficiency, extraction efficiency and hν/qV. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="warp"></a>**Warp** — A group of 32 threads (on NVIDIA GPUs) that execute in lockstep, sharing one program counter and issuing one instruction for all their lanes at a time. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [SIMT](#simt).

<a id="water-filling"></a>**Water-filling** — The capacity-maximizing allocation of power across channels of different noise, P_i = max(0, μ − N_i), with a common level μ set by the total power. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="watt-hour"></a>**Watt-hour** — A unit of energy equal to one watt for one hour, 3600 J; battery energy in Wh = capacity in Ah × voltage. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="wave-equation"></a>**Wave equation** — ∂²y/∂x² = (1/v²)∂²y/∂t², satisfied by any shape travelling as f(x ∓ vt); v = √(T/µ) on a string, ≈ 343 m/s for sound in air, c/n for light. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="wavefunction"></a>**Wavefunction** — The complex amplitude ψ(x, t) that describes a quantum particle; |ψ|² is the probability density of finding it at x, and the total probability integrates to 1. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="waveguide"></a>**Waveguide** — A structure that guides electromagnetic waves, especially a hollow metal pipe, which supports only TE and TM modes above their cutoff frequencies (no TEM mode, since it has a single conductor); dielectric waveguides such as optical fibre guide by total internal reflection. *First defined in* [13-10](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-10-waveguides-and-resonators.md). *See also:* [Cutoff frequency](#cutoff-frequency), [Optical fiber](#optical-fiber).

<a id="waveguide-mode"></a>**Waveguide mode** — A field pattern that propagates along a guide unchanged except for phase and attenuation; TE (transverse electric) modes have no axial E, TM modes no axial H, labelled by integers (TE₁₀, TM₁₁) counting half-wave variations across the guide. *First defined in* [13-10](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-10-waveguides-and-resonators.md). *See also:* [Waveguide](#waveguide).

<a id="wavelength"></a>**Wavelength** — The distance λ = v/f a wave travels in one period, where v is the propagation speed and f the frequency. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="weak-inversion"></a>**Weak inversion** — MOSFET operation with the gate below or near threshold, where the drain current is exponential in V_GS and g_m/I_D approaches its limit 1/(nV_T); moderate inversion lies between it and strong inversion. *First defined in* [10-04](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-04-small-signal-models.md). *See also:* [Subthreshold conduction](#subthreshold-conduction), [Transconductance efficiency](#transconductance-efficiency).

<a id="weibull-distribution"></a>**Weibull distribution** — A lifetime model with R(t) = exp(−(t/α)^γ); characteristic life α (63.2% failed) and shape γ (< 1 infant mortality, 1 random, > 1 wear-out). *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="weight-stationary"></a>**Weight-stationary** — A dataflow in which each processing element holds a weight while inputs stream past and partial sums move on, so each weight fetched is reused across a whole batch. *First defined in* [14-14](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-14-ai-accelerators.md). *See also:* [Dataflow (accelerator)](#dataflow-accelerator).

<a id="welch-t-test"></a>**Welch t-test** — A two-sample test of means that does not assume equal variances, using SE = √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂) and an approximate degrees-of-freedom formula; for paired data, test the differences instead. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="wheatstone-bridge"></a>**Wheatstone bridge** — Two voltage dividers fed from one source with the output taken between their midpoints; balanced (zero output) when R1R4 = R2R3, and used to measure small resistance changes. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md). *See also:* [Gauge factor](#gauge-factor).

<a id="white-noise"></a>**White noise** — Noise with a flat power spectral density, so that samples at different times are uncorrelated; an idealization valid within the bandwidth of interest. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="wide-bandgap-semiconductor"></a>**Wide-bandgap semiconductor** — A semiconductor with a gap well above silicon's, chiefly SiC (about 3.2–3.26 eV) and GaN (3.4 eV), whose high breakdown field and negligible intrinsic carriers suit high-voltage, high-temperature and fast-switching power devices. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="wide-sense-stationary"></a>**Wide-sense stationary** — A random process with constant mean and an autocorrelation that depends only on the time difference τ. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="width-quantization"></a>**Width quantization** — The restriction of a FinFET's channel width to whole multiples of one fin's width, which forces device sizing ratios to be ratios of integers. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="wien-bridge-oscillator"></a>**Wien-bridge oscillator** — An oscillator in which a series RC and a parallel RC divide an amplifier's output and feed it back; its poles are s² + (3 − K)ω₀s + ω₀² = 0, so it oscillates at ω₀ = 1/RC when the gain K reaches 3. *First defined in* [07-04](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-04-laplace-domain-circuit-analysis.md).

<a id="wiener-khinchin-theorem"></a>**Wiener–Khinchin theorem** — For a wide-sense stationary process, the power spectral density is the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation function. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="wilson-current-mirror"></a>**Wilson current mirror** — A three-transistor bipolar mirror with feedback that reduces the base-current error to 2/(β² + 2β + 2) and raises the output resistance to about βr_o/2. *First defined in* [10-08](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-08-current-sources-and-mirrors.md). *See also:* [Current mirror](#current-mirror).

<a id="window-function"></a>**Window function** — A taper w[n] multiplying a sequence before it is truncated or transformed (rectangular, Hamming, Hann, Kaiser, ...); tapering lowers the sidelobes of the spectrum at the price of a wider main lobe. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Dirichlet kernel](#dirichlet-kernel), [Frequency resolution](#frequency-resolution).

<a id="wordline-and-bitline"></a>**Wordline and bitline** — The row wire (wordline) that connects every cell of a memory row to its column wires, and the column wires (bitlines) that carry each cell's data to the sense amplifiers or bring write data in. *First defined in* [08-11](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-11-memories-and-programmable-logic.md). *See also:* [Memory array](#memory-array).

<a id="work"></a>**Work** — The energy transferred by a force acting along a displacement, W = ∫F·dr (J); only the component of force along the motion does work. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="work-function"></a>**Work function** — The minimum energy φ needed to remove an electron from a material's surface into vacuum, typically 2–6 eV; it sets the photoelectric threshold and the tunneling barrier in field emission and STM. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="worst-case-analysis"></a>**Worst-case analysis** — Evaluating a design at the combination of component tolerances and operating conditions that pushes each output furthest from nominal, to show it works in every case. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="wraparound"></a>**Wraparound** — The behaviour of fixed-width integer arithmetic, which keeps only the low n bits of a result, so that results wrap modulo 2^n (the largest 32-bit value plus 1 becomes the smallest). *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md).

<a id="write-allocate"></a>**Write-allocate** — A policy for store misses that first fetches the block into the cache and then writes it; its opposite, no-write-allocate, sends the store to the next level without fetching. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Write-back](#write-back).

<a id="write-back"></a>**Write-back** — A write policy in which a store updates only the cache and marks the line dirty; the block is written to the next level once, when it is evicted. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Write-through](#write-through), [Write-allocate](#write-allocate).

<a id="write-through"></a>**Write-through** — A write policy in which every store updates both the cache and the next level, usually through a write buffer, so lines are never dirty. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Write-back](#write-back).

<a id="wronskian"></a>**Wronskian** — W = y₁y₂′ − y₁′y₂; two solutions of a second-order linear ODE are independent, and can match any initial conditions, exactly when W ≠ 0. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="wurtzite"></a>**Wurtzite** — A hexagonal crystal structure built from the same tetrahedral bonds as zinc blende but stacked differently, described by two lattice constants a and c; GaN, AlN and ZnO crystallize in it. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md).

<a id="wye-y-connection"></a>**Wye (Y) connection** — Three-phase sources or loads joined at a common star (neutral) point, each element between a line and the neutral; allows a four-wire system serving single-phase loads. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="letter-y"></a>

## Y

<a id="y-parameters"></a>**y-parameters** — Short-circuit admittance parameters, I = y V, the inverse of the z matrix; natural for transistors (y21 ≈ gm) and for parallel connections, where they add. *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md). *See also:* [Two-port network](#two-port-network).

<a id="letter-z"></a>

## Z

<a id="z-parameters"></a>**z-parameters** — Open-circuit impedance parameters, V = z I; z11 and z22 are input and output impedances with the other port open, z12 and z21 transfer impedances. A reciprocal network has z12 = z21 and a T equivalent. *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md). *See also:* [Two-port network](#two-port-network).

<a id="z-plane"></a>**z-plane** — The complex plane of the variable z = re^{jω}: each point is the geometric sequence zⁿ, decaying inside the unit circle, growing outside, with the angle as DT frequency. *First defined in* [11-09](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-09-z-transform.md). *See also:* [Unit circle](#unit-circle), [s-plane](#s-plane).

<a id="z-transform"></a>**z-transform** — X(z) = Σ x[n] z^{−n}, the DT counterpart of the Laplace transform: the DTFT of x[n]r^{−n} for z = re^{jω}; meaningful only with its region of convergence, an annulus centered on the origin. *First defined in* [11-09](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-09-z-transform.md). *See also:* [Region of convergence (ROC)](#region-of-convergence-roc), [Discrete-time Fourier transform (DTFT)](#discrete-time-fourier-transform-dtft).

<a id="zener-diode"></a>**Zener diode** — A diode designed to operate in reverse breakdown at a specified voltage, by tunneling at low voltages and by avalanche at higher ones; the opposite temperature coefficients partly cancel near the crossover. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="zero-drift-amplifier"></a>**Zero-drift amplifier** — An op-amp that continuously measures and cancels its own offset (by autozeroing or chopping), achieving microvolt offset and near-zero drift at the cost of bandwidth, switching artifacts and higher current noise. *First defined in* [10-09](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-09-real-op-amps-nonidealities.md). *See also:* [Offset drift](#offset-drift).

<a id="zero-input-response"></a>**Zero-input response** — The part of a linear circuit's response caused by its initial stored energy alone, with all inputs zero; it contains only the circuit's natural modes. *First defined in* [07-04](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-04-laplace-domain-circuit-analysis.md).

<a id="zero-insertion-interpolation"></a>**Zero-insertion interpolation** — Upsampling by L by placing L − 1 zeros between samples, y[n] = x[n/L] for n a multiple of L and 0 otherwise; it loses nothing and keeps the energy, and a filter later fills in the zeros. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Decimation](#decimation).

<a id="zero-order-hold"></a>**Zero-order hold** — Holding a sampled input constant over each sample period; it gives the exact discretization A_d = e^{AT}, B_d = A⁻¹(e^{AT} − I)B of a state-space model, mapping poles as z = e^{sT}. *First defined in* [02-09](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-09-systems-of-odes-and-matrix-exponential.md).

<a id="zero-padding"></a>**Zero-padding** — Appending zeros to a sequence before a DFT, which samples the same DTFT more finely; it interpolates the spectrum but does not improve frequency resolution, which only a longer record does. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Frequency resolution](#frequency-resolution).

<a id="zero-state-response"></a>**Zero-state response** — The part of a linear circuit's response caused by its inputs alone, with all initial conditions zero; in the s-domain H(s)X(s). *First defined in* [07-04](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-04-laplace-domain-circuit-analysis.md). *See also:* [Zero-input response](#zero-input-response).

<a id="zero-value-time-constants"></a>**Zero-value time constants** — The resistances seen by one capacitor with another shorted, used in pairs to give the second denominator coefficient b_2 = Σ R_i0C_iR_j^iC_j and from it the second pole, about b_1/b_2. *First defined in* [12-04](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-04-high-frequency-analysis-methods.md). *See also:* [Open-circuit time constants](#open-circuit-time-constants).

<a id="ziegler-nichols-tuning"></a>**Ziegler–Nichols tuning** — Classic 1942 PID tuning rules; the ultimate-gain version sets K_p = 0.6 K_u, T_i = P_u/2, T_d = P_u/8 from the gain and period at which proportional control just oscillates. It gives fast disturbance rejection but typically only about 30° of phase margin. *First defined in* [15-08](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-08-pid-control.md). *See also:* [Ultimate gain](#ultimate-gain).

<a id="zinc-blende"></a>**Zinc blende** — The diamond structure with its two basis sites occupied by different elements, as in GaAs and InP, so that each atom of one kind has four neighbors of the other. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Diamond structure](#diamond-structure), [Wurtzite](#wurtzite).

<a id="zoh-equivalent"></a>**ZOH equivalent** — The discrete transfer function G(z) = (1 − z⁻¹) Z{P(s)/s} of a continuous plant driven through a zero-order hold and sampled; it is exact at the sample instants because the held input lets the state be advanced exactly, x_{k+1} = e^{AT}x_k + Γu_k. *First defined in* [15-11](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-11-digital-control.md). *See also:* [Zero-order hold](#zero-order-hold).
